teile.einleitung: Alexander Suvorov was a famous Russian general. In 1799 he marched with his army over the Gotthard and through the Schöllenen Gorge in the canton of Uri. A large monument there recalls this campaign.
wichtigste: Alexander Suvorov was a Russian field marshal.
In 1799 he fought in Switzerland against the French army.
He crossed the Gotthard with his troops.
In the Schöllenen at the Devil's Bridge there was fierce fighting.
After that he went on over several Alpine passes.
A monument cut into the rock in the Schöllenen recalls him.

abschnitte.text: In **1799** Switzerland was a theatre of the wars between **France** and other European powers. **Russia** and **Austria** also fought against the French. General **Alexander Suvorov** was to come into Switzerland from Italy with his army. For the local population this time was very hard, because many troops moved through the country and needed food.

In September 1799 Suvorov crossed the **Gotthard** with his soldiers. In the **Schöllenen Gorge** at the **Devil's Bridge** there was fierce fighting with the French. After that the army moved on through the Muota Valley and over the **Panix Pass** to the Grisons. The marches over the snowy passes were extremely hard for the soldiers. In the end Suvorov left Switzerland with his troops.

In the **Schöllenen** stands a large **monument** to Suvorov and his soldiers. It is a huge cross cut straight into the **rock face**. It was put up at the end of the 19th century. The land belongs to Russia. Many travellers who drive through the Schöllenen stop there.

gewusst: The plot of land with the Suvorov monument in the Schöllenen was given to Russia.

teile.einleitung: Fondue is a well-known Swiss dish made of melted cheese. You dip pieces of bread on a long fork into the hot cheese. The “moitié moitié” fondue from the canton of Fribourg is especially popular.
wichtigste: Fondue is made from melted cheese.
It is eaten together from one pot, the caquelon.
Pieces of bread are dipped into the cheese on a long fork.
“Moitié moitié” means “half and half”.
This fondue is made from Gruyère and Vacherin fribourgeois.
Fondue is regarded as a national dish of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The word **fondue** comes from the French “fondre”, which means “to melt”. For a cheese fondue, cheese is melted together with white wine, garlic and a little starch. Often a splash of kirsch is added. The mixture is stirred until it is nice and creamy. For children, the wine can be replaced with other liquids.

Fondue is served in a special pot, the **caquelon**. It is usually made of ceramic or cast iron. The pot stands on a **rechaud**, a small burner, so that the cheese stays warm and runny. Everyone sits around the table and dips their pieces of bread in on a long **fondue fork**. It is best to stir the pot a little all the time.

In the **canton of Fribourg**, the “**moitié moitié**” fondue is very popular. In French this means “half and half”. For it you use half **Gruyère** and half **Vacherin fribourgeois**. Both kinds of cheese come from the canton of Fribourg. There is also a fondue made only from Vacherin, which is prepared with water instead of wine.

In the past, fondue was mainly eaten in the mountain regions. In the 20th century, the Swiss cheese industry made it known all over the country. Today it is regarded as a **national dish** and is especially enjoyed in winter. In many families there is a funny custom: anyone who loses their bread in the pot has to do a small task.

gewusst: The crispy crust of cheese that is left at the bottom of the caquelon at the end is called “la religieuse”.
In Switzerland there are many regional fondue mixtures, depending on which cheeses there are in the area.

teile.einleitung: Lake Geneva is a large lake in the west of Switzerland. It lies between Switzerland and France. Well-known cities such as Geneva, Lausanne and Montreux lie on its shores.
wichtigste: In French, Lake Geneva is called “Lac Léman”.
It is the largest lake in Switzerland, but Switzerland shares it with France.
The northern shore belongs to Switzerland, and a large part of the southern shore to France.
The city of Geneva lies at the south-western end of the lake.
Lausanne lies on the northern shore.
The Rhône flows through the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Geneva** is called **Lac Léman** in French. It is shaped like a crescent moon. With an area of about 580 square kilometres, it is one of the largest lakes in central Europe. The northern shore belongs to **Switzerland**, and a large part of the southern shore to **France**. The cantons of **Geneva**, **Vaud** and **Valais** border Lake Geneva.

The city of **Geneva** lies at the **south-western end** of the lake. The famous **Jet d'eau**, a huge fountain of water, stands there. **Lausanne** lies on the **northern shore** and climbs steeply up the slope from the lake. Further east come **Vevey** and **Montreux**. At Montreux, **Chillon Castle** stands right on the water.

The **Rhône** comes from the Valais and flows into the lake at Villeneuve. It leaves the lake again in Geneva and flows on to France. At its deepest point, Lake Geneva is over 300 metres deep. Because it holds so much water, it also influences the **climate**: on the shore it is often milder than in the surrounding area.

On the northern shore between Lausanne and Vevey lie the steep vineyards of **Lavaux**. Since 2007 they have been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Old **paddle steamers**, which are already over a hundred years old, sail on the lake. In summer, many people swim, sail or row on Lake Geneva.

gewusst: The biggest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland is not Lake Geneva but Lake Neuchâtel.
The Jet d'eau in Geneva shoots water about 140 metres into the air.

teile.einleitung: The Glacier Express is a famous panoramic train through the Swiss Alps. It runs from Zermatt in the Valais to St Moritz in the canton of Graubünden and is known as the slowest express train in the world.
wichtigste: The Glacier Express runs between Zermatt and St Moritz.
The journey takes about eight hours.
It has been running since 1930.
It crosses many bridges and goes through many tunnels.
The highest point is the Oberalp Pass at 2,033 metres.
It is known as the slowest express train in the world.

abschnitte.text: The **Glacier Express** links two well-known holiday resorts: **Zermatt** in the canton of Valais and **St Moritz** in the canton of Graubünden. On the way it also passes through the canton of Uri. The journey takes about **eight hours**. The train has been running since **1930**. Its name means “glacier express” because in the past you could see the Rhône Glacier on the way.

The Glacier Express is often called the **slowest express train in the world**. It runs on a narrow gauge, the **metre gauge**, through steep terrain. That is why it only makes slow progress. But this is intended: passengers have enough time to enjoy the landscape. The carriages have large **panoramic windows** that reach up into the roof.

On the route, the train crosses almost **300 bridges** and goes through about **90 tunnels**. The highest point is the **Oberalp Pass** at **2,033 metres**. Especially famous is the **Landwasser Viaduct** in Graubünden, a tall stone bridge that leads straight into a tunnel in the rock face. The Albula line with this viaduct is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

The Glacier Express is run by two railway companies: the **Matterhorn Gotthard Railway** and the **Rhaetian Railway**. On the way you see mountains, glaciers, gorges and small mountain villages. In Zermatt the journey begins at the foot of the **Matterhorn**. In St Moritz it ends in the Engadine.

gewusst: The Glacier Express takes about eight hours for the route, which is around 290 kilometres long.
The Landwasser Viaduct is about 65 metres high and leads straight into a tunnel in the rock.

teile.einleitung: Basel Läckerli are small, hard gingerbread biscuits from Basel. They are baked with honey, spices, almonds and candied fruit and are a well known speciality of the canton of Basel City.
wichtigste: Basel Läckerli are a baked speciality from Basel.
They are small, hard gingerbread biscuits.
The ingredients include honey, spices, almonds and candied orange peel.
On top they are covered with a thin sugar glaze.
They can be bought all year round.
The recipe has existed for centuries.

abschnitte.text: A **Läckerli** consists mainly of **honey**, flour and sugar. In addition come **almonds** or hazelnuts, **candied orange peel** and **candied lemon peel**. Candied orange and lemon peel are sugared rinds of oranges and lemons. Spices such as cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg give the typical taste.

The dough is rolled out and baked as a large sheet. After that a thin **sugar glaze** is spread over it. While still warm the sheet is cut into small **rectangles**. Läckerli are rather hard and grow even firmer with time. So they can be kept for a long time.

Läckerli have existed in Basel for **centuries**. In the past spices and sugar were expensive, and only rich people could afford such baked goods. Today Läckerli are sold in pretty tins and sent all over the world as a **gift**. Unlike many gingerbreads they are not eaten only at Christmas.

gewusst: The name Läckerli has to do with “lecker”, meaning something delicious.
Because Läckerli keep so long, they were already well suited to long journeys in the past.

teile.einleitung: The Hammetschwand Lift is a lift on the Bürgenstock in the canton of Nidwalden. It runs up the outside of a steep rock face and is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe. It opened as early as 1905.
wichtigste: The Hammetschwand Lift stands on the Bürgenstock in Nidwalden.
It goes up the outside of a rock face.
It is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe.
It opened in 1905.
At the top you have a wide view over Lake Lucerne.
The spectacular Felsenweg (“rock path”) leads to the lift.

abschnitte.titel: A lift on the rock face
abschnitte.text: Most lifts run inside a building. The **Hammetschwand Lift**, however, runs up the **outside** of a vertical rock face. The cabin glides about 150 metres upwards in a steel frame. Through the windows you look far down to the lake during the ride. At the top you reach the summit of the **Hammetschwand**, the highest point of the Bürgenstock.

The lift opened in **1905**. It belonged to a large hotel area that businessmen had built up on the **Bürgenstock**. It was meant to be a special attraction for guests from all over the world. Later the lift was modernised so that it now runs safely and quickly.

You reach the lift along the **Felsenweg**. This path was cut into the steep rock face and runs high above **Lake Lucerne**. In places it goes through small tunnels. From the top station you can see across the lake, to Lucerne and as far as the Alps.

gewusst: The Bürgenstock lies between the cantons of Nidwalden and Lucerne, right on Lake Lucerne.
A funicular railway also runs up to the Bürgenstock, starting at a boat landing on the lake.

teile.einleitung: The Hauenstein Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel through the Jura. It runs from Tecknau in the canton of Basel-Landschaft to Olten in the canton of Solothurn. Since 1916 it has been an important link between Basel and the Central Plateau.
wichtigste: The Hauenstein Base Tunnel runs from Tecknau (BL) to Olten (SO).
It opened in 1916.
It is about 8 kilometres long.
It passes under the ridges of the Jura.
It replaced the older, higher Hauenstein summit tunnel.
Many trains between Basel and Bern or Zurich go through it.

abschnitte.text: Between **Basel** and the **Central Plateau** lies the **Jura**, a long chain of hills and mountains. For the railway this is an obstacle, because trains cannot climb steep slopes. That is why tunnels were built through the mountain. The **Hauenstein** is a pass in the Jura over which roads have led since ancient times.

As early as the 19th century, the **Hauenstein summit tunnel** was built near Läufelfingen. It lies higher up in the mountain, and the trains had to climb a steep ramp. This was slow and hard work for the locomotives. As traffic grew, a new tunnel at a lower level became necessary.

The **Hauenstein Base Tunnel** opened in **1916**. It lies lower and is therefore flatter than the old tunnel. It begins at **Tecknau** in the canton of Basel-Landschaft and ends at **Olten**. Since then, most express trains and freight trains between Basel and the Central Plateau have used it. This makes Olten one of the most important railway junctions in Switzerland.

gewusst: The name “base tunnel” means that a tunnel lies low down at the foot of a mountain.
Regional trains still use the old summit tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The Helvetic Republic was a state on the territory of present-day Switzerland from 1798 to 1803. It came about after French troops marched in. Its first capital, for a short time, was Aarau in what is now the canton of Aargau.
wichtigste: The Helvetic Republic existed from 1798 to 1803.
It came about after the French invasion.
Its first capital was briefly Aarau, then Lucerne and later Bern.
It was a unitary state with a single government.
The cantons lost a large part of their power.
In 1803 Napoleon ended it with the Act of Mediation.

abschnitte.titel: The end of the old Confederation
abschnitte.text: Before 1798, Switzerland was a loose alliance of states, the **Old Swiss Confederacy**. Many people in subject territories had few rights. After the **French Revolution**, new ideas of freedom and equality spread. In 1798, **French troops** marched into Switzerland, and the old order collapsed.

Following the example of France, the **Helvetic Republic** came into being. It was a **unitary state**: there was a single government, a constitution and a parliament for the whole country. The **cantons** became administrative districts with no power of their own. All citizens were to be equal before the law, and the subject territories were freed.

In **1798**, the town of **Aarau** became the first capital of the Helvetic Republic. The government and parliament met there. But after only a few months, the government moved to **Lucerne** and later to **Bern**. Aarau is therefore proud of having been the first capital of Switzerland for a short time.

Many people, especially in central Switzerland, rejected the new state. They wanted their old rights and the independence of the cantons back. There was fierce **conflict** between supporters and opponents. In 1803, **Napoleon** issued the **Act of Mediation**. With it, the cantons regained more rights, and the Helvetic Republic came to an end.

gewusst: New cantons later grew out of areas of the Helvetic period, such as Aargau, Thurgau, St Gallen, Ticino and Vaud, which became independent in 1803.
In the Helvetic Republic, a single currency for the whole country, the franc, was introduced for the first time.

teile.einleitung: Flüeli-Ranft is a small place in the canton of Obwalden. Niklaus von Flüe, known as Brother Klaus, lived here for many years as a hermit in a gorge. Today the place is a well-known place of pilgrimage.
wichtigste: Flüeli-Ranft belongs to the municipality of Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
Flüeli is a village, and the Ranft is a gorge below it.
Niklaus von Flüe lived as a hermit in the Ranft from 1467.
He is called Brother Klaus.
He is regarded as the patron saint of Switzerland.
He was declared a saint in 1947.

abschnitte.text: **Flüeli** is a small village above Lake Sarnen and belongs to the municipality of **Sachseln**. Below the village lies the **Ranft**, a wooded gorge with the stream Grosse Melchaa. A steep path leads down from the village into the gorge. There you will find a small chapel and the cell of Brother Klaus.

**Niklaus von Flüe** was born in 1417. He was a farmer, had a large family and was also a judge and councillor in Obwalden. In **1467**, with the agreement of his wife Dorothea, he left his family. He withdrew to the Ranft and lived there for about twenty years as a **hermit**. He prayed a lot, and it is said that he ate nothing during this time.

Many people came to Brother Klaus to ask him for advice. In **1481**, the Confederate states were arguing fiercely with each other. Advice from Brother Klaus helped them to agree on the **Covenant of Stans** (“Stanser Verkommnis”). In this way, a war between the Confederates was avoided. That is why he is still seen as a peacemaker today.

Brother Klaus died in 1487. In **1947**, the Catholic Church **declared him a saint**. He is regarded as the **patron saint** of Switzerland. Every year many pilgrims visit Flüeli-Ranft. His grave is in the church of Sachseln.

gewusst: In the village of Flüeli you can still visit the house where Brother Klaus was born and the house where he lived.
Brother Klaus is also valued as a role model by many Protestant Christians.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Charter of 1291 is a treaty between Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. It is regarded as the founding document of the Confederation, and Switzerland recalls it every year on 1 August.
wichtigste: The Federal Charter was written in early August 1291.
The partners were Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden (more precisely Nidwalden).
These three places are called the original cantons.
They promised each other mutual help.
The Federal Charter is written in Latin.
Today it lies in the Museum of the Federal Charters in Schwyz.
That is why 1 August is the Swiss national holiday.

abschnitte.text: The Federal Charter is an **alliance**, that is, a treaty between the valley communities of **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden**. In it they promised to help one another against attacks from outside. They also wanted to settle disputes among themselves peacefully. One important point was that they did not want to accept any **foreign judges**. The judges were to come from their own valleys.

Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the **original cantons**. They lie around **Lake Lucerne**. Unterwalden consisted of two parts, **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**, which are two cantons of their own today. In the Federal Charter it is really Nidwalden that is meant. Because the three places stood right at the beginning, they are also called the **founding cantons**. Later more places joined, until today’s Switzerland came into being.

The Federal Charter is written on **parchment**, which is processed animal skin. The text is in **Latin**, the language of scholars in the Middle Ages. **Seals** hung on the letter, with which the partners confirmed the treaty. Today the Federal Charter is on display in the **Museum of the Federal Charters** in Schwyz. There you can look at it with your own eyes.

The letter gives only “early August” as the date. That is why Switzerland celebrates its **national holiday** on **1 August**. Historians point out that there were several such alliances at that time. Only in the 19th century was the Federal Charter of 1291 especially highlighted as the beginning of the Confederation. Legends such as the **Rütli Oath** and the story of **William Tell** are also connected with it.

gewusst: The Federal Charter names no exact date, only “early August 1291”.
1 August has been an official holiday throughout Switzerland only since 1994.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Rail Tunnel is the first railway tunnel through the Gotthard. It runs from Göschenen in the canton of Uri to Airolo in Ticino and opened in 1882. At that time it was a masterpiece of engineering and made the journey through the Alps much faster.
wichtigste: The Gotthard railway tunnel opened in 1882.
It is about 15 kilometres long.
It connects Göschenen (UR) with Airolo (TI).
It is also called the summit tunnel, because it lies high in the mountain.
Construction took about ten years and was very dangerous.
The engineer Louis Favre led the building work.

abschnitte.titel: A tunnel for the Gotthard Railway
abschnitte.text: In the 19th century, many railways were built in Europe. The **Gotthard Railway** was meant to link the north with Italy. The biggest obstacle was the Gotthard massif. That is why a tunnel about 15 kilometres long was built between **Göschenen** and **Airolo**. It opened in **1882**.

From **1872**, workers dug into the mountain from both sides. They drilled holes in the rock and blasted it with **dynamite**. The work was hard, hot and dusty, and many workers lost their lives in accidents. Most of the workers came from Italy. The engineer **Louis Favre** led the building work, but died in 1879, shortly before the two sides met.

abschnitte.titel: Spiral tunnels and a little church
abschnitte.text: So that the train could climb up to the tunnel, **spiral tunnels** were built. In these tunnels the train goes round in a circle through the mountain and gains height as it does so. Near **Wassen** in the canton of Uri you therefore see the church three times from different angles. The “Chileli vo Wasse” (the little church of Wassen) is very well known for this.

Since the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** has existed, most trains go through the new tunnel down below. Mainly regional trains and day trippers still use the old **mountain line**. Many people use the line because it is very beautiful. The old tunnel is an important piece of Swiss transport history.

gewusst: When it opened, the Gotthard Rail Tunnel was the longest tunnel in the world.
The Zurich politician and businessman Alfred Escher drove the building of the Gotthard Railway forward strongly.

t13w50if.t: Grand Council of the Canton of Thurgau

teile.einleitung: The Grand Council is the parliament of the canton of Thurgau. It makes the laws of the canton and decides on money. What is special is that it meets alternately in two places: in Frauenfeld and in Weinfelden.
wichtigste: The Grand Council is the cantonal parliament of Thurgau.
It has 130 members.
In the summer half of the year it meets in Frauenfeld, in the winter half in Weinfelden.
This arrangement is unusual in Switzerland.
The members are elected by the people every four years.
The government of the canton is called the Regierungsrat (Government Council).

abschnitte.titel: What does a cantonal parliament do?
abschnitte.text: Every canton has a **parliament** of its own. In Thurgau it is called the **Grand Council**. The members discuss and pass **laws** that apply in the whole canton. They also decide on the **budget**, that is, on what the canton spends its money on. They also keep a check on the work of the government.

The Grand Council does not always meet in the same place. In the **summer half of the year** it meets in **Frauenfeld**, the main town of the canton. In the **winter half of the year** it meets in **Weinfelden**. Weinfelden lies roughly in the middle of the canton. This arrangement is old and unique in Switzerland.

The **130 members** of the Grand Council are elected by the people of Thurgau, every **four years**. They belong to different **parties**. Most of them do this work alongside their jobs, which is known as the **militia system**. In this way, farmers, teachers, business owners and many others bring their experience to the work.

Besides the parliament there is the **government**, called the **Regierungsrat** in Thurgau. It has five members and runs the administration of the canton. The parliament makes the laws, and the government carries them out. Important decisions can also be put to the people in a **vote**.

gewusst: Weinfelden is not the main town, but it is home to the cantonal parliament in winter.
In other cantons the parliament is called, for example, the Kantonsrat, Landrat or Grosser Rat.

teile.einleitung: In May 1861 a fire broke out in Glarus. A strong Föhn wind drove the flames through the town, and a large part of Glarus burned down.
wichtigste: The fire of Glarus happened in May 1861.
A strong Föhn wind drove the fire through the town.
A large part of the town was destroyed.
Thousands of people lost their homes.
Help came from all over Switzerland and from abroad.
Glarus was rebuilt with wide, straight streets.

abschnitte.text: In the night of **10 to 11 May 1861** a fire broke out in Glarus. A strong **Föhn** was blowing, a warm, dry wind from the south. The wind carried sparks from roof to roof. Many houses were then built of wood and stood close together. So the fire spread at lightning speed.

The fire destroyed a **large part of the town**, about two thirds. Hundreds of houses burned down, including the church and the town hall. Several thousand people lost their **homes** and their belongings. The fire brigades from the whole of the Glarus region could do little against the flames in the storm.

After the fire a lot of **help** came. People all over Switzerland and abroad gave money, clothes and food. The families without a house first found shelter with others. This great solidarity helped the town to get back on its feet.

Glarus was rebuilt to a new **plan**. Instead of narrow, crooked streets **wide, straight streets** were built that cross at right angles. The houses are now made of stone. In this way a fire should never again be able to spread so fast. That is why Glarus looks different today from many old Swiss towns.

gewusst: The straight streets of Glarus remind some visitors of American cities.
Glarus is the main town of the canton in which the Landsgemeinde takes place every year.

teile.einleitung: The Churfirsten are a striking mountain chain in the canton of St Gallen. They stand between Lake Walen and the Toggenburg and look quite different from the two sides.
wichtigste: The Churfirsten lie in the canton of St Gallen.
The chain has seven peaks.
In the south steep rock faces drop to Lake Walen.
In the north gentle meadow slopes fall to the Toggenburg.
The highest peak is the Hinterrugg at around 2,300 metres.
A cable car runs up the Chäserrugg.

abschnitte.text: The Churfirsten consist of **seven peaks** that stand side by side like teeth. From west to east they are called **Selun**, **Frümsel**, **Brisi**, **Zuestoll**, **Schibenstoll**, **Hinterrugg** and **Chäserrugg**. The **Hinterrugg** is the highest at around 2,300 metres. Together they form a long, jagged line.

From **Lake Walen** you see mighty, almost vertical **rock faces** that drop steeply to the water. From the north side, the **Toggenburg**, the Churfirsten look much friendlier. There gentle **meadows** and alpine pastures stretch right up to the peaks. The mountains are tilted layers of rock that have broken off on one side.

The Churfirsten consist mainly of **limestone**. This rock formed a very long time ago from deposits in the sea. When the Alps came into being, the layers were lifted up and tilted. Rain and ice then shaped the forms further.

From **Unterwasser** in the Toggenburg, cable cars run up to the **Chäserrugg**. At the top stands a summit building designed by the well known Basel architects **Herzog & de Meuron**. In summer many people hike over the alpine pastures, in winter they ski. From the top you see far over eastern Switzerland and down to Lake Walen.

gewusst: From the north side you can hike comfortably up some of the Churfirsten, while on the south side that would only be possible by climbing.
Lake Walen lies at the foot of the rock faces more than 1,800 metres lower than the Hinterrugg.

teile.einleitung: The Alpstein is a small, rocky mountain range in eastern Switzerland. Its highest peak is the Säntis. It lies in the cantons of Appenzell Inner Rhodes, Appenzell Outer Rhodes and St Gallen.
wichtigste: The Alpstein is a limestone range in eastern Switzerland.
The highest peak is the Säntis at 2,502 metres.
The Hoher Kasten and the Ebenalp also belong to it.
In the Alpstein lies the Seealpsee.
The range is a popular hiking area.

abschnitte.text: The **Alpstein** consists mainly of **limestone**. It has steep rock faces, sharp ridges and several chains. The highest peak is the **Säntis** at **2,502 metres**. Other well known mountains are the **Hoher Kasten** and the **Ebenalp**. The range lies in Appenzell Inner Rhodes, Appenzell Outer Rhodes and St Gallen.

The Alpstein is a popular **hiking area**. **Cable cars** go up to several peaks. In the valleys lie mountain lakes such as the **Seealpsee**. Many hikers stop at mountain inns. Well known is the **Gasthaus Äscher**, which clings under a rock face on the Ebenalp. Beside it lie the caves of the **Wildkirchli**.

From the **Säntis** in clear weather you can see far over eastern Switzerland, Lake Constance and into several neighbouring countries. On the summit a **weather station** has stood for a long time. A tall transmission tower has been added. Because of its position on the edge of the Alps there is often a lot of wind and snow on the Säntis.

gewusst: In the caves of the Wildkirchli traces of cave bears and of Stone Age people were found.

teile.einleitung: The Hoher Kasten is a mountain in the Alpstein in Appenzell Innerrhoden. On its summit there is a revolving restaurant that moves slowly in a circle. From there you can see into the Rhine valley, to Lake Constance and to the mountains.
wichtigste: The Hoher Kasten lies in the Alpstein in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
It is just under 1,800 metres high.
A cable car runs from Brülisau to the summit.
At the top there is a revolving restaurant.
You can see into the Rhine valley, to Lake Constance and as far as Austria.
A geology walking trail explains how the mountains were formed.

abschnitte.text: The **Hoher Kasten** is part of the **Alpstein**, the mountain range in the Appenzell region. It lies on the border between the cantons of Appenzell Innerrhoden and St Gallen. From **Brülisau**, a **cable car** goes to the summit in a few minutes. If you like walking, you can also climb up on foot.
On the summit there is a **revolving restaurant**. The floor with the tables turns slowly in a circle. This way, while you eat, you gradually see in all directions without getting up.

To the east, the mountain drops steeply into the **Rhine valley**. The Rhine flows there, and on the other side lies **Austria**. To the north, **Lake Constance** glitters, and to the south you can see the Säntis and many other peaks. In clear weather the view reaches very far.

From the Hoher Kasten, a **geology walking trail** leads along the ridge towards the Saxer Lücke. Signs explain how the Alpstein was formed. The rocks were laid down in the sea long ago and later folded up into mountains. That is why you sometimes find fossils of sea animals in the **limestone**.

gewusst: The rock of the Alpstein was originally laid down on the floor of a sea.
At 2,502 metres, the Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

teile.einleitung: The Älplerchilbi is a traditional festival of the Alpine herders in Central Switzerland, especially in Nidwalden and Obwalden. It is celebrated in autumn, when the cattle are back from the alp.
wichtigste: The Älplerchilbi is celebrated in autumn.
It is especially widespread in Nidwalden and Obwalden.
People give thanks for a good summer on the alp.
The festival includes a church service, a parade and music.
Funny verses about events in the village are well known.

abschnitte.text: In summer many cows live with the **Alpine herders** high up on the **alp**. In autumn animals and people return to the valley. After that the **Älplerchilbi** is celebrated. The word **Chilbi** means a church consecration festival. People thank God for a good summer without misfortune for people and animals.

The festival day usually begins with a **church service**. After that a **parade** moves through the village. The herders wear their traditional costumes, and there is music and flag throwing. Often the **Wildmannli** and the **Wildwybli** walk along too, figures in clothes made of fir twigs or moss. Every village has its own festival day.

A high point are the **verses** (Sprüche). In them funny events from the past year in the village are told, often in rhyme and in dialect. Anyone who had a mishap during the year can count on everyone hearing about it. In the evening there is dancing and celebrating to **Ländler music**.

gewusst: At many Älplerchilbis the Wildmannli make fun of people with their verses.
The word Chilbi for a festival comes from the consecration festival of a church.

teile.einleitung: Heiden is a village in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. It lies high above Lake Constance and offers a wide view as far as Germany and Austria. Heiden is also known as the home of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
wichtigste: Heiden lies in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
From the village you can see across Lake Constance.
Germany and Austria lie on the other shore.
Henry Dunant spent the last years of his life in Heiden.
After a fire in the 19th century, the village was rebuilt in the Biedermeier style.
A rack railway links Heiden with Rorschach on the lake.

abschnitte.text: Heiden lies on a terrace in the **Appenzell Vorderland**, about 800 metres above sea level. **Lake Constance** spreads out below. On the opposite shore lie **Germany** and **Austria**. In clear weather you can see far across the water. This beautiful location made Heiden well known early on.

abschnitte.titel: A village in the Biedermeier style
abschnitte.text: In **1838**, a fire destroyed a large part of the village. After that, Heiden was rebuilt in the style of the time, the **Biedermeier** style. The houses are light, plain and neatly arranged. That is why the village centre still looks very uniform today and is protected.

In the 19th century, Heiden became a popular **health resort**. Visitors from many countries came to recover in the fresh air. They drank, for example, **whey**, the liquid left over when cheese is made, because it was thought to be healthy. Hotels and walking paths were built for the visitors.

**Henry Dunant** of Geneva lived in Heiden from 1887 and died here in 1910. He had co-founded the **Red Cross** and in 1901 received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**. In Heiden, the **Henry Dunant Museum** recalls his life. The village is therefore a special place for people from all over the world.

gewusst: The rack railway from Rorschach to Heiden has been running since 1875.
Three countries meet on Lake Constance: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.

teile.einleitung: The Chriesisturm is a folk festival in the town of Zug. Teams race through the old town with a cherry ladder and baskets, and the custom recalls the start of the cherry harvest.
wichtigste: The Chriesisturm is a folk festival in the town of Zug.
“Chriesi” is the Swiss German word for cherries.
The participants race with ladders and baskets.
The custom recalls the start of the cherry harvest.
Zug has long been known for its cherries.
A well known speciality of Zug is the Zug cherry cake (Zuger Kirschtorte).

abschnitte.text: At the **Chriesisturm** the participants run in groups through the **old town of Zug**. They carry a long, narrow **Chriesileitere**, that is, a cherry ladder, and baskets. Whoever reaches the finish first wins. The race is funny to watch because the long ladders are heavy and awkward. Many spectators cheer the teams on.

In the past people in Zug were not allowed simply to pick cherries whenever they liked. Only when the cherries were ripe was the start of the **harvest** announced, for example with a **bell**. Then people stormed to the trees with their ladders. That is where the name **Chriesisturm** (cherry storm) comes from. Today it has become a cheerful folk festival.

Many **cherry trees** have grown around Zug for a long time. The cherries are eaten fresh or made into **kirsch**, a schnapps. With this kirsch the famous **Zug cherry cake** is soaked. It consists of sponge, butter cream and crisp layers made of nuts and egg white. The Chriesisturm shows how important cherries are for Zug.

gewusst: “Chriesi” means cherries in standard German.
The Zug cherry cake is soaked in kirsch and is one of the best known cakes in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Gornergrat Railway is a rack railway in the canton of Valais. Since 1898 it has run from Zermatt up to the Gornergrat at over 3,000 metres. From the top you can see the Matterhorn and many glaciers.
wichtigste: The Gornergrat Railway runs from Zermatt to the Gornergrat.
It opened in 1898.
It was the first electrically powered rack railway in Switzerland.
The top station lies at over 3,000 metres above sea level.
From the Gornergrat you can see the Matterhorn, Monte Rosa and the Gorner Glacier.

abschnitte.text: Normal trains can only manage gentle slopes, otherwise the wheels slip. A **rack railway** therefore has a **rack rail** between the rails. A cogwheel on the train grips this rail and pulls the train safely uphill. On the way down, too, the cogwheel brakes reliably. This is how the Gornergrat Railway can climb steep slopes.

The Gornergrat Railway opened in **1898**. It ran on **electricity** from the start and was therefore the first electric rack railway in Switzerland. At that time this was modern technology. The line leads from **Zermatt** through forests and over alpine pastures right up into a world of rock and ice.

The **Gornergrat** is a rocky ridge above the **Gorner Glacier**. From there you can see the **Matterhorn** and **Monte Rosa** with the Dufourspitze, the highest peak in Switzerland. All around stand many more four-thousand-metre peaks. At the top there is a hotel with two observatory towers.

The starting point, **Zermatt**, is a **car-free** village. Visitors arrive by train and get around the village on foot or in small electric vehicles. The Gornergrat Railway runs all year round. In winter it also takes skiers up to the ski area.

gewusst: The Gornergrat Railway is regarded as the highest open-air rack railway in Europe.
At 4,634 metres, the Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Estavayer-le-Lac is a pretty little town in the canton of Fribourg. It lies on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel and is known for its well-preserved medieval old town.
wichtigste: Estavayer-le-Lac lies on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel.
The little town belongs to the canton of Fribourg.
French is spoken here.
The old town largely dates from the Middle Ages.
Chenaux Castle is the best-known building.
Since 2017, Estavayer-le-Lac has been part of the larger municipality of Estavayer.

abschnitte.text: Estavayer-le-Lac lies on **Lake Neuchâtel**, the largest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland. The little town is on the southern shore, in the Broye district of the canton of Fribourg. The name gives it away: “le Lac” means “the lake” in French. From the shore you can look across the water to the hills of the Jura.

The old town with its narrow lanes, arcades and old houses is very well preserved. Especially well known is **Chenaux Castle**, a medieval castle with thick walls and towers. Today it houses offices. The big collegiate church of Saint Laurence also shapes the look of the town. Anyone strolling through the lanes feels a little as if they had been taken back to another time.

In Estavayer-le-Lac there is an unusual **Frog Museum**. It shows stuffed frogs that are arranged like people in scenes from everyday life, for example playing cards. The collection was made in the 19th century. The museum also shows objects from the history of the little town.

In summer, many people come to the lake for swimming, sailing and other **water sports**. The shore is flat and in many places lined with reeds. This shore zone is an important habitat for birds. In this way, Estavayer-le-Lac combines history, nature and leisure.

gewusst: In the Frog Museum in Estavayer-le-Lac, stuffed frogs act out scenes from everyday life.
The southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel is one of the largest reed and wetland areas in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Bellinzona is the main town of the canton of Ticino. The city is famous for its three medieval castles, which belong to the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: Bellinzona is the main town of the canton of Ticino.
Many think of Lugano, but the main town is Bellinzona.
In the past the seat of government changed between Bellinzona, Locarno and Lugano.
Since 1878 Bellinzona has been the fixed main town.
The three castles are called Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro.
The castles have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 2000.

abschnitte.text: Above Bellinzona stand three **castles**: **Castelgrande**, **Montebello** and **Sasso Corbaro**. They were built in the Middle Ages, above all by the Dukes of Milan. Walls joined the castles and closed off the whole valley. Since the year **2000** they have belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

abschnitte.titel: At the gate to the Alps
abschnitte.text: Bellinzona lies in the valley of the river **Ticino**. Here the routes over the **Gotthard** and the **San Bernardino** meet. Whoever wanted to travel from the north to Italy in the past almost always passed Bellinzona. So the place was important, and the great castles were built for protection.

In the **19th century** Ticino had no fixed main town. The government moved every few years, alternating between **Bellinzona**, **Locarno** and **Lugano**. That was awkward, because files and officials had to travel with it each time. In **1878** Bellinzona was made the fixed main town.

Today Bellinzona is the seat of the government and parliament of the canton of Ticino. In the old town there are squares with arcades and a popular market on Saturday. At carnival time the city celebrates the **Rabadan**, one of the biggest carnival festivals in southern Switzerland.

gewusst: Lugano is the biggest city in Ticino, but not the main town.
The Castelgrande stands on a rock in the middle of the city and can be reached by a lift.

teile.einleitung: Basel is the main town of the canton of Basel City and one of the biggest cities in Switzerland. The city lies on the Rhine, exactly where Switzerland, Germany and France meet.
wichtigste: Basel is the main town of the canton of Basel City.
Liestal is the main town of the neighbouring canton of Basel Country.
Basel lies on the Rhine, on the border with Germany and France.
The University of Basel was founded in 1460 and is the oldest in Switzerland.
The Basel Fasnacht (carnival) is world famous.
Basel is an important place for chemistry and the pharmaceutical industry.

abschnitte.text: The **Rhine** flows in a great curve through the middle of Basel. It divides the city into **Greater Basel** and **Lesser Basel**. Several bridges link the two sides. In Basel there is a **Rhine port**, from which ships carry goods as far as the North Sea. In summer many people swim in the Rhine.

Basel joined the Confederation in **1501**. In the 19th century there was a quarrel between the city and the countryside. So in **1833** the canton was divided: into **Basel City** and **Basel Country**. The main town of Basel City is Basel, the main town of Basel Country is **Liestal**.

The **Basel Fasnacht** begins on the Monday after Ash Wednesday at four in the morning with the **Morgenstreich**. Then all the lights in the old town go out, and groups with lanterns, drums and piccolos march through the streets. The Fasnacht lasts exactly three days. Since 2017 it has been part of the intangible cultural heritage of UNESCO.

Basel has the **oldest university** in Switzerland, founded in 1460. There are many museums and, with **Art Basel**, a well known art fair. Big firms of the **pharmaceutical industry** have their seat here. The Basel Zoo, affectionately called the “Zolli”, is the oldest zoo in Switzerland.

gewusst: At the Three Countries Corner in Basel the borders of Switzerland, Germany and France meet in the Rhine.
The Basel railway station has a French part, and in Lesser Basel there is a German station.

teile.einleitung: Baar is the second largest municipality in the canton of Zug. It lies directly beside the town of Zug and is known for the Höllgrotten caves and for many firms.
wichtigste: After the town of Zug, Baar is the largest municipality in the canton of Zug.
Baar borders directly on the town of Zug.
The Lorze flows through Baar.
In Baar lie the Höllgrotten, well known stalactite caves.
Many firms have their seat in Baar.

abschnitte.titel: Neighbour of the town of Zug
abschnitte.text: **Baar** lies in a broad plain north of Lake Zug. The municipality has almost grown together with the town of Zug. After Zug, Baar is the **second largest municipality** in the canton. Through the municipality flows the **Lorze**, the most important river in the canton of Zug.

In the Lorzentobel near Baar lie the **Höllgrotten**. These are caves with stalactites and stalagmites that you can visit. They form when water containing lime drips from the ceiling and very slowly deposits lime as it does so. So over a very long time cones grow from above and from below.

Baar has grown strongly in recent decades. Many people live here and work in Zug, Lucerne or Zurich. The canton of Zug has low **taxes**, so many **firms** have settled in Baar. Even so, around Baar there are also farms, woods and hills.

gewusst: The stalactites in the Höllgrotten grow only a few millimetres in many years.
The Lorze, which flows through Baar, comes from Lake Ägeri and flows into Lake Zug.

teile.einleitung: Frauenfeld is the main town of the canton of Thurgau. It is also the largest town in the canton and lies on the Murg in north-eastern Switzerland.
wichtigste: Frauenfeld is the main town of the canton of Thurgau.
It is also the largest town in Thurgau.
Kreuzlingen on Lake Constance follows closely behind.
The town lies on the river Murg.
Its landmark is Frauenfeld Castle.
The big music festival Openair Frauenfeld is also well known.

abschnitte.text: **Frauenfeld** is the **main town** of the canton of **Thurgau**. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament, the Grand Council, meet here. Frauenfeld is also the **largest town** in the canton. **Kreuzlingen** on Lake Constance follows closely behind. Thurgau has no really big cities, but many smaller towns and villages.

In the middle of the old town stands **Frauenfeld Castle** with a mighty medieval tower. Today it houses the **Thurgau Historical Museum**. The old town lies on a rise above the river **Murg**. The town's coat of arms shows a woman and a lion.

Every summer, **Openair Frauenfeld** takes place, one of the biggest hip-hop festivals in Europe. Then tens of thousands of music fans come to the big meadow, the **Grosse Allmend**. **Horse races** are also held there. The Swiss Army also has an important military training area in Frauenfeld.

Around Frauenfeld there are many fields, meadows and **fruit trees**. Because of its many apple trees, Thurgau is sometimes called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”). Frauenfeld is well connected to Zurich and Winterthur by train. Many people therefore live here and work in the larger cities.

gewusst: Because of its many apple trees and its cider, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien”.
Frauenfeld is only a little bigger than Kreuzlingen, the second largest town in Thurgau.

teile.einleitung: CERN is one of the biggest research centres in the world. It lies near Geneva on the border with France, and there scientists investigate what everything in the universe is made of.
wichtigste: CERN lies near Geneva, on the border between Switzerland and France.
It was founded in 1954.
At CERN people study the smallest particles of matter.
The biggest particle accelerator has a ring of around 27 kilometres.
The ring lies deep underground in a tunnel.
At CERN the World Wide Web was invented in 1989.
Many countries work together at CERN.

abschnitte.text: Everything around us is made of tiny **atoms**. Atoms in turn are made of even smaller **particles**. At CERN scientists investigate which particles exist and how they hold together. This field is called **particle physics**. The research helps us to understand how the universe is built.

The most important device at CERN is the **Large Hadron Collider**, or **LHC** for short. It is a **particle accelerator** with a ring around **27 kilometres** long. The ring lies in a **tunnel** about 100 metres underground, partly in Switzerland and partly in France. In it tiny particles are brought almost to the speed of light and smashed together. Huge **detectors** measure what is produced.

At CERN the **World Wide Web** was invented in **1989**. The researcher **Tim Berners Lee** wanted scientists to be able to exchange their results more easily. Out of that came the web pages that we use every day today. The first web page in the world ran on a computer at CERN.

CERN was founded in **1954** so that European countries could do research together after the Second World War. **Switzerland** was involved from the start. Today thousands of researchers from all over the world take part. In **2012** researchers at CERN announced that they had found a long sought particle, the **Higgs particle**. You can visit CERN, as there is a visitor centre there.

gewusst: The ring of the LHC is so long that it runs under the border between Switzerland and France.
The World Wide Web was invented at CERN so that researchers could share their data more easily.

teile.einleitung: The Crème double de la Gruyère is a very thick cream from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg. Together with meringues it is a popular dessert.
wichtigste: Crème double means double cream in English.
It comes from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
Double cream is much thicker and richer than normal cream.
People like to eat it with meringues.
Berries are also often served with double cream.
The Gruyère region is also known for Gruyère cheese.

abschnitte.text: **Crème double** is French and means **double cream**. It is an especially thick cream that contains a great deal of **milk fat**. It is so thick that a spoon almost stands up in it. You do not have to whip it, as it is creamy by itself.

Double cream is best known together with **meringues**. Meringues are light, crisp foam pastries made of **egg white** and **sugar**. You put them on a plate and add generous helpings of double cream. Often **berries** such as strawberries or raspberries are added too.

The **Gruyère region**, in French **la Gruyère**, lies in the south of the canton of **Fribourg**. It is an area with hills, Alps and many cows. The little town of **Gruyères** with its castle is a well known destination for outings. The famous **Gruyère cheese** is also made from the milk of the region.

Double cream is one of the well known specialities of the canton of Fribourg. In many restaurants of the region the dessert with meringues is on the menu. Double cream is also often served at festivals. Because it is so rich, people usually eat only a small portion.

gewusst: Double cream is so thick that you can cut it off with a spoon.
For meringues you need only two ingredients: egg white and sugar.

teile.einleitung: The Einsiedeln World Theatre is a large open-air theatre in Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is performed on the square in front of the monastery, and hundreds of people from the village take part.
wichtigste: The World Theatre is performed in Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is played in the open air on the monastery square.
The first performance took place in 1924.
It is only performed every few years.
Hundreds of amateur actors from Einsiedeln take part.
The idea goes back to a Spanish play from the 17th century.

abschnitte.text: The **Einsiedeln World Theatre** is an **open-air theatre**. That means it is performed outdoors. The stage is the large square in front of the **monastery church** of Einsiedeln. The magnificent façade of the monastery forms the backdrop. Thousands of spectators sit on stands in front of it.

The idea comes from the Spanish poet **Pedro Calderón de la Barca**. In the 17th century he wrote the play **“The Great Theatre of the World”**. In it, people play their roles in life as if on a stage, for example as a king, a farmer or a beggar. At the end, the play asks how each person has played their role.

What is special is that mostly **amateurs** from Einsiedeln take part. Amateurs are people who do not act as their job. Hundreds of children, teenagers and adults help on stage, with sewing the costumes or behind the scenes. For the village, the World Theatre is therefore a big celebration that everyone shares.

The first performance took place in **1924**. Since then, the World Theatre has not been performed every year, but at **longer intervals**. In more recent times, Swiss authors have reworked the play. This way it also fits the questions of our own time.

gewusst: At the Einsiedeln World Theatre, the façade of a real monastery church is the scenery.
The idea for the play is almost 400 years old.

teile.einleitung: In Basel small ferries cross the Rhine with no engine at all. They hang from a cable and are pushed to the other bank by the current of the river alone.
wichtigste: The Basel Rhine ferries have no engine.
They hang from a cable stretched across the Rhine.
The current of the Rhine pushes them to the other bank.
In Basel there are four such ferries.
The ferryman is called “Fährimaa” in Basel German.
The ferries have existed since the 19th century.

abschnitte.text: High above the Rhine a **steel cable** is stretched. The ferry hangs from it with a second rope and can glide along it. The ferryman sets the boat at an angle to the current with the **rudder**. The water presses against the boat and so pushes it to the other bank. This is called a **reaction ferry** (Gierseilfähre).

In Basel there are **four ferries**. Each has a name: **Vogel Gryff**, **Leu**, **Wilde Maa** and **Ueli**. The names come from figures of Basel tradition. The ferries link Greater Basel and Lesser Basel between the bridges.

Because the ferries use only the power of the water, they need **no fuel** and make no noise. The trip lasts only a few minutes. For many people in Basel the ferry ride is a small experience in everyday life. Tourists also like to ride.

The ferryman is called **Fährimaa** in Basel. He makes sure the ferry gets safely across the river. Depending on the water level and current he has to set the rudder differently. In high water the ferries do not run, for safety reasons.

gewusst: The Basel Rhine ferries work on a very old principle that needs no engine at all.
When the ferry goes back, the Fährimaa simply sets the boat at an angle in the other direction.

teile.einleitung: Farmers' painting (Bauernmalerei) from the Appenzell region shows herdsmen, cows and goats on the way to the alp. It is also called Sennenmalerei, and it is a well known folk art of eastern Switzerland.
wichtigste: Appenzell farmers' painting is also called Sennenmalerei.
It shows above all the ascent to the alp with herdsmen and animals.
Typical are cows, goats, herdsmen in costume and mountains.
The pictures often decorate furniture and the bottoms of milking pails.
This painting also exists in the Toggenburg.

abschnitte.text: In the pictures you usually see the **ascent to the alp** (Alpaufzug). That is the day in early summer when the herdsmen move up to the alp with their cows and goats. The herdsmen wear their colourful **costume**, and the cows walk in a long line. In the background stand the mountains and farmhouses. The pictures are colourful and painted very exactly.

In the past mostly everyday things were painted. Popular were the round **bottoms of milking pails**, which were hung on the house. **Furniture**, cupboards and chests were also decorated. Later pictures were also painted on cardboard or canvas. Many painters were farmers or craftsmen themselves and had not learned painting at a school.

**Sennenmalerei** shows how important alpine farming is for the Appenzell region. Old pictures are valuable today and hang in museums. But there are still painters today who carry on this art. Many houses in the Appenzell region are decorated with such pictures.

gewusst: In many pictures the cows are painted so exactly that you could recognise every single one.
Sennenmalerei is often called “naive art” because the painters had not attended an art school.

teile.einleitung: The Centre Dürrenmatt in Neuchâtel is a museum about the Swiss writer Friedrich Dürrenmatt. It stands where Dürrenmatt lived for many years, high above Lake Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: Friedrich Dürrenmatt was a famous Swiss writer.
He lived in Neuchâtel from 1952 until his death.
The Centre Dürrenmatt stands next to his former home.
The museum was opened in the year 2000.
The Ticino architect Mario Botta designed the new building.
Dürrenmatt did not only write, he also painted and drew.
In the museum it is above all his pictures that are on show.

abschnitte.text: **Friedrich Dürrenmatt** was born in **1921** in Konolfingen in the canton of Bern and died in **1990** in Neuchâtel. He is among the best known writers of Switzerland. His **plays** such as **“Der Besuch der alten Dame”** (The Visit) and **“Die Physiker”** (The Physicists) are famous. He also wrote **crime novels**, for example “Der Richter und sein Henker” (The Judge and His Hangman). Many school classes read his works in lessons.

In **1952** Dürrenmatt moved with his family to **Neuchâtel** in French speaking Switzerland. His house lay on a slope high above **Lake Neuchâtel**. From there he had a wide view over the lake as far as the Alps. Here he wrote many of his most important works. He lived in Neuchâtel until his death.

The **Centre Dürrenmatt** was opened **in 2000**. It consists of Dürrenmatt’s former home and a modern new building. This was designed by the Ticino architect **Mario Botta**. A large part of the museum lies in the slope and can hardly be seen from outside. There are exhibitions, readings and events on literature and art.

Many people do not know that Dürrenmatt also **painted** and **drew**. He said himself that painting was very important to him. In the Centre Dürrenmatt it is above all his **pictures** and **drawings** that can be seen. Often they show the same themes as his books. So in the museum you get to know another side of the writer.

gewusst: Friedrich Dürrenmatt wrote in German although he lived in the French speaking city of Neuchâtel.
Besides his books Dürrenmatt created hundreds of pictures and drawings.

teile.einleitung: The A16 motorway is called the Transjurane. It links Biel with the canton of Jura and runs as far as the French border at Boncourt. It has many tunnels and bridges.
wichtigste: The A16 is called the Transjurane.
It runs from Biel through the Jura to Boncourt.
At Boncourt it reaches the border with France.
It runs through the cantons of Bern and Jura.
Since 2017 it has been open to traffic along its whole length.

abschnitte.text: The **A16** is a motorway in the north west of Switzerland. It is called the **Transjurane** because it runs right across the **Jura**. It begins at **Biel** in the canton of Bern. Via Moutier and **Delémont** it leads to **Porrentruy**. At **Boncourt** it ends at the border with **France**.

The Jura consists of many mountain chains and valleys. So the A16 needs numerous **tunnels** and **bridges**. The building was difficult and took several decades. Section by section it was opened. Since **2017** the Transjurane has been open to traffic along its whole length.

abschnitte.titel: Important for the canton of Jura
abschnitte.text: For the young canton of **Jura** the A16 is very important. In the past the region could be reached by car only along winding roads and passes. Today it is linked much more quickly with Biel and the Plateau. Traffic to **France** also became easier.

gewusst: The canton of Jura was founded only in 1979 and is thus the youngest canton of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Bös Fulen is the highest mountain in the canton of Schwyz. It is about 2,802 metres high and lies on the border with the canton of Glarus.
wichtigste: The Bös Fulen is the highest point in the canton of Schwyz.
It is about 2,802 metres high.
It lies on the border between the cantons of Schwyz and Glarus.
The mountain belongs to the Glarus Alps.
Better known Schwyz mountains such as the Rigi and the Mythen are much lower.

abschnitte.text: At about **2,802 metres** the **Bös Fulen** is the highest mountain in the canton of **Schwyz**. It stands in a remote mountain region on the border with the canton of **Glarus** and belongs to the **Glarus Alps**. On the Schwyz side lies the **Muota Valley**. The summit is surrounded by rock and scree, and there is often snow there until well into summer.

When many people think of Schwyz they think of the **Rigi** or of the two **Mythen** near the town of Schwyz. These mountains are well known and easy to reach, but much lower than the Bös Fulen. The Rigi is just under 1,800 metres high, the Grosser Mythen just under 1,900 metres. The Bös Fulen, by contrast, can be climbed only by experienced mountaineers.

The name sounds unusual. Words such as **“bös”** (bad) and **“ful”** (rotten) occur quite often in mountain names in Switzerland and describe difficult or crumbling terrain. The mountain lies in a quiet region without mountain railways. So only a few people get up there.

gewusst: The highest mountain in the canton of Schwyz is almost 1,000 metres higher than the well known Rigi.

teile.einleitung: Cham is a municipality in the canton of Zug on the northern shore of Lake Zug. Here the Lorze flows out of the lake and continues its way towards the Reuss.
wichtigste: Cham lies in the canton of Zug on Lake Zug.
In Cham the Lorze flows out of Lake Zug.
The Lorze then flows on towards the Reuss.
In Cham stands St Andreas Castle on the lakeshore.
In the 19th century a well known milk factory was founded in Cham.
Cham is one of the larger municipalities in the canton of Zug.

abschnitte.titel: Where the Lorze leaves the lake
abschnitte.text: The **Lorze** is the most important river in the canton of **Zug**. It first flows through the Ägerital into **Lake Zug**. At **Cham** it leaves the lake again. This spot is called the **outflow** of the lake. From there the Lorze flows on through the Zug countryside and later joins the **Reuss**.

abschnitte.titel: On the shore of Lake Zug
abschnitte.text: Cham lies at the north western end of **Lake Zug**. On the lakeshore there are parks and bathing places that are popular in summer. A well known building is **St Andreas Castle**, which stands on a small peninsula on the lake. There is also the **Villette Park** with an old villa and beautiful trees. From Cham you see across the lake as far as the Rigi.

In **1866** a company that made **condensed milk** was founded in Cham. That is thickened milk that can be kept for a long time. The company was very successful and sold its milk in many countries. Later it joined with the company **Nestlé**. So one of the biggest food groups in the world also has roots in Cham.

gewusst: The Lorze flows through two lakes: first through Lake Aegeri and then through Lake Zug.
Part of the history of the Nestlé group begins in Cham in the canton of Zug.

teile.einleitung: The Fraumünster is a well-known church in the old town of Zurich. Its coloured glass windows, designed by the artist Marc Chagall, are world famous.
wichtigste: The Fraumünster stands in Zurich on the Limmat.
It was founded as a convent in the year 853.
The abbesses of the convent were very powerful for a long time.
During the Reformation, the last abbess handed the convent over to the city.
Marc Chagall made five glass windows in the choir around 1970.
Today the Fraumünster is a Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The Fraumünster was founded in the year **853**. King **Louis the German** gave the convent to his daughter Hildegard, who became the first **abbess**. An abbess is the head of a convent. That is why the church is called “Frau”münster (“Women's Minster”). It stands on the Limmat, opposite the Grossmünster.

In the Middle Ages, the abbesses of the Fraumünster were very **influential**. For a long time, for example, they were allowed to have **coins** minted. During the **Reformation**, the last abbess, **Katharina von Zimmern**, handed the convent over to the city of Zurich in 1524. In this way she prevented conflict and violence. Since then, the Fraumünster has been a Reformed church.

Around **1970**, the artist **Marc Chagall** designed five large **glass windows** in the choir of the church. They glow in strong colours such as blue, green, red and yellow. The pictures show stories from the Bible. Chagall was already over 80 years old at the time. Many visitors come to Zurich specially to see these windows.

In the Fraumünster there is also a large glass window by the Swiss artist **Augusto Giacometti**. It dates from the 1940s. The church's **organ** is also well known and is played at concerts. With its pointed green tower, the Fraumünster is part of the picture of Zurich's old town.

gewusst: Chagall came from what is now Belarus and was already over 80 when he worked on the Zurich windows.
In the Middle Ages, the abbesses of the Fraumünster were so powerful that they had their own coins minted.

teile.einleitung: Georg Fischer, GF for short, is a large industrial company from Schaffhausen. Today the firm is mainly known for piping systems and operates worldwide.
wichtigste: Georg Fischer was founded in Schaffhausen.
The firm still has its headquarters there today.
Its beginnings go back to the year 1802.
The abbreviation is GF.
Today GF is mainly known for piping systems.
The company operates in many countries around the world.

abschnitte.text: The history of the company begins in **1802** in **Schaffhausen**. At that time, **Johann Conrad Fischer** founded a workshop where metal was worked. Later it grew into a large **foundry**. In a foundry, liquid metal is poured into moulds. The firm was named **Georg Fischer** after a member of the family.

Today GF is mainly known for **piping systems**. These are pipes, connectors and valves through which, for example, **water** or **gas** flows. Many of them are made of **plastic**. They are needed in houses, factories and for the water supply of cities. GF also makes other technical products.

Georg Fischer still has its **headquarters** in **Schaffhausen** today. But the company has factories and branches in many countries. It employs thousands of people around the world. For the town of Schaffhausen, GF is an important **employer**. The firm is listed on the Swiss stock exchange.

gewusst: Georg Fischer is over 200 years old, which makes it one of the oldest industrial firms in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Ajoie is a region in the far north of the canton of Jura. Its main town is Porrentruy (in German Pruntrut). The region is known for its big autumn festival, the Saint-Martin.
wichtigste: The Ajoie lies in the north of the canton of Jura.
The main town is Porrentruy, in German Pruntrut.
The region borders France on several sides.
In November the Saint-Martin is celebrated with a long festive meal.
The people of the Ajoie speak French.

abschnitte.text: The **Ajoie** forms the northernmost part of the canton of **Jura**. It juts into **France** like a tongue and is surrounded by France on several sides. The land is hilly, with fields, meadows and woods. The main town is **Porrentruy** (Pruntrut) with its castle. The Prince Bishops of Basel used to live there.

In **November** the **Saint-Martin** is celebrated in the Ajoie. The festival goes back to the time when, after the harvest, animals were slaughtered on the farms. It includes a very **long festive meal** with many courses, often with meat and sausage. Restaurants all over the region offer the menu. Many guests also come from other cantons.

Typical of the Ajoie is the **Damassine**, a small red plum. A well known spirit is distilled from it. Since 2017 the region has been linked with Biel by the **A16** motorway, the Transjurane. It ends at **Boncourt** on the French border.

gewusst: The Ajoie is surrounded by France on three sides.

teile.einleitung: The Three Lakes Region is the area around Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten. The three lakes are connected to one another by canals.
wichtigste: Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten belong to the Three Lakes Region.
Canals connect the three lakes to one another.
Lake Neuchâtel is the biggest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland.
The region lies in the cantons of Bern, Fribourg, Neuchâtel and Vaud.
The Jura Water Correction changed the landscape greatly.
The Seeland is an important area for vegetables.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Neuchâtel**, **Lake Biel** and **Lake Murten** lie close together. The **Broye Canal** connects Lake Murten with Lake Neuchâtel. The **Zihl Canal** connects Lake Neuchâtel with Lake Biel. So ships can travel from one lake to the other.

In the past there were often **floods** in the area, and much of the land was marsh. So the rivers and lakes were reorganised with the **Jura Water Correction**. The first took place in the 19th century, the second in the 20th century. In the process the **Aare** was diverted into Lake Biel, and the lake levels fell.

Fertile fields came into being on the drained land. The plain east of the lakes is called **Grosses Moos** and belongs to the **Seeland**. Very many vegetables such as lettuce, carrots and onions grow here. That is why the area is often called the **vegetable garden of Switzerland**.

The Three Lakes Region lies on the **language border** between German and French. It is spread over the cantons of **Bern**, **Fribourg**, **Neuchâtel** and **Vaud**. In towns such as **Biel** both languages are heard in everyday life. Murten too is a bilingual place.

On the shores of the lakes people lived in **pile dwelling settlements** thousands of years ago. These are villages whose houses stood on wooden piles. Remains of them have been found in the ground and in the water. Some of these sites are part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

gewusst: Because of the Jura Water Correction remains of ancient pile dwellings appeared on Lake Biel when the water level fell.
The St Peter’s Island in Lake Biel is now joined to the shore by a strip of land.

teile.einleitung: Altdorf is the main town of the canton of Uri. The town lies in the Reuss Valley, near Lake Uri. Altdorf is famous because of the legend of William Tell and its great monument.
wichtigste: Altdorf is the main town of the canton of Uri.
The government and the cantonal parliament meet here.
The town lies in the Reuss Valley near Lake Uri.
On the village square stands the famous Tell monument.
The Tell plays are performed in Altdorf.

abschnitte.text: **Altdorf** is the **main town** of the canton of **Uri**. Here the **government** and the cantonal parliament, the **Landrat**, have their seat. The town lies in the valley of the **Reuss**, only a few kilometres from **Lake Uri**. Through the valley leads the way to the **Gotthard**. So Altdorf was important early on for traffic over the Alps.

Altdorf is closely linked with the legend of **William Tell**. Here Tell is said to have shot the apple from his son's head. On the village square stands, since **1895**, the great **Tell monument**. It shows Tell with his crossbow and his son. The monument is one of the best known in Switzerland.

In Altdorf the **Tell plays** are performed regularly. The play performed is **“William Tell”** by **Friedrich Schiller**. The actors are mostly amateurs from the region. For the theatre there is a building of its own in the town, the **Tellspielhaus**.

gewusst: The Tell monument in Altdorf was made by the sculptor Richard Kissling.

teile.einleitung: In Arlesheim in the canton of Basel Landschaft stands a magnificent cathedral. It was built in the 17th century and later remodelled in the style of the Baroque and Rococo.
wichtigste: The cathedral stands in Arlesheim in the canton of Basel Landschaft.
It was built in the 17th century.
Later it was remodelled in the Baroque style.
It was built for the cathedral chapter of the diocese of Basel.
In the cathedral stands a famous organ by Johann Andreas Silbermann.
Nearby lies the Ermitage, a landscape garden.

abschnitte.text: After the **Reformation** Basel became Protestant. The Catholic **Bishop of Basel** and his clergy left the city. The **cathedral chapter**, a group of clergy who supported the bishop, settled in **Arlesheim** in the 17th century. The cathedral was built for them and was finished in 1681.

In the 18th century the cathedral was **remodelled**. It received magnificent **stucco work**, which are decorations made of plaster, and coloured **ceiling paintings**. This kind of playful decoration is called **Rococo**, a late form of the Baroque. Outside, the two towers and the bright façade on the **Domplatz** stand out.

In the cathedral stands a valuable **organ** by the famous organ builder **Johann Andreas Silbermann**. It was built in the 18th century. Concerts still take place on it today. Musicians from many countries come to play on this instrument.

Not far from the cathedral lies the **Ermitage**. It is a **landscape garden** from the 18th century with ponds, grottoes and walking paths. Above the garden stands **Birseck Castle**. The Ermitage is regarded as one of the biggest landscape gardens of this kind in Switzerland.

gewusst: The cathedral was built because after the Reformation the clergy of the diocese could no longer stay in Basel.
The Ermitage in Arlesheim was laid out in the English garden style, which was popular all over Europe at the time.

teile.einleitung: The Basel Town Hall stands on the Marktplatz in Basel and stands out at once: its façade is bright red. Here the government and parliament of the canton of Basel City still meet today.
wichtigste: The Basel Town Hall stands on the Marktplatz in Basel.
Its façade is bright red.
The walls are decorated with colourful paintings.
It was built at the beginning of the 16th century.
Here the government and the Grand Council of Basel City meet.

abschnitte.text: The **Town Hall** is one of the best known buildings in Basel. Its façade is painted bright red and decorated with **murals**. At the front it has large arches, and above them stand figures and coats of arms. On the roof sits a pointed tower. The building stands in the middle of the lively **Marktplatz**.

Basel joined the Confederation in **1501**. Shortly afterwards, at the beginning of the **16th century**, the city built a new town hall. Later it was extended and repainted several times. The tall tower and a side wing were added only around 1900.

abschnitte.titel: Here is where the governing happens
abschnitte.text: The Town Hall is not a museum but is still used today. The **Government Council**, that is, the government of the canton, has its seat here. The **Grand Council**, the parliament of Basel City, also meets in the Town Hall. In the inner courtyard you can look at the colourful paintings and a statue up close.

gewusst: In the inner courtyard of the Town Hall stands a statue of the Roman Munatius Plancus, who is regarded as the founder of Augusta Raurica.
On the Marktplatz in front of the Town Hall a market takes place almost every day.

teile.einleitung: Between Beckenried in the canton of Nidwalden and Gersau in the canton of Schwyz a car ferry shuttles across Lake Lucerne. It takes cars, bicycles and pedestrians directly to the other shore.
wichtigste: The car ferry links Beckenried in Nidwalden with Gersau in the canton of Schwyz.
It crosses Lake Lucerne straight across.
With the ferry you save a long detour on the road around the lake.
Cars, motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrians fit on the ship.
The ferry runs mainly in the warm season.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Lucerne** has many arms and bays. Anyone who wants to drive from Nidwalden to Schwyz therefore has to go a long way round the lake. The **car ferry** takes the shortcut straight across the water. The trip takes only a short time, and you enjoy the view of the mountains on the way.

A **ferry** is a ship that always travels back and forth between two fixed places. The cars roll over a ramp onto the deck. During the crossing the vehicles stay put, and people can get out and look at the water. On the other shore everyone drives off onto land again.

**Beckenried** lies on the southern shore of the lake in Nidwalden, at the foot of the Klewenalp. **Gersau** lies on the northern shore in the canton of Schwyz, on the slope of the Rigi. For many centuries Gersau was a small republic of its own. Only in 1817 did it finally become part of the canton of Schwyz.

gewusst: Gersau was long regarded as one of the smallest republics in the world.
From the ship you see the Rigi on one side and the mountains of Nidwalden on the other.

teile.einleitung: The Hölloch is a huge cave in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz. With over 200 kilometres of passages, it is one of the longest cave systems in the world.
wichtigste: The Hölloch lies in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz.
The known passages are over 200 kilometres long altogether.
It is one of the longest cave systems in the world.
The cave was formed in limestone, and water shaped the passages.
Researchers are still discovering new parts.
In heavy rain, passages can suddenly be flooded.

abschnitte.text: The Hölloch is not a single chamber, but a huge **cave system** with passages on many levels. The surveyed passages are over 200 kilometres long altogether. This makes the Hölloch one of the longest caves in the world and one of the longest in Europe. There are narrow crawl spaces, steep shafts and big halls. Inside it is dark and cool all year round.

The Hölloch lies in **limestone**. Rainwater contains a little carbonic acid and can slowly dissolve lime. Over a very long time, the water has in this way widened cracks in the rock into passages. Water still flows through the cave today. After heavy rain or during the snowmelt, it sometimes rises quickly and fills whole passages.

In the 19th century, a farmer from the Muota valley began to explore the cave. Later, **cave explorers** studied it more closely and surveyed the passages. In 1952, a group of explorers was caught by floodwater and had to wait for several days in the cave until they could get out again. Today research groups with good equipment are out and about and are still finding new passages.

A small part of the Hölloch can be visited on **guided tours**. For this you need warm clothes, good shoes and a lamp. Longer tours take many hours, some even with a night in the cave. You should never go in alone, because it is easy to get lost and the water can become dangerous.

gewusst: For a long time, the Hölloch was regarded as the longest known cave in the world.
In the depths of the Hölloch there is no time of day: it is always completely dark.

teile.einleitung: The Banntag is an old custom in Basel Country (Baselbiet). In Liestal and other municipalities people walk together along the municipal boundary and check the boundary stones.
wichtigste: The Banntag is a custom in the canton of Basel Country.
People walk together along the boundary of the municipality.
On the way they check the boundary stones.
The Banntag takes place in spring before Ascension Day.
The Banntag in Liestal is especially well known.
