abschnitte.text: By the word **Bann** people used to mean the territory of a municipality. The boundary was marked with **boundary stones**. At that time there were as yet no exact maps. So you had to check regularly whether all the stones were still in the right place and nobody had moved them.

On the **Banntag** men, women and children set off together. They walk in groups over fields, through woods and over hills along the boundary. On the way there are breaks with food and drink. In Liestal people split into several groups, each walking one part of the boundary.

The Banntag takes place in **spring**, in the days before **Ascension Day**. Today it is less about checking the stones, because the boundaries are exactly surveyed. More important is the community: you get to know your own municipality and meet neighbours. In other cantons too there are similar boundary walks.

gewusst: Some boundary stones in Basel Country are several hundred years old.
In Liestal the Banntag is such an important day that many celebrate it like a festival.

teile.einleitung: The Bénichon is a traditional autumn festival in the canton of Fribourg. People give thanks for the harvest and celebrate the cows' return from the alp, and a long festive meal with many courses belongs to it.
wichtigste: The Bénichon is an autumn festival in the canton of Fribourg.
In German it is called Kilbi.
People celebrate the end of the harvest and the return of the cows from the alp.
A big menu with many courses is part of the festival.
Typical are the Cuchaule and the Bénichon mustard.
The festival is celebrated in many villages on different weekends.

abschnitte.text: The **Bénichon** is a festival at the end of summer and in autumn. The farmers have brought in the **harvest**, and the cows have returned from the **alp** to the valley. For this people give thanks and celebrate together. The name comes from the French word for blessing, **“bénédiction”**. In the German speaking part of the canton of Fribourg it is called **Kilbi**.

The most important thing about the Bénichon is the **festive meal**. It consists of many courses and often lasts several hours. To begin there is the **Cuchaule**, a sweet saffron bread, with the **Bénichon mustard**, which is sweet and spicy at once. Then follow, for example, soup, ham, roast lamb and cooked pears. For dessert people often eat **meringues with double cream** from the Gruyère region.

The Bénichon is not celebrated everywhere on the same day. Every village has its own weekend, mostly in **September** or **October**. Besides the food there is music, dancing and games for children. Many families invite relatives and friends to their homes. Restaurants in the canton also offer the traditional Bénichon menu at this time.

gewusst: A complete Bénichon menu can consist of seven or more courses.
The Cuchaule from the canton of Fribourg is coloured yellow by the saffron.

teile.einleitung: The Engelberger Aa is a river in central Switzerland. It comes from the valley of Engelberg, flows through Nidwalden and runs into Lake Lucerne at Buochs.
wichtigste: The Engelberger Aa comes from the valley of Engelberg.
It flows through the canton of Nidwalden.
At Buochs it flows into Lake Lucerne.
The old word “Aa” simply means water or river.
In storms it can carry dangerous floodwater.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountain to the lake
abschnitte.text: The **Engelberger Aa** collects its water in the mountains around **Engelberg** in Obwalden. Then it flows down through the **Engelberg valley** into the canton of **Nidwalden**. It passes places such as **Wolfenschiessen** and **Dallenwil**. At **Buochs** it flows into **Lake Lucerne**.

The word **Aa** is very old and simply means **water** or **river**. There are several rivers with this name in Switzerland. So people add where the river comes from, which gives “Engelberger Aa”. Other streams in the region are also called Aa.

After heavy rain, the Engelberger Aa can carry a great deal of water. In **2005**, a major **flood** caused serious damage in Nidwalden. Afterwards the **embankments** were strengthened and new protective measures were built. This is meant to protect villages and fields better in future.

gewusst: In Switzerland there are several rivers that are simply called “Aa”, because the word used to mean water.

t1lgrtke.t: The asphalt mines of La Presta

teile.einleitung: At La Presta in the Val-de-Travers in the canton of Neuchâtel there are old mines. There asphalt was mined for a long time. Today the mine is a museum that you can visit.
wichtigste: The mines lie near Travers in the Val-de-Travers.
Asphalt rock was mined there.
The asphalt was used, among other things, for roads.
Mining went on until the 1980s.
Today you can visit the tunnels as a show mine.

abschnitte.text: In the rock at **La Presta** there is **asphalt**. That is limestone soaked with **bitumen**, a black, sticky substance. Since the 18th century asphalt was mined here. The workers dug long **tunnels** into the mountain. Mining lasted until the **1980s**.

abschnitte.titel: For roads all over the world
abschnitte.text: The asphalt from the Val-de-Travers was in great demand. It was used for **roads**, pavements and for waterproofing. It was also delivered to big cities abroad. Many people in the valley found work in the mines.

Today the mines are a **show mine**. With helmet and lamp you walk through part of the tunnels. Guides explain how work was done in the past. In the mine's restaurant there is a speciality: a **ham** that is cooked in hot asphalt. It is well wrapped so that it does not turn black.

gewusst: A ham cooked in hot asphalt is a speciality of the mines of La Presta.

teile.einleitung: The EPFL is the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, in the canton of Vaud. It belongs to the Confederation and is the French-speaking sister of ETH Zurich.
wichtigste: EPFL stands for École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne.
In English it is called the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne.
It lies near Lausanne, right on Lake Geneva.
Since 1969 it has been a university of the Confederation.
Together with ETH Zurich it belongs to the ETH Domain.
People from many countries study and do research there.

abschnitte.text: The **EPFL** is one of two **technical universities** that belong to the **Confederation**. The other is **ETH Zurich**. Together with several research institutes, they form the **ETH Domain**. At the EPFL, teaching is mainly in **French** and English.

The school began in the 19th century as a small private **school of engineering** in Lausanne. Later it was part of the **University of Lausanne**. In **1969**, the Confederation took over the school, and it became the EPFL. Since then it has grown a lot.

At the EPFL, people study subjects such as **engineering**, **computer science**, **physics**, **chemistry**, **mathematics** and **architecture**. Many researchers work on new technologies, for example for energy, medicine or robots. New **companies** also come out of the research. The university is known around the world.

The **campus** is in **Ecublens** near Lausanne, very close to **Lake Geneva**. The University of Lausanne is also next to the EPFL. A well-known building is the **Rolex Learning Center**, a library with a wavy floor. Students come here from all over the world.

gewusst: In the Rolex Learning Center at the EPFL, the floor is so wavy that inside you walk up and down little hills.
ETH Zurich and the EPFL are the only two universities that belong directly to the Confederation.

teile.einleitung: The Axenstrasse runs along the eastern shore of Lake Uri, between Flüelen in the canton of Uri and Brunnen in the canton of Schwyz. It is built into steep rock faces and leads through several tunnels and galleries.
wichtigste: The Axenstrasse links Flüelen in Uri with Brunnen in the canton of Schwyz.
It runs along the eastern shore of Lake Uri.
The road was opened in 1865.
It is built into the steep rock and has many tunnels and galleries.
It is an important part of the road to the Gotthard.
Because of rockfall it sometimes has to be closed.

abschnitte.text: On Lake Uri the mountains fall almost vertically into the water. For a long time you could travel here only by ship. With the **Axenstrasse** a road was built straight into the rock face in the 19th century. It was opened in **1865** and was then a great achievement.

The road leads through **tunnels** and **galleries**. A gallery is a tunnel that is open on one side, so that you can look out over the lake. In the past the tunnels were cut into the rock and narrow. Today cars, lorries and Swiss Post buses drive on the Axenstrasse.

The rock faces above the road are steep. In heavy rain **stones and rubble** can fall onto the carriageway. Then the Axenstrasse is closed for safety. That is why for years new, longer tunnels have been planned to protect traffic better.

The Axenstrasse passes places linked with the history of Switzerland. Nearby lies the **Tellsplatte** with the Tell Chapel. There William Tell is said, according to the legend, to have leapt from the boat. Along the shore also runs the hiking trail **Way of Switzerland**.

gewusst: Before the Axenstrasse existed, people travelled mainly by boat across Lake Uri.
From the road you see the Rütli meadow on the other side of the lake.

teile.einleitung: “Crypto Valley” is a nickname for the Zug region. Many firms that work with cryptocurrencies and blockchain have settled there.
wichtigste: The Zug region is called “Crypto Valley”.
Many firms work there on cryptocurrencies and blockchain.
The name recalls Silicon Valley in California.
A blockchain is a kind of digital ledger kept by many computers.
In 2016 the city of Zug became one of the first authorities in the world to accept Bitcoin as a means of payment.
Cryptocurrencies are not official money like the franc.

abschnitte.text: In **Silicon Valley** in California many big computer firms are based. Echoing that, the **Zug** region is called “Crypto Valley”. What is meant is the many firms that deal with **cryptocurrencies** and **blockchain**. Today the name is often used for the whole of Switzerland in this field.

A **blockchain** is a kind of digital **ledger**. In it is stored who has transferred something to whom. This book is not held by a single bank but on many computers at the same time. Because everyone has the same list, it is very hard to change it in secret.

**Cryptocurrencies** are digital money that works with a blockchain. The best known is called **Bitcoin**. Unlike the **franc**, they are not issued by a national bank. Their value can rise sharply but also fall sharply, so they involve risks.

The canton of Zug has long been popular with firms, among other things because of low **taxes** and a good location. In 2014 a foundation that promotes the **Ethereum** project was founded in Zug. Many more firms followed. In 2016 the city of Zug accepted **Bitcoin** for small fees on a trial basis and became known worldwide as a result.

gewusst: From 2016 in Zug you could pay small fees to the city with Bitcoin.
In area the canton of Zug is one of the smallest cantons, but it is home to a great many firms.

teile.einleitung: FIFA is the world football association. It organises the football World Cups and has its headquarters in Zurich.
wichtigste: FIFA is short for “Fédération Internationale de Football Association”.
FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904.
Since 1932 it has been based in Zurich.
It organises the men's and women's football World Cup.
Over 200 national football associations are members.
There is a FIFA museum in Zurich.

abschnitte.text: **FIFA** is the umbrella organisation of all the national football associations in the world. The name is French and means “International Federation of Association Football”. Together with other bodies, FIFA sets the rules of the game. It also organises big international tournaments. The Swiss Football Association is also a member.

FIFA's best-known tournament is the **football World Cup**. The first one took place in Uruguay in 1930. Since then it has usually been held every four years. Since 1991 there has also been a women's World Cup. The matches are watched on television by a great many people all over the world.

FIFA was founded in **Paris in 1904**. Since **1932**, its headquarters have been in **Zurich**. Today the building stands on the Zürichberg. Switzerland is a popular home for many international sports associations, because the country is neutral and offers good conditions. For example, the International Olympic Committee is also based in Lausanne.

In 2016, a **FIFA museum** opened in Zurich. There you can discover the history of football. You can see, for example, shirts, balls and trophies. There are also games you can join in. The museum is a popular day out for football fans.

gewusst: FIFA has more member associations than the UN has member states.
FIFA has been at home in Zurich for over 90 years.

teile.einleitung: The Basel Minster is one of the landmarks of Basel. It is built mainly of red sandstone and stands high above the Rhine.
wichtigste: The Basel Minster is built mainly of red sandstone.
That is why it glows reddish.
It stands on a hill high above the Rhine.
The Minster has two towers, the St George's Tower and the St Martin's Tower.
The roof is covered with coloured tiles.
Since the Reformation it has been a Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The **Minster** is the best known church in Basel. It is built mainly of **red sandstone**. Sandstone is a rock that consists of pressed together grains of sand. It can be worked well but is worn away over time by wind and rain. So the Minster has to be renovated again and again.

The Minster was built over many **centuries**. So you see parts in the **Romanesque** and in the **Gothic** style. In the great **Basel earthquake** of 1356 the Minster was badly damaged. After that it was rebuilt. The two towers are called the **St George's Tower** and the **St Martin's Tower**.

The roof of the Minster is covered with **coloured tiles** that form a pattern. On the façade you see figures, for example St George with the dragon. In the past the Minster was the church of a **bishop**. Since the **Reformation** in 1529 it has been a Reformed church.

Behind the Minster lies the **Pfalz**, a terrace high above the Rhine. From there you have a wide view over the river as far as Germany. In the Minster also lies the grave of the famous scholar **Erasmus of Rotterdam**.

gewusst: You can climb the towers of the Minster and look out over the whole city.
Below the Pfalz the Minster ferry crosses the Rhine on a cable.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Road Tunnel connects Göschenen in the canton of Uri with Airolo in Ticino. It is about 17 kilometres long and opened in 1980. It is one of the most important road links through the Alps.
wichtigste: The Gotthard Road Tunnel opened in 1980.
It is about 17 kilometres long.
It runs from Göschenen (UR) to Airolo (TI).
It is part of the A2 motorway from Basel to Chiasso.
So far it has only had one tube, with traffic in both directions.
A second tube is being built.

abschnitte.text: Before the tunnel existed, cars had to drive over the **Gotthard Pass**. The pass is high and often closed in winter. With the **road tunnel**, you can drive through under the mountain all year round since **1980**. The tunnel is about 17 kilometres long and belongs to the **A2 motorway**.

The tunnel has only one **tube**. Cars drive in both directions in it, separated only by a centre line. That is why strict rules apply: you have to keep your distance and must not overtake. Lorries are metered, which means they may only enter at certain intervals. On days when many people travel, long **traffic jams** often form in front of the portals.

In **2001**, two lorries collided in the tunnel, and a serious fire broke out in which people died. Safety was improved afterwards. There is a **safety tunnel** next to the main tunnel, shelters and emergency call niches. Since then, lorries have been checked more carefully and metered.

The tunnel has to be thoroughly renovated. So that it does not have to be closed for years while this is done, voters agreed in **2016** to the building of a **second tube**. When it is finished, the old tube will be renewed first. After that, only one direction of travel is to run in each tube, but still only on one lane.

gewusst: Today there are three big tunnels under the Gotthard: the old railway tunnel, the road tunnel and the base tunnel.
When it opened in 1980, the Gotthard Road Tunnel was the longest road tunnel in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Areuse is a river in the canton of Neuchâtel. It flows through the Val-de-Travers and has dug a wild gorge. At the end it flows into Lake Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: The Areuse flows in the canton of Neuchâtel.
It crosses the Val-de-Travers.
It flows into Lake Neuchâtel at Boudry.
The Gorges de l'Areuse are a well known gorge.
A popular hiking trail leads through the gorge.

abschnitte.text: The **Areuse** rises in the western **Val-de-Travers**, a valley in the **Jura**. It flows eastwards through the whole valley. After that it forces a way through the mountains to **Lake Neuchâtel**. It flows into the lake near **Boudry**. On the way it takes up water from many springs.

Between **Noiraigue** and **Boudry** the Areuse has dug a deep **gorge** into the limestone. It is called the **Gorges de l'Areuse**. A popular **hiking trail** leads along the water over bridges, walkways and steps. There you see waterfalls, rock walls and dense forest. In high water the trail can be closed.

Near the gorge lie springs that supply Neuchâtel and other municipalities with **drinking water**. Very close by also lies the **Creux du Van**, a huge rock amphitheatre. It is another popular destination in the region.

gewusst: Through the valley of the Areuse there also runs a railway that leads from Neuchâtel into the Val-de-Travers.

teile.einleitung: The Brünig Schwinget is a big Swiss wrestling festival held every summer on the Brünig Pass. Here wrestlers from Central Switzerland compete against wrestlers from the Bernese Oberland.
wichtigste: The Brünig Schwinget takes place every summer on the Brünig Pass.
The Brünig lies between the cantons of Obwalden and Bern.
Wrestlers from Central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland compete against each other.
The Brünig Schwinget is a so called mountain wreath festival (Bergkranzfest).
The festival attracts many spectators every year.

abschnitte.text: **Schwingen** is a traditional Swiss form of wrestling. Two wrestlers wear short cloth trousers over their clothes, the **Schwingerhosen**. They hold on to each other by them. The aim is to put the opponent on his back in the **sawdust**. The wrestling takes place in a round ring covered with sawdust.

The Brünig Schwinget takes place right on the summit of the **Brünig**, on the border between **Obwalden** and the **canton of Bern**. Here the best wrestlers from **Central Switzerland** meet those from the **Bernese Oberland**. Because the two regions fight for victory, the atmosphere is especially exciting. Yodelling, alphorn music and flag throwing are also part of the festival.

The Brünig Schwinget is one of the **mountain wreath festivals** (Bergkranzfeste). These are especially important wrestling festivals held in the mountains, for example also on the Rigi or on the Schwägalp. The best wrestlers receive a **wreath** of oak or fir leaves. A mountain wreath is a great honour for a wrestler.

gewusst: In Schwingen the winner shakes hands with the loser at the end and brushes the sawdust off his back.
Schwingen is regarded as the Swiss national sport and has a very long tradition.

teile.einleitung: The Gross-Titlis ski jump is a large ski jump in Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. Every year in December, a Ski Jumping World Cup event takes place there. The best ski jumpers in the world travel there for it.
wichtigste: The Gross-Titlis ski jump stands in Engelberg (OW).
It is a large hill for ski jumping.
A World Cup event takes place there every December.
Thousands of fans watch the jumpers.
The ski jump is named after the mountain Titlis.

abschnitte.text: In **ski jumping**, you first ride down a steep track, the **in-run**, and become very fast. At the end of the track you jump off and fly through the air. The jumpers hold their skis in a V shape so that they stay in the air longer. Points are given for **distance** and for a beautiful, safe jump with a good landing.

In the **World Cup**, the best athletes compete against each other over a whole winter. Engelberg has been a regular stop for many years. The jumps always take place shortly before Christmas. Many **fans** stand at the side of the ski jump, wave flags and cheer on the jumpers. For the Swiss ski jumpers, it is a home event.

abschnitte.titel: At the foot of the Titlis
abschnitte.text: Engelberg lies in a high valley in **Obwalden**, surrounded by high mountains. The best known is the **Titlis**, up which a cable car with a rotating cabin runs. Engelberg is also known for its **monastery**, which was founded as early as the Middle Ages. In winter, many visitors come to ski.

gewusst: On a large hill, the best jumpers fly further than the length of a football pitch.
The Gross-Titlis ski jump is regarded as one of the biggest natural ski jumps in the world, because it is built into a natural slope.

teile.einleitung: The Locarno Film Festival is one of the best-known film festivals in the world. It takes place every year in August in Locarno in the canton of Ticino. The main prize is the Golden Leopard.
wichtigste: The Locarno Film Festival takes place every year in August.
It was held for the first time in 1946.
The main prize is called the Golden Leopard, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”.
In the evenings, films are shown in the open air on the Piazza Grande.
The screen on the Piazza is one of the biggest in Europe.
Locarno lies in the canton of Ticino on Lake Maggiore.

abschnitte.text: The Locarno Film Festival has existed since **1946**. This makes it one of the oldest film festivals in the world. Every year in **August**, filmmakers, experts and many visitors come to Locarno. For about eleven days, hundreds of films from all over the world are shown. Many of them are shown in public for the first time.

What is special is the **Piazza Grande**, the big square in the old town. A huge screen is set up there every evening. Thousands of people sit on chairs in the open air and watch films together. This **open-air cinema** is one of the biggest in Europe. When it rains, many people simply take out their umbrellas.

The symbol of the festival is the **leopard**. All over the city you then see yellow and black leopard patterns. The best film in the competition wins the **Golden Leopard**, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”. There are also other prizes, for example for the best director or for young filmmakers.

Locarno lies in the **canton of Ticino** on the northern shore of **Lake Maggiore**. Italian is spoken here. The warm climate with palm trees and views of the lake makes the town especially popular in summer. The festival brings many visitors to the region every year.

gewusst: About 8,000 people have room on the Piazza Grande for one screening.
During the festival, the whole of Locarno is decorated with yellow and black leopard spots.

teile.einleitung: The Brünig Pass is a pass between the cantons of Obwalden and Bern. It connects Central Switzerland with the Haslital in the Bernese Oberland and, at around 1,000 metres, is a rather low Alpine pass.
wichtigste: The Brünig Pass connects Obwalden with the Bernese Oberland.
The summit lies at around 1,000 metres above sea level.
A road and a railway line lead over the pass.
On the Bernese side lies the Haslital with Meiringen.
On the Obwalden side lies Lungern on Lake Lungern.
A big wrestling festival takes place on the pass every summer.

abschnitte.text: The Brünig Pass lies on the border between the canton of **Obwalden** and the **canton of Bern**. From Lungern in Obwalden the road climbs up to the summit. On the other side it goes down into the **Haslital** to **Meiringen** and to **Lake Brienz**. At a height of around 1,000 metres the Brünig is much lower than passes such as the Gotthard or the Grimsel.

An important **main road** from Lucerne to Interlaken leads over the Brünig. Because the pass is not very high, it is usually open all year round. The **Brünig Railway** also runs over the pass. On the steep stretches it uses a **cog wheel**. So the Brünig is an important link between Central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland.

On the summit the **Brünig Schwinget** takes place every summer. There the best wrestlers from Central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland compete. The festival draws many spectators. For the wrestling there is a permanent site with stands on the Brünig.

Many **hiking trails** start from the Brünig. You can hike, for example, to the **Hasliberg** region, which lies above Meiringen. From there you have a beautiful view of the Bernese Alps. In winter there are ski areas in the surroundings.

gewusst: Because the Brünig is only around 1,000 metres high, the pass road can almost always be used, even in winter.
The Brünig is one of the few Swiss passes over whose summit a railway runs directly.

teile.einleitung: The Eiger is a famous mountain in the Bernese Oberland. Together with the Mönch and the Jungfrau it forms a trio of peaks that can be seen from far away.
wichtigste: The Eiger is about 3,970 metres high.
The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side in the Bernese Oberland.
You can see them well from Grindelwald or Interlaken.
The Eiger North Face is one of the best-known rock walls in the Alps.
It was climbed for the first time in 1938.
The Jungfrau Railway runs through a tunnel inside the Eiger and the Mönch.

abschnitte.text: In the **Bernese Oberland**, three well-known mountains stand side by side: the **Eiger**, the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau**. The Eiger is about **3,970 metres** high, while the Mönch and the Jungfrau are both over 4,000 metres high. You can see them especially well from **Grindelwald**, **Interlaken** or **Kleine Scheidegg**. The picture of the three peaks can be seen on many postcards.

The **North Face** of the Eiger is about 1,800 metres high and very steep. It is considered one of the most difficult and best-known walls in the Alps. In **1938**, a rope team of four climbers managed to climb all the way up it for the first time. Because of falling rocks and sudden changes in the weather, the wall is still dangerous today.

The **Jungfrau Railway** runs from Kleine Scheidegg through a long **tunnel** inside the Eiger and the Mönch. Its destination is the **Jungfraujoch**, at over 3,400 metres. The highest railway station in Europe is there. The railway was finished in 1912.

The area around the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** “Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch”. The **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps, is also found there. The World Heritage Site protects this special high mountain landscape. Every year, a great many visitors come from all over the world.

gewusst: An old tale says that the Mönch (“monk”) stands between the Eiger and the Jungfrau (“maiden”) to protect her.
The Jungfraujoch station is at over 3,400 metres and is the highest railway station in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Gottlieber Hüppen are thin, rolled wafer tubes from Gottlieben in the canton of Thurgau. They are crisp and often filled with a sweet cream. All over Switzerland they are known as a fine pastry.
wichtigste: Gottlieber Hüppen come from Gottlieben in Thurgau.
They are thin, rolled wafers.
They are often filled with chocolate or praline.
Gottlieben lies on the Seerhein between Lake Constance and the Untersee.
The Hüppen are sold in tins and are often given as presents.

abschnitte.text: A **Hüppe** is a very thin wafer. The batter is baked wafer-thin and rolled into a tube while it is still warm. As it cools, the wafer becomes crisp. The tubes are then filled with a cream, for example made of **chocolate** or **praline**. You eat them with coffee, as a dessert or simply as a treat.

**Gottlieben** is a small village in the canton of **Thurgau**. It lies on the **Seerhein**, the short stretch of the Rhine between Lake Constance and the Untersee. The village has lovely old half-timbered houses and a **castle**. Right opposite, on the other side of the Rhine, lies Germany.

The Hüppen carry the name of the place they come from. They are made in Gottlieben and sold in pretty **tins**. Many people buy them as a souvenir or a present. This is how a very small village has become known all over Switzerland.

gewusst: Gottlieben is one of the smallest municipalities in the canton of Thurgau.
Hüppen are baked so thin that you can almost see through them.

teile.einleitung: St Bernards are big, strong dogs. They are named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard Pass in Valais, where monks searched for travellers in the snow with their help.
wichtigste: St Bernards are named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard Pass.
The pass lies in Valais, on the border with Italy.
Monks kept big dogs there that helped travellers in the snow.
The most famous St Bernard was called Barry.
The St Bernard is regarded as the national dog of Switzerland.
Today helicopters and avalanche dogs of other breeds do the rescuing.

abschnitte.text: The **Great St Bernard** is a high Alpine pass between Valais and Italy. Almost 1,000 years ago monks founded a **hospice** up there. A hospice is a house where travellers spend the night and get help. The way over the pass was dangerous, especially in winter in snow and fog.

From the 17th century the monks kept big **dogs**. The dogs accompanied the monks on their journeys and with their good **noses** could find people in the snow. In this way they helped to save many travellers. Later these dogs were named after the pass **St Bernards**.

The best known St Bernard was called **Barry**. He lived around the year 1800 and is said to have saved over 40 people. After his death he was preserved and can be seen today in the **Natural History Museum of Bern**. The famous little barrel at the neck, by the way, is only a legend.

Today's St Bernards are heavier than the dogs of the past and are no longer used for rescue. That task is taken over by **helicopters** and lighter **avalanche dogs**. The **Fondation Barry** in Martigny goes on breeding St Bernards. In summer you can also visit the dogs on the pass.

gewusst: A fully grown St Bernard can become as heavy as a grown person.
The hospice on the Great St Bernard is still lived in by canons today.

teile.einleitung: Aarau is the main town of the canton of Aargau. The town lies on the Aare at the foot of the Jura. It is known for its pretty old town with painted gables.
wichtigste: Aarau is the main town of the canton of Aargau.
The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament work here.
The town lies on the Aare.
Aarau is called the “Town of the Beautiful Gables”.
In 1798 Aarau was for a short time the capital of the Helvetic Republic.

abschnitte.text: Aarau is the **main town** of the canton of **Aargau**. Here the **government** and the cantonal parliament, the **Grand Council**, have their seat. The canton of Aargau came into being in **1803**. The town lies on the **Aare**, between Zurich, Basel and Bern. That is why it is also an important railway junction.

The **old town** of Aarau is well preserved. Many houses have brightly painted wooden surfaces under the roof, the **eaves soffits**. Whoever walks through the streets and looks up sees patterns, flowers and figures. That is why Aarau is called the “**Town of the Beautiful Gables**”. In the old town also stands the old Rore tower, part of today's town hall.

In **1798** the old Confederation was replaced by the **Helvetic Republic**. Aarau was then for a short time its **capital**. Also well known is the **Aarau Cantonal School**. There the young **Albert Einstein** took his school leaving exam in 1896. Every year in September the children celebrate the **Bachfischet**, a parade with lanterns along the town stream.

gewusst: Aarau was the first capital of a republic for the whole of Switzerland, if only for a few months.

teile.einleitung: Lake Hallwil is a lake in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau. Its southern end reaches into the canton of Lucerne. In summer you can swim there, take a boat trip and walk along the shore.
wichtigste: Lake Hallwil lies in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau.
A small part in the south belongs to the canton of Lucerne.
It is the largest lake that lies almost entirely in Aargau.
Hallwyl moated castle stands at the northern end.
In summer, scheduled boats cross the lake.
In many places the shore is a nature reserve.

abschnitte.text: The **Seetal** (“Lake Valley”) is a long valley between Aargau and Lucerne. Two lakes lie in it: **Lake Baldegg** and the larger **Lake Hallwil**. Both were shaped by a glacier in the Ice Age. On the shore of Lake Hallwil there are villages such as Meisterschwanden, Seengen and Beinwil am See.

At the northern end of the lake stands **Hallwyl Castle**. It is a **moated castle**, which means it is surrounded by water-filled moats and stands on islands. The noble family of Hallwyl lived here for many centuries. Today the castle is a **museum** where you can learn about life in earlier times.

In summer, Lake Hallwil is a popular place to visit. There are **lidos**, sailing boats and **scheduled boats** that link the villages on the shore. A walking path leads around the lake. In winter, in very cold years, the lake sometimes freezes over.

In the past, many **nutrients** from fertiliser and waste water got into the lake. As a result, too many algae grew, and the fish in the depths lacked **oxygen**. With sewage treatment plants and artificial aeration, the lake became healthier again. Many stretches of shore are a **nature reserve**, so that birds and plants have a habitat.

gewusst: The river Aabach flows out of Lake Hallwil and past Hallwyl Castle.
Rare plants and many water birds live in the reedbeds on the shore.

teile.einleitung: The Höllgrotten are dripstone caves near Baar in the canton of Zug. They lie in the Lorzentobel, a narrow gorge of the river Lorze, and can be visited.
wichtigste: The Höllgrotten lie in the Lorzentobel near Baar in the canton of Zug.
They are dripstone caves with many glittering lime formations.
They were discovered in the 19th century while tufa stone was being quarried.
The formations grew over thousands of years.
Today a circular path leads through several cave chambers.

abschnitte.text: The Höllgrotten are in the **Lorzentobel**, where the Lorze has cut deep into the land. The caves are not very big, but they are richly decorated. Visitors walk along a path through several chambers. Lamps light up the formations so that they can be seen well. Inside, it is cool and damp all year round.

Rainwater seeps through the ground and dissolves **lime** from the rock as it goes. When the water drips from the ceiling in the cave, a tiny bit of lime stays behind. In this way **stalactites** grow downwards from above and **stalagmites** grow upwards from the floor. This is very slow, often only millimetres in many years. That is why the formations in the Höllgrotten are thousands of years old.

The caves were discovered in the 19th century when workers were quarrying **tufa stone** on the slope. Tufa is a porous limestone that used to be popular for building. Soon people noticed how beautiful the hollows were. So they were opened to visitors. Since then, the Höllgrotten have been a popular place to visit in the canton of Zug.

gewusst: Stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites grow from the floor. When they meet, a column forms.
The Höllgrotten are among the best-known show caves in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Fête des Vendanges is the big wine growers' festival of the city of Neuchâtel. It takes place every year at the end of September and celebrates the end of the grape harvest.
wichtigste: The Fête des Vendanges takes place every year in Neuchâtel.
It is celebrated on the last weekend in September.
“Vendanges” means “grape harvest” in English.
The highlight is a big parade with decorated floats.
There is a lot of music, including Guggenmusik bands.
The festival is one of the biggest popular festivals in French-speaking Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: A festival for the grape harvest
abschnitte.text: In autumn, the ripe **grapes** are picked in the vineyards. This harvest is called the **grape harvest**, in French “vendanges”. There are many vineyards around **Lake Neuchâtel**. At the end of the grape harvest, the city of **Neuchâtel** holds a big festival, the **Fête des Vendanges**. It always takes place on the last weekend in September.

The highlight of the festival is the **parade** on Sunday, in French “Corso fleuri”. Floats magnificently decorated with **flowers** move through the streets. **Bands** and Guggenmusik groups play along. Thousands of spectators stand at the side of the road. There is also a parade of its own for children.

For three days, the old town of Neuchâtel is full of stalls, stages and music. Many clubs sell food and drinks. The festival has been celebrated for many decades. Every year it attracts visitors from all over Switzerland. Neuchâtel is the main town of the canton of the same name, where French is spoken.

gewusst: The floats in the Fête des Vendanges parade are decorated with thousands of real flowers.

teile.einleitung: The Glasi Hergiswil is a glassworks in Hergiswil in the canton of Nidwalden. Glass is still blown by hand there. Visitors can watch the glassblowers at work.
wichtigste: The Glasi lies in Hergiswil on Lake Lucerne.
Glass is blown and shaped by hand there.
You can watch the glassblowers at work.
The glassworks has existed since the 19th century.
A museum and a shop belong to the Glasi.

abschnitte.text: Glass consists mainly of **quartz sand**, with other substances such as soda and lime added. In a furnace, everything is melted at very high heat until a glowing, sticky mass is formed. The **glassblower** picks some of it up on a long tube, the **blowpipe**. Then he blows into it, turns and shapes the glass until, for example, a vase or a drinking glass is made.

Glass has been made in Hergiswil since the **19th century**. Like many small glassworks, this one ran into difficulties because factories make glass more cheaply with machines. In the 1970s, the glass artist **Roberto Niederer** took over the Glasi and focused on handwork and designs of its own. This allowed it to carry on.

Today the Glasi is a popular **place to visit**. In the workshop you can see how a finished piece is made from glowing mass. A **museum** tells the history of glassmaking. For children there are play areas all about glass. Hergiswil is easy to reach from Lucerne by train and boat.

gewusst: Molten glass is so hot that it glows red and orange.
Finished glass has to cool down slowly, otherwise it can crack.

teile.einleitung: The apricot is a sweet, orange stone fruit. In Switzerland it is grown mainly in Valais. Apricots from Valais are popular all over the country.
wichtigste: The apricot is a stone fruit with a hard stone.
It originally comes from Asia.
In Switzerland most of the apricots come from Valais.
The Rhône Valley is sunny and dry, ideal for apricots.
They are harvested in summer, above all in July and August.

abschnitte.text: The **apricot** is a **stone fruit**. That means that in its middle lies a hard **stone**. It is related to the plum, the peach and the cherry. Its skin is velvety and orange, sometimes with red cheeks. The apricot originally comes from **Asia**. Over many centuries it came to Europe.

In Switzerland most of the apricots are grown in **Valais**. The **Rhône Valley** is especially **sunny** and **dry**. The mountains protect it from a lot of rain. Apricot trees like that. Dangerous, however, are late **frosts** in spring, when the trees are already in blossom. Then the farmers sometimes protect the blossoms with water or fire.

The apricots are harvested in summer, above all in **July** and **August**. They are eaten fresh, as **jam** or on a tart. Dried apricots are also well known. In Valais a spirit is also distilled from apricots, the **Abricotine**. In summer many farmers sell their fruit directly at the roadside.

gewusst: A good fruit tree does not grow from apricot stones: new trees are mostly grafted so that the fruit stays equally good.

teile.einleitung: Andermatt is a village in the Urseren Valley in the canton of Uri. It lies where the routes over the Gotthard, Furka and Oberalp cross. Today it is a well known holiday and ski resort.
wichtigste: Andermatt lies in the Urseren Valley in the canton of Uri.
Here the routes over the Gotthard, Furka and Oberalp meet.
From Göschenen you reach Andermatt through the Schöllenen Gorge.
In winter Andermatt is a popular ski resort.
The ski area is linked with Sedrun in the Grisons.

abschnitte.titel: In the middle of the Alps
abschnitte.text: **Andermatt** lies at about 1,400 metres in the **Urseren Valley**. From here roads lead over the **Gotthard** to Ticino, over the **Furka** to Valais and over the **Oberalp Pass** to the Grisons. From the north you come through the **Schöllenen Gorge** with the famous **Devil's Bridge**. A railway also links Andermatt with Göschenen and the passes.

In winter there is usually a lot of snow in Andermatt. So it is a popular **ski resort**. The ski area is linked with **Sedrun** in the Grisons. In summer guests come for walking, cycling and trips over the passes. In recent years new hotels, flats and a golf course have been built.

Because of its position on the Gotthard Andermatt was for a long time an important place for the **Swiss army**. Many soldiers were stationed here, and in the mountains there were fortresses. Later the army reduced its installations. After that Andermatt developed more and more into a tourist resort.

gewusst: From Andermatt you can reach three language areas in a few hours: German, Italian and Romansh.

teile.einleitung: The Fondation Beyeler is a famous art museum in Riehen in the canton of Basel-Stadt. It shows works by great modern artists in a bright building in the middle of a park.
wichtigste: The Fondation Beyeler is in Riehen in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
It was founded by the art dealers Ernst and Hildy Beyeler.
The museum opened in 1997.
The Italian architect Renzo Piano designed the building.
The collection includes works by Monet, Cézanne, Picasso and many others.
It is one of the most visited art museums in Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: A museum made from a collection
abschnitte.text: **Ernst and Hildy Beyeler** were art dealers in Basel. Over many years they collected important paintings and sculptures. Later they set up a **foundation**, in French “fondation”. So that their collection would be open to everyone, they had a museum of their own built. It opened in **1997**.

The museum was designed by the famous Italian architect **Renzo Piano**. The long, low building has a glass roof that lets plenty of **daylight** into the rooms. It lies in a beautiful **park** with old trees. In front of the museum there is a pond with water lilies, which recalls the water lily paintings by Claude Monet.

The collection includes works of **classical modernism**, that is art mostly from the 19th and 20th centuries. These include paintings by **Claude Monet**, **Paul Cézanne**, **Vincent van Gogh** and **Pablo Picasso**. Sculptures by the Swiss artist **Alberto Giacometti** can also be seen. The museum also puts on big special exhibitions from time to time.

The canton of **Basel-Stadt** consists of only three municipalities: Basel, **Riehen** and Bettingen. Riehen lies right on the border with Germany. The tram runs from Basel to right in front of the museum. Many visitors also come to Riehen from abroad.

gewusst: So much daylight comes in through the museum's glass roof that you often see the paintings almost as if you were outdoors.
With only three municipalities, Basel-Stadt is the canton with the fewest municipalities in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Fricktal is a region in the north of the canton of Aargau, right on the Rhine. For centuries it belonged to Austria and only became part of the canton of Aargau in 1803.
wichtigste: The Fricktal lies in the north of the canton of Aargau.
In the north, the Rhine forms the border with Germany.
For centuries the Fricktal belonged to Further Austria.
Further Austria was a territory ruled by the Habsburgs.
In 1803 the Fricktal became part of the new canton of Aargau.
Dinosaur bones were found in Frick.

abschnitte.text: The **Fricktal** lies in the north of the canton of **Aargau**, between the Jura and the **Rhine**. Here the Rhine forms the border with **Germany**. The districts of Rheinfelden and Laufenburg belong to the Fricktal. Important places include Rheinfelden, Laufenburg and Frick. The landscape is hilly, with forests, fields and many fruit trees.

For a long time, the Fricktal was not part of the Swiss Confederation. It was part of **Further Austria**. This was the name for the lands of the **Habsburgs** in the west, far away from Vienna. So for centuries the people of the Fricktal had an Austrian ruler. That is why the region is still mostly Catholic today.

Around **1800**, Europe changed greatly because of the wars with France. Austria had to give up the Fricktal. For a short time there was even a **canton of Fricktal** of its own. In **1803**, the area then became part of the newly founded **canton of Aargau**. Since then it has belonged to Switzerland.

In a clay pit near **Frick**, many bones of **dinosaurs** were found, mostly of **Plateosaurus**. These plant-eaters lived over 200 million years ago. At the **Frick Dinosaur Museum** you can marvel at the finds. The Fricktal is also known for its **cherries**.

gewusst: So many Plateosaurus fossils have been found in the Fricktal that it is one of the most important sites for these dinosaurs in Europe.
There are two towns called Rheinfelden: one on the Swiss side and one on the German side of the Rhine.

teile.einleitung: Hohenklingen Castle sits on a wooded hill high above the little town of Stein am Rhein in the canton of Schaffhausen. From up there you have a wide view over the Rhine and the Untersee.
wichtigste: Hohenklingen Castle stands above Stein am Rhein in the canton of Schaffhausen.
It was built in the Middle Ages.
The castle lies on a hill high above the Rhine.
From above you see the Rhine and the Untersee.
Since the Middle Ages the castle has belonged to the town of Stein am Rhein.
Today there is a restaurant in the castle.

abschnitte.text: Hohenklingen Castle lies on a hill north of **Stein am Rhein**. Down on the Rhine lies the little town with its beautifully painted **old town**. The castle is visible from far away. You reach it on foot along a hiking trail or by car along a narrow road. The climb takes about half an hour.

The castle was built in the **Middle Ages**, probably around the year 1200. It first belonged to the **Lords of Klingen**, after whom it is named. Later the **town of Stein am Rhein** bought the castle. Typical of a medieval castle are the tall **keep**, which is the main tower, and the thick **walls**. The castle is well preserved to this day.

From the tower of the castle you have a magnificent **view**. You see the **Rhine**, the **Untersee**, a part of Lake Constance, and in clear weather as far as the Alps. Today there is a **restaurant** in the castle. Many guests combine a visit to the old town of Stein am Rhein with an outing to the castle.

gewusst: Hohenklingen Castle is among the especially well preserved medieval castles in Switzerland.
Stein am Rhein is famous for its brightly painted houses in the old town.

teile.einleitung: The Bürgenstock is a mountain ridge in the canton of Nidwalden high above Lake Lucerne. It has been known for its hotels for over 100 years, and in 1954 the famous actress Audrey Hepburn was married there.
wichtigste: The Bürgenstock lies in the canton of Nidwalden on Lake Lucerne.
Big hotels were built there as early as the 19th century.
Many famous guests visited the Bürgenstock.
Audrey Hepburn was married in 1954 in the chapel on the Bürgenstock.
The Hammetschwand Lift is a lift that goes up the outside of a rock face.
A funicular leads from the lake up to the hotels.

abschnitte.text: The **Bürgenstock** is a mountain ridge that juts into **Lake Lucerne**. It belongs for the most part to the canton of **Nidwalden**. On one side it drops steeply to the lake. From above you see the lake, Lucerne and mountains such as Pilatus and the Rigi. The highest point is called **Hammetschwand**.

As early as **1873** a first big hotel was opened on the Bürgenstock. More were added later. A **funicular** brought the guests up from the landing stage at Kehrsiten. The Bürgenstock became popular with rich and famous guests from all over the world, including politicians and film stars. Today there is a big, modern **hotel resort** there.

The film actress **Audrey Hepburn** married the actor Mel Ferrer in **1954** in the little **chapel** on the Bürgenstock. Audrey Hepburn was already a world star then. Later she made her home in Switzerland and lived in the canton of Vaud until her death. The wedding made the Bürgenstock even better known.

A special sight is the **Hammetschwand Lift**. This lift goes up the outside of a vertical rock face to the Hammetschwand viewpoint. It was opened in **1905** and is about 150 metres high. It is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe. A rock path built into the steep wall leads to it.

gewusst: The Hammetschwand Lift on the Bürgenstock is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe.
Audrey Hepburn later lived for many years in Tolochenaz in the canton of Vaud.

teile.einleitung: The Eringer is a breed of cattle from the Valais. The cows are small, strong and dark, and they like to test their strength against each other. This is how the well-known cow fights came about.
wichtigste: The Eringer is an old breed of cattle from the Valais.
The name comes from the Eringer valley, in French the Val d'Hérens.
The cows are rather small, strong and mostly dark brown to black.
They measure their strength by pushing their heads against each other.
At the cow fights, the strongest cow is crowned queen.
The breed is well suited to life in the mountains.

abschnitte.text: The **Eringer** is an old **breed of cattle** from the **Valais**. Its name comes from the **Eringer valley**, in French the **Val d'Hérens**, a side valley near Sion. The animals are rather small, but very **strong**. Their coat is mostly dark brown to black, and they have short, strong horns.

Eringer cows are well suited to life in the **mountains**. They can walk safely on steep pastures and manage with simple feed. In summer, many of them spend their time on the **alp**. Farmers keep them for **milk** and **meat**.

Eringer cows have a strong will and want to settle their rank in the herd. To do this, they push their **heads** against each other and shove. The cow that gives up and runs away has lost. This natural behaviour led to the **cow fights**, in French **Combats de reines**.

At the cow fights, cows compete against each other in different **categories**. The strongest cow is crowned **queen** and often receives a big bell. In spring there are fights in several places in the Valais and a big **final**. In summer, the queen often also leads the herd on the alp.

For many people in the Valais, the cow fights are an important **tradition** and a popular festival. Supporters say that the cows are only showing their natural behaviour. Animal welfare groups make sure the animals are well looked after. There are therefore rules to make the fights as safe as possible for the cows.

gewusst: Only cows fight at the cow fights, no bulls.
The queen of a herd is called “reine” in French.

teile.einleitung: Charlie Chaplin was one of the most famous film actors in the world. He became known through his silent films, and for almost 25 years, until his death, he lived in Corsier sur Vevey in the canton of Vaud.
wichtigste: Charlie Chaplin was born in London in 1889.
He became world famous with silent films.
His best known character is the Tramp with bowler hat, cane and shoes that are too big.
From 1953 he lived in Corsier sur Vevey in the canton of Vaud.
He died there in 1977.
His former home is now the museum “Chaplin’s World”.

abschnitte.text: **Charlie Chaplin** was born in **London** in **1889**. He grew up in poverty and was on the stage as a child. As a young man he went to America and became famous there with **silent films**. In silent films there are no spoken words. The actors tell the story with gestures and facial expressions, and music plays along.

Chaplin’s most famous character is the **Tramp**, a poor but lovable vagabond. He wears a **bowler hat** on his head, a small moustache, a **walking cane** and far too big **shoes**. He waddles in a funny way and gets into many crazy situations. Chaplin was not only an actor but also a **director** and often wrote the music for his films. Well known films are **“The Gold Rush”** and **“Modern Times”**.

In **1953** Chaplin moved to Switzerland with his family. He lived in the **Manoir de Ban**, a big house with a park in **Corsier sur Vevey** above **Lake Geneva**. There he lived with his wife and his many children. From here he still made a few films. Charlie Chaplin died in **1977** in Corsier sur Vevey and is buried there.

His former home is now a **museum** called **“Chaplin’s World”**. It was opened in **2016**. You can see the rooms in which the family lived, and in a film studio you can experience scenes from his films that have been rebuilt. In **Vevey** there is also a **statue** of Charlie Chaplin on the lakeshore. Many visitors have their photo taken there with him.

gewusst: Charlie Chaplin lived in Switzerland for almost 25 years.
Chaplin composed many of the tunes for his films himself.

teile.einleitung: At 991 metres, the Hohgrat is the highest point in the canton of Thurgau. It lies in the south of the canton near Fischingen. Thurgau is hilly, but it has no really high mountains.
wichtigste: The Hohgrat is 991 metres high.
It is the highest point in the canton of Thurgau.
It lies in the south of the canton near Fischingen.
The area is called the Hinterthurgau.
Thurgau has hills, but no Alpine peaks.

abschnitte.titel: A hill as the highest point
abschnitte.text: At **991 metres** above sea level, the **Hohgrat** is the highest point in **Thurgau**. Compared with the Alps this is not much, and many Alpine peaks are three times as high. The Hohgrat is wooded and is more a long ridge of hills than a pointed peak. It is easy to reach on walking trails.

The Hohgrat lies in the **Hinterthurgau**, the southern and hilliest part of the canton. Nearby is **Fischingen** with its well-known **monastery**. In the north, Thurgau is flatter and reaches as far as **Lake Constance**. There are many fruit trees there, which is why Thurgau is also called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”).

abschnitte.titel: The highest points of the cantons
abschnitte.text: Every canton has a **highest point**. In mountain cantons such as Valais or Graubünden, these are peaks over 4,000 metres. In cantons of the Central Plateau such as Thurgau, Zurich or Aargau, they are hills and mountains under 1,300 metres. The canton with the lowest highest point is Basel-Stadt.

gewusst: The highest point in Switzerland is the Dufourspitze at 4,634 metres, almost five times as high as the Hohgrat.
Because of its many apple trees, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien”.

teile.einleitung: Chur is the main town of the canton of the Grisons. The city lies in the Rhine Valley, surrounded by high mountains, and is regarded as one of the oldest cities in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Chur is the main town of the canton of the Grisons.
The city lies in the Rhine Valley, where the Plessur flows into the Rhine.
The Romans already had a settlement here, which they called Curia.
Chur has been a bishop’s seat for many centuries.
In the old town stand the cathedral and many old houses.
The Rhaetian Railway has its headquarters in Chur.

abschnitte.titel: A city in the Rhine Valley
abschnitte.text: Chur lies in the Rhine Valley of the Grisons, where the valley of the **Plessur** meets the Rhine Valley. The Plessur flows into the **Rhine** shortly after the city. Mountains rise all around Chur, for example the local mountain **Brambrüesch**, up which a cable car runs. Because Chur is so easy to reach, it is often called the gateway to the mountains of the Grisons.

People lived in the area of Chur as early as the **Stone Age**. Later the **Romans** built a settlement here called **Curia**, from which the name Chur comes. Because the place lay on important routes over the Alpine passes, it was important early on. That is why Chur is regarded as one of the oldest cities in Switzerland.

Chur has been the seat of a **bishop** since the early Middle Ages. The diocese of Chur is among the oldest dioceses north of the Alps. High above the old town stands the **cathedral**, a big church with valuable decoration. In the past the bishop also had a great deal of worldly power over the area.

As the **main town**, Chur is the seat of the government of the Grisons and of the cantonal parliament, which in the Grisons is called the **Grand Council**. The **Rhaetian Railway** also has its headquarters in Chur. It runs red trains through the whole of the Grisons. The famous **Glacier Express** also stops in Chur.

The Grisons is the only canton with three official languages: **German**, **Romansh** and **Italian**. In Chur itself the majority speak German. As the main town, however, the city is there for all three language groups. Many signs and documents of the canton therefore exist in several languages.

gewusst: The name Chur comes from the Roman name Curia.
The artist H. R. Giger, known for his dark fantasy creatures, was born in Chur.

teile.einleitung: Glarus is the main town of the canton of Glarus. The canton and its main town have the same name. Glarus is especially known for the Landsgemeinde, where those entitled to vote cast their votes in the open air.
wichtigste: Glarus is the main town of the canton of the same name.
The town lies in the valley of the Linth, at the foot of the Glärnisch.
Every year in May the Landsgemeinde takes place in Glarus.
In 1861 a great fire destroyed most of the town.
After that, Glarus was rebuilt with straight streets at right angles.
Since 2011 the canton of Glarus has had only three municipalities.

abschnitte.text: Glarus lies in the **Glarus region**, a valley shaped by the river **Linth**. The mighty **Glärnisch** rises right above the town. The mountains are so close that on some days in winter the sun shines only briefly. Glarus is well connected by train to Zurich and Lake Walen.

On the first Sunday in May, those entitled to vote gather on the **Zaunplatz** in Glarus. At the **Landsgemeinde**, they vote by raising their hands instead of putting a slip of paper in a ballot box. This is how laws are passed and offices are filled. Apart from Glarus, only Appenzell Innerrhoden still has this old form of direct democracy.

In May **1861**, a fire broke out in Glarus. A strong foehn wind drove the flames through the town, and a large part of the houses burned down. After that, Glarus was planned anew: since then, the streets have run straight and at right angles, almost like a **chessboard**. You can still see this today when you walk through the town.

In the past, the canton of Glarus had over twenty municipalities. The Landsgemeinde decided to merge them into just three municipalities. Since **2011** there have been **Glarus Nord**, **Glarus** and **Glarus Süd**. Since then, Netstal, Ennenda and Riedern have also belonged to the municipality of Glarus. No other canton has so few municipalities.

gewusst: The Glarus cantonal flag shows Saint Fridolin, a wanderer with a staff and a Bible.
Glarus used to be an important centre of the textile industry, known for printed fabrics.

teile.einleitung: Herisau is the largest municipality in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament have their seat here. Herisau lies in a hilly landscape not far from St Gallen.
wichtigste: Herisau is the largest municipality in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
The government and the cantonal parliament have their seat here.
The cantonal court, however, is in Trogen.
Herisau lies close to the city of St Gallen.
In the past, Herisau was an important centre of the textile industry.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell Ausserrhoden does not have a single main town in the usual sense. In **Herisau**, the **Regierungsrat** (government) and the **Kantonsrat** (parliament) meet. The court is in **Trogen**. This division has to do with the history of the canton, in which various villages were important. Herisau is nevertheless regarded as the main town of the canton.

Herisau is the municipality with the most inhabitants in the canton. In the centre there are beautiful old **Appenzell houses** and the Reformed church. Around the town lie hills with farms and woods. Herisau has a railway station where several railway lines cross.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, many **fabrics** were made and traded in Herisau. The **textile industry** brought work and prosperity to the region. Wealthy merchants built magnificent houses that can still be seen today. Later, other businesses appeared, and today many people also work in nearby St Gallen.

gewusst: Appenzell Ausserrhoden abolished the Landsgemeinde in 1997, and today votes are held at the ballot box.
In Herisau there is the Herisau Museum, which shows the history of the municipality.

teile.einleitung: The Land of Appenzell was once a single state of the Confederation. Only later was it divided into two half-cantons: Appenzell Inner Rhodes and Appenzell Outer Rhodes.
wichtigste: Appenzell joined in 1513 as the 13th state of the Confederation.
At that time Appenzell was still a single Land.
Before that the people of Appenzell had freed themselves from the Abbot of St Gallen.
In 1597 the Land was divided because of religion.
Inner Rhodes stayed Catholic, Outer Rhodes became Reformed.

abschnitte.text: In the Middle Ages the people of Appenzell were subject to the **Abbot of the monastery of St Gallen**. At the start of the 15th century they won more freedom in the **Appenzell Wars**. After that they made alliances with the Confederates. In **1513** Appenzell became a full member of the **Confederation** as the **13th state**. With that the old Confederation of 13 states was complete.

With the **Reformation** came quarrels. Part of the population stayed **Catholic**, another part became **Reformed**. In **1597** the Land was therefore divided into two parts. The Catholic **Inner Rhodes** with the main town of Appenzell and the Reformed **Outer Rhodes**. Since then the two have had governments of their own.

In the Land of Appenzell the men entitled to vote met every year at the **Landsgemeinde**. In the open air they elected their authorities and voted by show of hands. In **Appenzell Inner Rhodes** the Landsgemeinde still exists today, and women now vote there too. Outer Rhodes abolished it in 1997.

gewusst: Appenzell was the last member to join the old Confederation of 13 states.

teile.einleitung: The Bündner Nusstorte, or Grisons walnut tart, is a well known sweet speciality from the canton of the Grisons. It consists of a shortcrust pastry and is filled with walnuts and caramel.
wichtigste: The Bündner Nusstorte comes from the canton of the Grisons.
It is filled with walnuts and caramel.
On the outside it consists of a shortcrust pastry.
It is also called the Engadine Nusstorte.
The tart keeps for a long time.
It is a popular souvenir from the Grisons.

abschnitte.text: The Bündner Nusstorte has a base and a lid of **shortcrust pastry**. This pastry is made from flour, butter, sugar and eggs. In between lies a thick **filling** of chopped **walnuts** cooked in **caramel** and cream. Often a little **honey** is added too. This makes a sweet, sticky and very nourishing cake.

The Nusstorte stays fresh for several weeks if you keep it cool and well wrapped. That is because it contains a lot of **sugar** and **fat** and little water. So it can easily be posted or taken home as a **souvenir**. Because it is so sweet, people usually eat only a small piece.

In the past many people emigrated from the Grisons because there was little work in the mountain valleys. Many of them became **confectioners** abroad and opened cafés in big cities in Europe. The Nusstorte is especially associated with the **Engadine** and is therefore also called the **Engadine Nusstorte**. Today it is sold in many bakeries all over Switzerland.

gewusst: Baumnüsse is the Swiss word for walnuts.
Confectioners from the Grisons used to run cafés in many cities in Europe.

teile.einleitung: In Réclère in the canton of Jura there are dripstone caves, the Grottes de Réclère. There you can marvel at stalactites and stalagmites that have grown over a very long time. Right next to them is a park with large models of dinosaurs.
wichtigste: The Grottes de Réclère are in the canton of Jura.
They are dripstone caves.
Stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites grow up from the floor.
Dripstones grow very slowly from water containing lime.
Next to the caves there is a park with dinosaur models.

abschnitte.text: Rainwater seeps through the ground and the **limestone**. As it does so, it dissolves a little lime. When the water drips from the ceiling of a cave, a tiny bit of lime stays behind. In this way, over a very long time, a spike grows down from the ceiling, the **stalactite**. Where the drops fall on the floor, a **stalagmite** grows upwards. When the two meet, a column forms.

The caves of **Réclère** are in the **Ajoie**, in the far north-west of the canton of Jura, near the border with France. The caves were discovered in the 19th century. Today a lit tour leads through the underground passages. In the cave it is cool and damp all year round, so it is worth taking a jacket.

Next to the caves there is a park where life-size **models of dinosaurs** and other prehistoric animals stand in the forest. There you can find out how these animals lived many millions of years ago. For children especially, the combination of a cave and a prehistoric park makes an exciting day out.

gewusst: A dripstone often grows only a few millimetres in a hundred years.
A way to remember: stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites stand on the ground.

teile.einleitung: The Ebenalp is a mountain in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Inner Rhodes. A cable car runs up from Wasserauen, where the Appenzell Railway also ends.
wichtigste: The Ebenalp lies in the Alpstein in Appenzell Inner Rhodes.
The cable car starts in Wasserauen.
In Wasserauen the railway line of the Appenzell Railways also ends.
Below the summit lie the Wildkirchli caves.
The Aescher mountain inn clings directly to a rock face.
From the Ebenalp you look down on the Seealpsee.

abschnitte.text: The **Ebenalp cable car** is an **aerial cableway**. It runs from **Wasserauen** to the Ebenalp, which is a good 1,600 metres high. In Wasserauen the railway line of the **Appenzell Railways** also ends, so the place is easy to reach. At the top the Ebenalp offers a wide view over the Appenzell region as far as Lake Constance.

Below the summit lie the caves of the **Wildkirchli**. There people found bones of **cave bears** and traces of humans from the **Old Stone Age**. Later hermits lived here, and a small **chapel** was set up. A path leads down from the top station through the caves.

abschnitte.titel: The inn on the rock face
abschnitte.text: Directly below the caves stands the **Aescher mountain inn**. It is built right against a huge **rock face**. Photos of it became known worldwide, and many people come to see it for themselves. From here you hike on to the **Seealpsee**.

The Ebenalp belongs to the **Alpstein**, a mountain range made of **limestone**. The highest peak of the Alpstein is the **Säntis**. In the Alpstein there are many hiking trails, mountain lakes and mountain inns. Another cable car runs from **Brülisau** up the **Hoher Kasten**.

gewusst: In the Wildkirchli caves bones of cave bears were found that lived a very long time ago.
The Aescher mountain inn became known all over the world through photos on the internet.

teile.einleitung: The Chienbäse is a spectacular fire custom at carnival in Liestal in the canton of Basel Landschaft. On the evening of Carnival Sunday people walk through the old town with burning bundles of wood and fire carts.
wichtigste: The Chienbäse takes place in Liestal in the canton of Basel Landschaft.
It belongs to carnival and takes place on Carnival Sunday in the evening.
The participants carry burning bundles of pine wood.
In addition burning fire carts are pulled through the town.
The procession goes through the town gate, the Törli.
The fire brigade makes sure that nothing happens.

abschnitte.text: On the evening of **Carnival Sunday** it gets dark in **Liestal** and suddenly bright. Many people carry burning **Chienbäse** on their shoulders through the town. A Chienbäse is a big bundle of **pine wood** that burns fiercely. The word “Chien” comes from **Kienholz**, that is resin rich pine wood, which burns well. Thousands of spectators line the streets.

Besides the bundles of wood, **fire carts** are also pulled through the town. These are carts made of iron, piled high with wood and set alight. The flames shoot metres high into the air. The procession goes through the **Törli**, the old town gate of Liestal. When the fire carts pass through the narrow gate, it gets very hot there.

So that nobody comes to harm, the **fire brigade** is there. It sprays the house fronts and the Törli with water. The spectators have to keep enough distance. The Chienbäse is an old **custom** that is meant to drive away the winter, like other fire customs at carnival time. For Liestal it is a special high point of the year.

gewusst: At the Chienbäse it is so hot near the Törli that the fire brigade has to cool the town gate with water.

teile.einleitung: Fribourg, in German Freiburg im Üechtland, is the main town of the canton of Fribourg. The city has a beautiful medieval old town and lies exactly on the language border between German and French.
wichtigste: Fribourg is the main town of the canton of Fribourg.
In German the city is called Freiburg.
It was founded in 1157 by the Dukes of Zähringen.
The city is bilingual, and most people speak French.
The river Saane flows in loops around the old town.
The Cathedral of St Nicholas is the landmark.

abschnitte.text: Fribourg was founded in **1157** by **Berthold IV of Zähringen**. The Zähringens also founded other towns, for example Bern. The addition “im Üechtland” in the German name distinguishes the city from Freiburg im Breisgau in Germany. In **1481**, Fribourg joined the Swiss Confederation.

Fribourg lies exactly on the **language border**. Most people speak **French**, but many also speak **German**. The river **Saane**, in French Sarine, is often seen as the border between the two language areas. That is why people sometimes talk about the “Röstigraben” (the “rösti ditch”). The **University of Fribourg** is also bilingual.

The **old town** is one of the biggest medieval old towns in Switzerland. It lies high above the loops of the Saane. Old **bridges**, some of them made of wood, cross the river. The landmark is the **Cathedral of St Nicholas** with its tall tower. From the top you have a wide view over the rooftops.

Since 1899, a **funicular railway** has run in Fribourg between the lower town and the upper town. What is special is that it is driven by **waste water** from the city. One car is filled with water at the top and, with its weight, pulls the other car up. This technique is very rare today.

gewusst: The Fribourg funicular runs on waste water and is one of the last of its kind in Europe.
The University of Fribourg is the only bilingual university in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Birs is a river that rises in the Jura. It flows through the Laufen Valley in the canton of Basel Country and flows into the Rhine at Birsfelden and Basel.
wichtigste: The Birs rises in the Bernese Jura.
It flows through the Laufen Valley in the canton of Basel Country.
At Birsfelden and Basel it flows into the Rhine.
The Birs is about 70 kilometres long.
It flows through the cantons of Bern, Jura, Basel Country and Basel City.
In the past its water drove many mills and factories.

abschnitte.text: The **Birs** rises in the **Jura**, near the place Tavannes in the canton of Bern. From there it flows through narrow valleys and **gorges** northwards. It passes Moutier and Delémont. After that it flows through the **Laufen Valley** and the Birseck as far as Basel.

At **Birsfelden** and Basel the Birs flows into the **Rhine**. The municipality of Birsfelden is named after the river. On its way the Birs flows through four cantons: Bern, Jura, Basel Country and Basel City. It is about **70 kilometres** long.

In the past the water of the Birs was used to drive **mills**, sawmills and factories. For this the water was led into canals. So businesses arose early in the Laufen Valley and the Birseck. Today many stretches of the Birs have been made **more natural** again so that fish and other animals can live there.

gewusst: In the Laufen Valley the Birs is part of a landscape shaped by the Jura.
On hot days many people cool off in the water of the Birs.

teile.einleitung: The Alpine Rhine is the stretch of the Rhine between the Grisons and Lake Constance. In the St Gallen Rhine Valley it forms the border with Liechtenstein and Austria.
wichtigste: The Alpine Rhine arises where the Vorderrhein and Hinterrhein flow together at Reichenau.
It flows through the Rhine Valley into Lake Constance.
In the canton of St Gallen it forms the border with Liechtenstein and Austria.
In the past there were often severe floods.
Today the river is secured with high embankments.

abschnitte.text: At **Reichenau** in the Grisons the **Vorderrhein** and the **Hinterrhein** flow together. From here on it is called the **Alpine Rhine**. It flows past Chur northwards through the **Rhine Valley**. In the end it flows into **Lake Constance**. Later the Rhine leaves Lake Constance again and flows on towards Basel.

In the **St Gallen Rhine Valley** the Rhine forms a **national border**. Further up on the other side lies **Liechtenstein**, further down **Austria** with the federal state of **Vorarlberg**. Over many bridges you can get from one country to the other. Many people live in one country and work in the other.

In the past the Rhine burst its banks again and again and flooded villages and fields. So in the 19th century Switzerland and Austria agreed to **regulate** the river together. High **embankments** were built and the river was made straighter. Today too both countries plan together how to protect the Rhine Valley from **floods**.

gewusst: The Alpine Rhine brings so much gravel and sand into Lake Constance that the shore at the mouth keeps growing further out into the lake.

teile.einleitung: Delémont, in German Delsberg, is the main town of the canton of Jura. The town lies in a wide valley in the Jura and is French speaking.
wichtigste: Delémont is the main town of the canton of Jura.
In German the town is called Delsberg.
The government and parliament of the canton of Jura meet there.
The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland and has existed since 1979.
French is spoken in Delémont.
The old town has a castle of the former Prince Bishops of Basel.

abschnitte.text: **Delémont** is the main town of the canton of **Jura**. Here the **government** and the **parliament** of the canton have their seat. The parliament is called **Parlement** in French in the Jura. The town is also the most important centre for work, schools and shopping in the region.

The canton of Jura used to belong to the canton of **Bern**. Many people in the northern Jura wanted a canton of their own. After several votes, including one in the whole country in 1978, the canton of Jura came into being on **1 January 1979**. So it is the **youngest canton** in Switzerland, and Delémont became its main town.

Delémont has a pretty **old town** with gates, fountains and old houses. There stands a **castle** that was built in the 18th century. It served the **Prince Bishops of Basel** as a residence. These bishops once ruled over the area of today’s Jura.

Delémont lies in a broad valley through which the **Sorne** and the **Birs** flow. The town is an important **railway junction** on the line between Basel and Biel. The people here speak **French**. The German name Delsberg is heard mainly in German speaking Switzerland.

gewusst: In 1978 the whole Swiss people voted on the founding of the canton of Jura.
Delémont has two names: Delémont in French and Delsberg in German.

teile.einleitung: Bad Zurzach lies on the Rhine in the canton of Aargau, right on the border with Germany. The town is known for its warm thermal water, which was discovered in 1955.
wichtigste: Bad Zurzach lies on the Rhine in the canton of Aargau.
On the other side of the Rhine lies Germany.
In 1955 warm thermal water was discovered during drilling.
Since then the town has been a well known spa town.
Even in the Middle Ages Zurzach was known for its big markets.

abschnitte.text: In **1955** people drilled deep into the ground at Zurzach. They were actually looking for **salt**. Instead warm water suddenly shot out of the borehole. From this discovery a **thermal bath** arose, and Zurzach became a spa town. That is why the town today bears the name Bad Zurzach.

Long before there was a thermal bath, Zurzach was already well known. In the **Middle Ages** big **fairs** took place here. These were markets to which merchants came from many countries. They sold cloth, leather and other goods. The Rhine was an important route for transport.

In Zurzach stands the **Verena Minster**. It is named after Saint **Verena**. According to the legend she lived here and helped poor and sick people. Her grave became a place to which many pilgrims travelled. This too brought many people to Zurzach.

gewusst: The thermal water of Bad Zurzach comes from a depth of several hundred metres.
Bad Ragaz, Leukerbad and Scuol are also thermal resorts, but lie in other cantons.

teile.einleitung: The Geneva Conventions are international treaties that are meant to protect people in wars. They are named after the city of Geneva, where the first convention was signed in 1864.
wichtigste: The Geneva Conventions protect the wounded, prisoners and civilians in wars.
The first Geneva Convention was signed in 1864.
The impetus came from Henry Dunant of Geneva.
The four conventions in force today date from 1949.
Almost all the states in the world have accepted them.
Switzerland keeps the treaties.
