abschnitte.text: Even in a war there are **rules**. The most important ones are in the **Geneva Conventions**. They require that the **wounded** are cared for, no matter which side they fought on. **Prisoners** must be treated humanely. And **civilians**, people who are not fighting, are to be protected. These rules are also called **international humanitarian law**.

The impetus came from the Geneva businessman **Henry Dunant**. In 1859 he came to a battlefield at **Solferino** in northern Italy. He saw that many wounded men were left without help, and he organised help with volunteers. Afterwards he wrote a book about it. In 1863 this led to the founding of the **International Committee of the Red Cross** in Geneva. In 1901, Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

The **first Geneva Convention** was signed by several states in Geneva in **1864**. Further treaties were added later. After the Second World War, four new conventions were agreed in **1949**, and they still apply today. In 1977, additional protocols were added. Today **almost all the states in the world** have accepted the conventions.

**Switzerland** is the state that keeps the originals of the treaties. It is therefore called the **depositary state**. The **red cross** on a white background is the protective emblem of the conventions. It is the Swiss flag with the colours reversed, as a tribute to Switzerland. The International Committee of the Red Cross still has its headquarters in Geneva.

gewusst: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped.
The Geneva Conventions are among the few treaties that have been accepted by almost all the states in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Einsiedeln Schafbock is a traditional biscuit from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is a honey gingerbread biscuit that is shaped in wooden moulds.
wichtigste: The Schafbock is a speciality from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is a gingerbread biscuit made with honey.
The dough is pressed into carved wooden moulds.
The picture often shows a ram.
Einsiedeln is a well-known place of pilgrimage with a large monastery.

abschnitte.text: The **Einsiedeln Schafböcke** are a flat, firm biscuit made from **gingerbread dough** with **honey**. The dough is pressed into **wooden moulds**. These are wooden forms with a picture carved into them. After baking, you can see the picture as a relief on the biscuit, often a **ram** (“Schafbock”).

**Einsiedeln** in the canton of **Schwyz** has been an important **place of pilgrimage** since the Middle Ages. Many pilgrims visit the **monastery** with the Black Madonna. From early on, they bought biscuits as a souvenir for their families at home. This is how the Schafböcke became known far and wide.

You can still buy the Schafböcke in the **bakeries** of Einsiedeln today. Some bakeries still use old, beautifully carved **moulds** for them. The biscuit is quite hard and keeps for a long time. Many visitors take it home as a **souvenir**.

gewusst: Some of the wooden moulds for the Schafböcke are very old and are kept like little works of art.

teile.einleitung: The Bourbaki Panorama in Lucerne is a huge circular painting. It shows how in winter 1871 the French Bourbaki army came into Switzerland and was taken in here.
wichtigste: The Bourbaki Panorama stands in Lucerne.
It is a huge circular picture that you view from the middle.
It shows the crossing of the Bourbaki army into Switzerland in 1871.
Over 80,000 exhausted French soldiers were taken in in Switzerland.
The picture was painted by Edouard Castres.
The Panorama recalls humanitarian aid.

abschnitte.text: A **panorama** is a huge painting that hangs all the way round a wall. The visitors stand in the middle and are surrounded by the picture. In this way you feel as if you were standing in the middle of the landscape yourself. The **Bourbaki Panorama** is over 100 metres long and about 10 metres high.

In 1870 and 1871 France and Germany were at war. In winter a French army under **General Bourbaki** fell into great distress. The soldiers were hungry, sick and freezing. In February **1871** over **80,000 soldiers** were allowed to cross into Switzerland at Les Verrières in the canton of Neuchâtel. They had to hand over their weapons.

The soldiers were spread over many places all over Switzerland. The population gave them food, clothes and a place to sleep. Doctors and helpers nursed the sick. After a few weeks the soldiers could return to France. This **humanitarian aid** was one of the first great tasks for the young **Red Cross**.

The picture was painted by the painter **Edouard Castres**, who had himself been there as a helper. The Panorama was first shown in Geneva and came to **Lucerne** in 1889. Today it stands in a museum that explains the history.

gewusst: In the past panoramas were as popular as cinemas are today.
The Bourbaki Panorama is one of the few large circular pictures from the 19th century that still survive today.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzeller Mountain Dog is a dog breed from the Appenzell region. It is a lively, alert herding dog. Typical is its three coloured coat in black, white and brown.
wichtigste: The Appenzeller Mountain Dog comes from the Appenzell region.
It is one of four Swiss mountain dog breeds.
Its coat is marked in black, white and brown.
Typical is the curled tail, which is carried over the back.
It is very lively and watchful.

abschnitte.text: The **Appenzeller Mountain Dog** used to be a helper of the farmers in the **Appenzell region**. It rounded up the cattle and guarded house and farm. That is why it is called a **herding dog**. It is medium sized, strong and very agile. It reports with barking when strangers come.

The Appenzeller's coat is short and **three coloured**: mostly **black** with **white** and **brown** markings. Over the eyes it often has brown spots. Especially striking is its **ringed tail**, which it carries curled over its back. By this you can tell it easily from the other mountain dogs.

There are four Swiss **mountain dog breeds**: the **Bernese Mountain Dog**, the **Greater Swiss Mountain Dog**, the **Entlebucher** and the **Appenzeller**. All are three coloured. The Appenzeller needs a lot of exercise and a task. In a small town flat without room to run it does not feel well.

gewusst: Of the four Swiss mountain dogs only the Appenzeller has a curled ringed tail.

teile.einleitung: The Franches-Montagnes horse (known in German as the Freiberger) comes from the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura. It is strong, calm and friendly and is regarded as the last native horse breed of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Franches-Montagnes horse comes from the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
In German the area is called the Freiberge.
It is regarded as the last native horse breed of Switzerland.
These horses are strong, calm and versatile.
They are used as riding horses and as draught horses.
The National Stud Farm in Avenches looks after the breeding.

abschnitte.text: The **Franches-Montagnes horse** is a **breed of horse** from Switzerland. It is named after the **Franches-Montagnes**, a high plateau in the canton of **Jura**. In German the area is called “Freiberge”. Horses have been bred there for a long time. The Franches-Montagnes horse is regarded as the last original horse breed of Switzerland.

These horses are medium-sized and **strong**, with powerful legs. Most have a brown coat or are chestnuts with a reddish coat. They have a **calm and friendly** character. That is why they are also well suited to children and beginners. They have plenty of stamina and cope well with the harsh climate in the Jura.

These horses are very **versatile**. In the past they mainly helped on farms and pulled carts and ploughs. The Swiss Army also used them as draught animals for a long time. Today they are used as **riding horses**, as **carriage horses** and for leisure. Sometimes they even still work in the forest, pulling tree trunks.

Every year in August, the **Marché-Concours** takes place in **Saignelégier**. This is a big festival all about the Franches-Montagnes horse. There are horse shows, parades and races. The breed is also supported by the Confederation at the **National Stud Farm** in **Avenches** in the canton of Vaud. On the pastures of the Franches-Montagnes, you often see the horses grazing freely among the fir trees.

gewusst: In the Franches-Montagnes, horses often graze on open pastures between single fir trees, the so-called wooded pastures (“Wytweiden”).
The Marché-Concours in Saignelégier has been held for over a hundred years.

teile.einleitung: The Glarner Pastete is a sweet pastry from the canton of Glarus. It is made of crisp puff pastry and has a filling of almonds and plums. Throughout Switzerland it is regarded as a typical speciality of Glarus.
wichtigste: The Glarner Pastete is a speciality from the canton of Glarus.
It is made of puff pastry.
It is filled with almond paste and plum purée.
The pastry is round and nicely decorated on top.
You can buy it in bakeries and confectioners' shops in the Glarus region.

abschnitte.text: The case of the pastry is made of **puff pastry**. This dough consists of many thin layers of dough and butter. When it bakes, the layers rise and become crisp. Inside is a filling of **almond paste** and **plum purée**. This makes the pastry taste nutty and fruity at the same time.

abschnitte.titel: A piece of the Glarus region
abschnitte.text: The canton of **Glarus** lies in a narrow valley between high mountains. Many regions of Switzerland have a typical pastry of their own, and for Glarus it is the Pastete. Bakeries in the canton make it and also sell it as a gift. Anyone who visits the Glarus region often takes a Pastete home.

Besides the Pastete, Glarus is also known for **Schabziger**, a spicy herb cheese. Such **regional specialities** have often been made for many generations using old recipes. They are part of the culture of a canton, like customs or dialects. That is why they are gladly looked after in Switzerland.

gewusst: Puff pastry often has several hundred wafer-thin layers.
Schabziger from Glarus gets its greenish colour from a herb called blue fenugreek (“Schabzigerklee”).

teile.einleitung: The Étang de la Gruère is a moorland pond in the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura. It is surrounded by forest and raised bog and is a nature reserve.
wichtigste: The Étang de la Gruère lies in the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
“Étang” is the French word for pond.
The water is dark in colour because of the peat.
A protected raised bog lies around the pond.
In the past the pond was dammed to run a mill.

abschnitte.text: The Étang de la Gruère lies on the high plateau of the **Franches-Montagnes**, in the canton of **Jura**. The pond is surrounded by spruces, birches and mountain pines. A **raised bog** spreads out around the water. A raised bog is very wet ground that is fed only by rain.

Mostly **sphagnum moss** grows in the bog. When the plants die, they hardly rot at all because of the wetness and turn into **peat**. Brown substances dissolve from the peat into the water. That is why the pond looks dark, almost like tea. In calm weather, the trees are reflected in it as in a mirror.

The pond is partly man-made: in the past, the water was dammed for a **mill**. Today the area is a **nature reserve** and is one of the most valuable moorland landscapes in Switzerland. A circular path leads around the pond. Visitors must not leave the paths, so that the delicate bog soil is not trampled.

gewusst: Peat grows in a bog by only about one millimetre a year.
Many visitors come especially in autumn, when the birches turn yellow.

teile.einleitung: Biel/Bienne lies in the canton of Bern on Lake Biel. It is the biggest bilingual city in Switzerland: many people speak German, many French.
wichtigste: Biel/Bienne is the biggest bilingual city in Switzerland.
Biel is the German name, Bienne the French name.
The city lies in the canton of Bern on Lake Biel.
Street signs are written in both languages.
Biel is an important city of the watch industry.
Above the city lies Magglingen with the federal sports centre.

abschnitte.text: In **Biel/Bienne** live people who speak **German** and people who speak **French**. That is why the city has two names. Street signs, offices and many schools exist in both languages. Many people switch back and forth quite naturally in daily life. Sometimes a funny mixture of both languages arises.

Biel is an important city of the **watch industry**. Well known watch firms have their seat here, for example Swatch and Omega. Watchmaking came to Biel in the 19th century and brought many jobs. To this day many people work in this field.

abschnitte.titel: On the lake and the Jura
abschnitte.text: Biel lies at the north eastern end of **Lake Biel**, at the foot of the **Jura**. A funicular goes up to **Magglingen**. There stands the Federal University for Sport, where sportsmen and sportswomen train. In Lake Biel lies **St Peter's Island**, which is really a peninsula.
Biel has a pretty **old town** with narrow streets and old fountains. The city grew strongly above all with industry. At the national exhibition **Expo.02** in 2002 Biel was one of the venues.

gewusst: The city of Fribourg is also bilingual, but Biel/Bienne is bigger.
In Biel/Bienne many people say “Merci vielmal”, a mixture of French and German.

teile.einleitung: Bern is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament of Switzerland. Even so, the Federal Constitution names no capital. That is why Bern is officially called the Federal City.
wichtigste: Bern is officially called the Federal City (Bundesstadt).
The Federal Constitution does not lay down a capital.
The Federal Council and Parliament have their seat in Bern.
Bern was chosen as the seat by the Federal Assembly in 1848.
Other federal authorities have their seat in other cities.
The Federal Supreme Court, for example, is in Lausanne.

abschnitte.text: In many countries the constitution lays down exactly which city is the **capital**. In Switzerland it is different. The **Federal Constitution** names no capital. That is why Bern is officially called the **Federal City**, that is, the city in which the authorities of the Confederation sit. In everyday life many people nevertheless say that Bern is the capital of Switzerland.

In **1848** modern Switzerland was founded as a **federal state**. After that it had to be decided where government and parliament should work. The **Federal Assembly** chose Bern in November 1848. **Zurich** and **Lucerne** had also had hopes. Bern was well placed, close to the border between the German speaking and the French speaking parts of Switzerland.

Not all federal authorities sit in Bern. The **Federal Supreme Court**, the highest court in Switzerland, is in **Lausanne**. The **Federal Criminal Court** is in **Bellinzona**, the **Federal Administrative Court** in **St Gallen**. In this way responsibility is spread over different parts of the country. That suits Switzerland, where the cantons and regions carry a lot of weight.

Bern lies on the **Aare**, which flows in a big loop around the old town. The **old town** with its arcades and fountains is a **UNESCO World Heritage** site. Landmarks are the **Federal Palace**, the **Zytglogge** and the bears in the **Bear Park**. Bern is also the capital of the canton of Bern.

gewusst: In the Federal Constitution the word “capital” does not appear for Bern.
The highest court in Switzerland does not sit in Bern but in Lausanne.

teile.einleitung: The Old Cantonal School Aarau is one of the oldest secondary schools in Switzerland. It was founded at the start of the 19th century. It is world famous because Albert Einstein took his school leaving exam here.
wichtigste: The Cantonal School Aarau was founded in 1802.
It is regarded as the oldest non-church secondary school in Switzerland.
Albert Einstein attended the school as a teenager.
In 1896 he finished here with the Matura.
After that Einstein studied in Zurich.

abschnitte.text: The **Cantonal School Aarau** was founded in **1802**, so even before the canton of Aargau existed. It is regarded as the oldest **non-church secondary school** in Switzerland. At that time higher schools were otherwise mostly run by churches or monasteries. At the Cantonal School young people prepare for the **Matura**. With the Matura you can study at a university.

As a teenager **Albert Einstein** came to Aarau. He lived with a family in the town and attended the Cantonal School. The teaching there left the pupils plenty of room to think and observe for themselves. Einstein felt at home in Aarau. In **1896** he finished with the **Matura** and then began his studies in **Zurich**.

Later Einstein became one of the most famous **physicists** of all time. He developed the **theory of relativity** and received the **Nobel Prize in Physics**. Some of his most important work he wrote in Bern, where he worked at the Patent Office. The Cantonal School Aarau is still proud of its famous pupil today.

gewusst: Einstein is said to have later remembered his school days in Aarau fondly, because there one was allowed to think freely.

teile.einleitung: The Fête des Vignerons is a huge wine growers' festival in Vevey on Lake Geneva. It only takes place about every 20 to 25 years, most recently in 2019.
wichtigste: The Fête des Vignerons takes place in Vevey in the canton of Vaud.
It is only celebrated about every 20 to 25 years.
The last two festivals were in 1999 and 2019.
It honours the work of wine growers.
It is organised by the Confrérie des Vignerons.
Since 2016 it has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.

abschnitte.text: **Vignerons** is French for **wine growers**, the people who look after vines and make wine. The **Fête des Vignerons** honours their work. It is organised by the **Confrérie des Vignerons**, an old brotherhood of wine growers in Vevey. It also gives awards to the best vine growers of the region.

abschnitte.titel: Only a few times per century
abschnitte.text: The festival is very rare. It only takes place about **every 20 to 25 years**, which is roughly four or five times in a century. The last two festivals were in **1999** and **2019**. Many people therefore only experience the Fête des Vignerons a few times in their lives. Some even take part several times, as a child and later as an adult.

For the festival, a huge **arena** is built on the big **market square of Vevey**. In it, thousands of performers put on a show with **music, dance and singing**. It tells the story of the year in the vineyard. Most of the performers are volunteers from the region. The performances last several weeks.

abschnitte.titel: A cultural heritage of the world
abschnitte.text: In **2016**, **UNESCO** added the Fête des Vignerons to its list of **intangible cultural heritage**. This protects and recognises a living tradition. Vevey lies in the canton of **Vaud** on Lake Geneva. Nearby are the steep vineyards of **Lavaux**, which are also a World Heritage Site.

gewusst: Several thousand volunteers took part in the Fête des Vignerons in 2019.
In 2016, the Fête des Vignerons was the first Swiss tradition on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

teile.einleitung: The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland. It rises in the Bernese Alps and flows into the Rhine in Aargau. On the way it flows through several lakes and big cities.
wichtigste: The Aare is the longest river that lies wholly in Switzerland.
It rises at the Aare glaciers in the Grimsel area.
It flows through Lake Brienz, Lake Thun and Lake Biel.
In Bern it flows round the old town in a big loop.
The canton of Aargau is named after it.
At Koblenz in Aargau it flows into the Rhine.

abschnitte.titel: From the glaciers to the Rhine
abschnitte.text: The **Aare** begins at the **Aare glaciers** in the Grimsel area in the Bernese Oberland. It flows through **Lake Brienz** and **Lake Thun**, then to **Bern**. Later it is led through a canal into **Lake Biel**. It goes on past Solothurn, Olten and **Aarau**. At **Koblenz** in Aargau it flows into the **Rhine**. At this point it even carries more water than the Rhine itself.

In the city of **Bern** the Aare makes a big **loop** and flows almost completely round the old town. That is why Bern was once built exactly there: the river protected the city. In summer many people in Bern let themselves drift in the green water. This **Aare swimming** is a popular tradition. Because the current is strong, however, you must be a good swimmer.

The canton of **Aargau** has its name from the Aare. It means roughly “**land on the Aare**”. The river flows right across the whole canton. In Aargau the Reuss and Limmat also flow into the Aare. So it collects the water from a large part of Switzerland. On the Aare stand many hydroelectric power stations that produce electricity.

gewusst: At its mouth the Aare brings more water than the Rhine, yet after that the river is called the Rhine.
Almost half the area of Switzerland drains through the Aare.

teile.einleitung: The Ergolz is the most important river in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. It flows through the Ergolz valley and through Liestal and runs into the Rhine at Augst.
wichtigste: The Ergolz is a river in the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
It flows through the Ergolz valley.
On its way it flows through Sissach and Liestal.
At Augst it flows into the Rhine.
The Roman town of Augusta Raurica lies at Augst.

abschnitte.text: The **Ergolz** rises in the upper part of the canton of **Basel-Landschaft**, in the Tabular Jura. It flows westwards through the **Ergolz valley**. On its way it passes places such as **Sissach** and **Liestal**, the main town of the canton. Many streams from the side valleys flow into the Ergolz.

At **Augst**, the Ergolz flows into the **Rhine**. Right next to it lie the remains of the Roman town of **Augusta Raurica**. There you can visit a Roman theatre, temples and many finds. The Romans chose this place because roads and water came together here.

The Ergolz valley is an important **transport route**. A **railway line** and a **motorway** run through the valley from Basel towards the Central Plateau. That is why there are many villages, companies and residential areas here. The Ergolz flows right through the middle of this busy valley.

gewusst: At the mouth of the Ergolz lies the Roman town of Augusta Raurica with a large Roman theatre.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzell Wars were struggles at the start of the 15th century. The people of Appenzell no longer wanted to be subject to the Abbot of St Gallen. In the end they won more freedom.
wichtigste: The Appenzell Wars took place at the start of the 15th century.
The people of Appenzell fought against the Prince Abbot of St Gallen.
The abbot was supported by Habsburg.
Important battles were at Vögelinsegg in 1403 and at the Stoss in 1405.
After that Appenzell moved closer to the Confederation.

abschnitte.text: In the Middle Ages the Appenzell region belonged to the territory of the **monastery of St Gallen**. The **Prince Abbot** demanded dues and services from the farmers. The people of Appenzell found the burdens too high. They wanted to decide their own affairs themselves. Around 1400 this led to open quarrel.

The people of Appenzell were supported by the Land of **Schwyz**. The abbot received help from the city of St Gallen and later from the **Habsburgs**. In **1403** the people of Appenzell won the Battle of **Vögelinsegg**, in **1405** the Battle at the **Stoss**. After that their movement briefly spread across the whole region. Later, however, they had to accept setbacks again.

The Appenzell Wars ended after several years with negotiations. The people of Appenzell had won a great deal of independence. As early as **1411** they made an alliance with the **Confederates**. In **1513** Appenzell was finally taken in as the 13th state, a full member of the Confederation.

gewusst: The victory at the Stoss is still celebrated in Appenzell today with an annual pilgrimage.

teile.einleitung: The Badenfahrt is a huge folk festival in the town of Baden in the canton of Aargau. Because it takes place only about every ten years, it is a very special event for many people.
wichtigste: The Badenfahrt is the big town festival of Baden in Aargau.
It takes place only roughly every ten years.
The festival lasts several days in summer.
Clubs build their own festival pubs and stages.
The festival includes a big parade, music and theatre.
Hundreds of thousands of people visit the festival.

abschnitte.titel: A festival for the whole town
abschnitte.text: During the **Badenfahrt** the whole old town of Baden turns into a festival ground. Everywhere there is music, food, theatre and attractions. The festival lasts several days and takes place in summer. Many visitors come from all over Switzerland.

A large part of the festival is organised by **clubs** and groups from Baden. They build their own **festival pubs** (Festbeizen), that is, restaurants for the festival. The pubs are often imaginatively designed and fit the motto. Many volunteers work for months on the building.
Every Badenfahrt includes a big **parade** through the town. Groups show decorated floats, costumes and music. Each Badenfahrt has a **motto** of its own, which decides the design of the festival.

In the past people said **Badenfahrt** when someone travelled to Baden for recovery, to bathe in the hot springs. Such trips were a great pleasure for many people. The present day festival has taken over the old name.

gewusst: Because the Badenfahrt is so rare, many people experience only a few of them in their lives.
The Badenfahrt is among the biggest folk festivals in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Arve is a river that rises in the French Alps near Mont Blanc. In the city of Geneva it flows into the Rhône. At this spot you can see two quite different colours of water.
wichtigste: The Arve rises in the French Alps in the Mont Blanc area.
It flows through the Chamonix valley.
In Geneva it flows into the Rhône.
The spot is called la Jonction.
The water of the Arve is cloudy, that of the Rhône clear and blue.

abschnitte.text: The **Arve** begins in the **French Alps** in the area of **Mont Blanc**. It flows through the valley of **Chamonix** and on through Savoy. Its water comes to a large extent from **glaciers** and from snowmelt. Finally it reaches Switzerland and the city of **Geneva**.

At the **Jonction** in Geneva the Arve flows into the **Rhône**. The Rhône water comes from **Lake Geneva** and is clear and blue. The water of the Arve, on the other hand, is **cloudy** and grey, because it brings fine sand and rock flour from the glaciers. For a while the two colours flow side by side. This can be seen especially well from bridges.

The Arve is a **mountain river** and can swell quickly after thunderstorms or during snowmelt. Then it carries much more water than usual. Because it is cold and strong, swimming in the Arve is dangerous. In Geneva it separates some districts from one another.

gewusst: At the Jonction you can often see a clear line between blue and grey water.

teile.einleitung: Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German village that is completely surrounded by Switzerland. It lies on the Rhine near Schaffhausen, and in everyday life the Swiss franc plays an important part there.
wichtigste: Büsingen belongs to Germany, more precisely to the federal state of Baden-Württemberg.
The village is completely surrounded by Swiss territory.
Such a territory is called an exclave.
Büsingen lies on the Rhine, east of the city of Schaffhausen.
For customs purposes Büsingen belongs to Switzerland.
In everyday life people often pay in francs.

abschnitte.text: An **exclave** is a part of a country that has no direct connection to the rest of the national territory. That is exactly the case with **Büsingen**. The village belongs to **Germany** but is surrounded on all sides by the cantons of **Schaffhausen** and **Thurgau**. The German border is only a few hundred metres away, but Swiss ground lies in between.

Even in the Middle Ages Büsingen belonged to a different territory from the city of Schaffhausen. Later the surrounding area came to Schaffhausen and with it to Switzerland, but Büsingen did not. There were several attempts to attach the village to Switzerland. They had no success, however. So Büsingen has remained a part of Germany to this day.

A **state treaty** between Germany and Switzerland regulates life in Büsingen. For **customs** the village belongs to Switzerland, so there is no customs control at the border with Switzerland. In everyday life people often pay in **francs**, although officially the **euro** is also valid. Many residents work in Switzerland. Büsingen even has two postcodes, a German one and a Swiss one.

In Büsingen German laws apply, and the police come from Germany. Even so, there are many Swiss influences. The village football club, for example, plays in a **Swiss league**. For children it is exciting that you stand in Germany right in the middle of Switzerland.

gewusst: Büsingen has a German and a Swiss postcode.
The football club of Büsingen is the only German club that plays in the Swiss championship.

teile.einleitung: The Creux du Van is a huge rock basin in the Neuchâtel Jura. Its almost vertical walls form a mighty semicircle in which ibex and chamois can often be seen.
wichtigste: The Creux du Van lies in the canton of Neuchâtel in the Jura.
It is a huge rock amphitheatre with almost vertical walls.
The rock walls are around 160 metres high.
The semicircle is over a kilometre wide.
Ibex and chamois live there.
The area is a nature reserve.

abschnitte.text: The Creux du Van looks as if a giant had taken a bite out of the mountain. The **rock walls** are around 160 metres high and stand almost vertical. Together they form a **semicircle** that is over a kilometre wide. The name is French, because in the canton of Neuchâtel people speak French.

The Creux du Van is made of **limestone**, like the whole Jura. Over a very long time **water**, **frost** and **ice** have worn the rock away. Glaciers of the Ice Age also played a part in the basin. So little by little this special shape came about.

**Ibex** live on the Creux du Van, reintroduced here a few decades ago. **Chamois** also climb over the steep rocks. Often you can watch the animals well from the edge. The area is a **nature reserve**, so that plants and animals are protected.

Many people hike up from the village of **Noiraigue** to the Creux du Van. At the top you can walk along the edge of the basin and look far down. Because the walls are so steep, you have to stay behind the barrier. In clear weather you can see as far as the Alps.

gewusst: On the floor of the rock basin it often stays so cool that you can sometimes still find snow there in early summer.
Because of its shape the Creux du Van is sometimes compared to a giant amphitheatre.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Palace in Bern is the most important building of Swiss politics. Parliament meets here, and the Federal Council works here. You can recognise it easily by its big green dome.
wichtigste: The Federal Palace stands in the city of Bern.
The National Council and the Council of States meet here.
The Federal Council also has its seat here.
The parliament building was inaugurated in 1902.
It has a big green dome.
In front of the Federal Palace lies the Bundesplatz with a fountain display.
Visitors can look round the building.

abschnitte.text: In the Federal Palace the members of **Parliament** meet. The Swiss Parliament is called the **Federal Assembly** and consists of two chambers: the **National Council** and the **Council of States**. Each has its own hall in the Federal Palace. Four times a year they come together for a **session**, which lasts three weeks each time. Then they discuss new laws.

The **Federal Council** also has its seat in the Federal Palace. It is the government of Switzerland and consists of seven members. Each member heads a **department**, for example for finance or for transport. Part of the administration works in the **West Wing** and the **East Wing**, which stand to the left and right of the parliament building.

The parliament building was planned by the architect **Hans Wilhelm Auer** and inaugurated **in 1902**. The big **dome** is covered with copper, which has turned green over time. Stones from many parts of Switzerland were used for the building. In this way the building was meant to show that the whole country belongs together. In the hall under the dome stand statues of the three Confederates.

In front of the Federal Palace lies the **Bundesplatz**. There is a fountain display with **26 water jets**, one for each canton. In summer children like to play between the jets of water. Markets, festivals and demonstrations also take place on the square. From the Federal Palace you look down on the other side to the **Aare** and as far as the Alps.

gewusst: You can visit the Federal Palace for free, and during the session you may listen to the debates from the gallery.
The 26 water jets on the Bundesplatz stand for the 26 cantons of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Bündnerfleisch is a meat speciality from the canton of the Grisons. It is beef that is seasoned and dried in the air, and it is eaten in very thin slices.
wichtigste: Bündnerfleisch comes from the canton of the Grisons.
It is made from lean beef.
The meat is salted, seasoned and dried in the air.
In drying it loses a lot of water.
It is cut into wafer thin slices.
The name Bündnerfleisch is protected.

abschnitte.text: Bündnerfleisch is **air dried beef**. Lean pieces from the hind leg of the cow are used for it. The meat is not cooked and not smoked but preserved only by **salt** and **drying**. Its dark red colour is typical. Bündnerfleisch is very lean and has a strong, spicy taste.

First the meat is rubbed with **salt** and **spices**, for example pepper and herbs. After that it rests for a few weeks. Then it is **dried in the air**, which takes several weeks to months. In between the meat is **pressed**. This gives it its typical angular shape. In the end it has lost a large part of its water.

In the past farmers in the Grisons hung the meat in the fresh, dry **mountain air** in winter. In this way they could keep meat for a long time without it going bad. There were no refrigerators then. Today Bündnerfleisch is usually dried in rooms where temperature and humidity are set exactly.

Bündnerfleisch may only be called that if it is made in the canton of the **Grisons**. The name is registered as a **protected geographical indication**. People like to eat Bündnerfleisch on a **Plättli**, a cold platter, with bread, cheese and gherkins. A similar speciality from northern Italy is **bresaola**.

gewusst: Bündnerfleisch is cut so thin that you can almost see through the slices.
In drying the meat becomes much lighter because it loses a lot of water.

teile.einleitung: Chalandamarz is an old spring custom in the Engadine and in other valleys of the Grisons. On 1 March the children walk through the village with bells and songs to drive away the winter.
wichtigste: Chalandamarz is celebrated on 1 March.
The custom is found above all in the Engadine in the Grisons.
The children walk through the village with cowbells and large bells.
With the noise the winter is to be driven away.
The children sing songs in Romansh.
The custom became known through the children’s book “Schellen Ursli”.

abschnitte.text: On **1 March** it is **Chalandamarz** in the Engadine. On this day the schoolchildren walk through the villages. They wear **cowbells** and big **clanging bells** around their waists and ring them loudly. With the loud noise the **winter is to be driven away** and the **spring** welcomed. Many children wear blue herdsmen’s shirts and red caps for it.

The children stop in front of the houses and sing **songs** in **Romansh**. The people give them sweets, fruit or a little money for it. In the evening in some villages there is a festival, often with a dance. The name comes from Romansh and means roughly **“first day of March”**.

The custom became known all over Switzerland through the picture book **“Schellen Ursli”** (Ursli and his Bell). It was written by **Selina Chönz** and drawn by **Alois Carigiet** and appeared in **1945**. In it the story tells of a boy who badly wants a big bell for Chalandamarz. The book is a classic and was also made into a film.

gewusst: In the story Schellen Ursli lives in the Engadine village of Guarda.
In earlier times the year began in March in the old Roman calendar.

teile.einleitung: The old town of Bern lies in a loop of the Aare. It is especially well preserved and has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 1983. Typical are the long arcades, the fountains and the Zytglogge.
wichtigste: The Bern old town has been UNESCO World Heritage since 1983.
It lies in a big loop of the Aare.
Bern was founded in 1191.
The covered walkways are called arcades (Lauben).
Well known are the Zytglogge, the Minster and many fountains with figures.

abschnitte.titel: A city in a river loop
abschnitte.text: Bern was founded in **1191** by Duke **Berthold V of Zähringen**. He chose a spot where the **Aare** makes a tight bend. So the city was protected by the river on three sides. After a great fire in 1405 the houses were increasingly built of **sandstone**. That is why the old town has its typical grey green colour.

Along the main streets there are **arcades** (Lauben). These are covered **walkways** under the houses. Together they are several kilometres long. Underneath you can shop and stroll dry even in rain. Under the arcades steps often lead down into old **cellars**, which today hold shops and bars.

A landmark is the **Zytglogge**, an old gate tower with an astronomical clock. On the hour figures move there. In the streets stand many **fountains** with colourful figures, such as the Kindlifresser (Ogre) Fountain. The **Bern Minster** has the tallest church tower in Switzerland. At the edge of the old town stands the **Federal Palace**.

In **1983** **UNESCO** took the Bern old town into the **World Heritage**. It was honoured because the medieval layout is still very well preserved today. When converting buildings the residents must observe strict rules. In this way the look of the city is preserved.

gewusst: The tower of the Bern Minster is about 100 metres high and so the tallest church tower in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Lake Gruyère is a large reservoir in the canton of Fribourg. In French it is called Lac de la Gruyère. It was created by a dam on the Saane and supplies water for producing electricity.
wichtigste: Lake Gruyère lies in the canton of Fribourg.
In French it is called Lac de la Gruyère.
It was created by the Rossens dam on the Saane.
The dam was built in the 1940s.
The water is used to produce electricity.
The lake lies in the Gruyère region, known for its cheese.

abschnitte.text: Lake Gruyère is not a natural lake. It is a **reservoir**. At **Rossens**, a dam was built right across the valley of the **Saane**. The water built up behind it and filled the valley. This created a long, narrow lake that winds through the hilly landscape.

The water held back flows through **turbines** and produces electricity as it does so. This way of producing electricity is called **hydropower**. The lake is therefore important for the canton of Fribourg. When it was created, farmland and some houses in the valley were lost under the water.

In the middle of the lake there is a small **island** with the ruins of an old castle. In the past it was a hill in the valley. Only because of the reservoir did it become the island of **Ogoz**. When the water level is low, you can sometimes walk across to it. When the water is high, you can only reach it by boat.

The lake is named after the **Gruyère** region, in French Gruyère. The well-known little town of **Gruyères**, with its castle on a hill, lies there. **Gruyère cheese** comes from the region. At the lake you can walk, swim, cycle and paddle a canoe.

gewusst: Lake Gruyère is one of the largest reservoirs in Switzerland.
The Saane is called La Sarine in French and later flows into the Aare.

teile.einleitung: Engelberg is a well-known monastery and holiday village in central Switzerland. It belongs to the canton of Obwalden, but lies separate from the rest of the canton, behind Nidwalden.
wichtigste: Engelberg belongs to the canton of Obwalden.
It lies separate from the rest of the canton, behind Nidwalden.
An area that is cut off like this is called an exclave.
Anyone travelling from Sarnen to Engelberg therefore goes through Nidwalden.
In the village there is a Benedictine monastery from the 12th century.
The Titlis rises above Engelberg.

abschnitte.text: Engelberg belongs to the canton of **Obwalden**, but has no direct link to the rest of the canton. The Engelberg valley can only be reached through the canton of **Nidwalden**. An area that is cut off from the rest like this is called an **exclave**. Anyone travelling from **Sarnen**, the main town of Obwalden, to Engelberg therefore passes through Nidwalden.

In the 12th century, a **Benedictine monastery** was founded in Engelberg. The monks there still live by the rules of Saint **Benedict** today. In the past, the monastery itself ruled over the valley. Only in the 19th century did Engelberg become part of the canton of Obwalden.

The **Titlis**, which is over 3,200 metres high, rises above Engelberg. Cable cars run up to its summit. The **Rotair** gondola turns completely around once during the ride, so that everyone can enjoy the view. At the top there are glaciers and snow, even in summer.

Engelberg is a popular **holiday resort** for walking, climbing and **skiing**. The **Zentralbahn** takes you from **Lucerne** via Stans to Engelberg. Many visitors also come from distant countries. At the end of the railway line, the valley opens out into a wide valley floor.

gewusst: The gondola up the Titlis was the first rotating cable car in the world.
Engelberg means “mountain of the angels”.

teile.einleitung: The Grande Dixence is a huge dam in the canton of Valais. At about 285 metres, it is the tallest gravity dam in the world. It holds back Lac des Dix, whose water is used to produce electricity.
wichtigste: The Grande Dixence stands in the Val des Dix in the Valais.
It is about 285 metres high.
It is the tallest gravity dam in the world.
It holds back the water by its enormous weight alone.
Behind the dam lies the reservoir Lac des Dix.
The water is used to produce electricity.

abschnitte.text: The **Grande Dixence** is built of **concrete**. It is about 285 metres high, almost as tall as the Eiffel Tower in Paris. At the bottom the wall is very thick, and at the top it gets narrower. Huge amounts of concrete were needed to build it. It was built in the 1950s.

There are different kinds of dams. An **arch dam** is curved and directs the pressure of the water sideways into the rock. A **gravity dam**, on the other hand, is so heavy that the water cannot push it away. So the Grande Dixence holds back the water by its **weight** alone.

Behind the dam lies the reservoir **Lac des Dix**. Its water comes mainly from melting **glaciers**. Long tunnels also bring water here from other valleys. In summer the lake fills up, and in winter the water is used when more electricity is needed.

The water flows steeply down through pipes into the Rhône valley. There it drives **turbines** that produce electricity. **Hydropower** is the most important source of electricity in Switzerland. Because the Alps have a lot of water and big differences in height, the Valais is especially well suited to it.

gewusst: You can walk along the crest of the dam, and in summer there are guided tours of the inside.
Inside the dam there are passages through which experts check the wall regularly.

teile.einleitung: In the English Garden in Geneva stands a big clock made of flowers. The Flower Clock recalls the famous Geneva watchmaking craft and is a popular subject for photos.
wichtigste: The Flower Clock stands in the English Garden in Geneva.
Its dial consists of thousands of flowers.
The clock shows the right time.
It recalls the watchmaking craft of Geneva.
The flowers are replanted according to the season.
The Flower Clock has existed since 1955.

abschnitte.text: The **Flower Clock** lies on the shore of Lake Geneva in the **Jardin Anglais**, the English Garden. Its large round **dial** is planted entirely with flowers and plants. Above it the hands turn, driven by a clockwork in the ground. The clock shows the exact time.

The gardeners of the city of Geneva replant the flowers **several times a year**. So the clock fits the season, and the colours and patterns change. The planting needs **thousands** of flowers. The clock was set up in the year **1955**.

Geneva has been a city of **watchmakers** for centuries. Many famous watch firms come from here. The Flower Clock is a tribute to this tradition. Nearby lies the **Jet d’eau**, the famous tall water fountain in the lake.

gewusst: The Flower Clock is among the most photographed places in Geneva.
The clockwork of the Flower Clock is hidden under the ground.

teile.einleitung: The Furka Pass is a high Alpine pass between the cantons of Uri and Valais. It leads from the Urseren valley into the Goms and past a famous glacier.
wichtigste: The Furka Pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of Valais.
It is 2,429 metres high.
It leads from Realp in the Urseren valley to Gletsch in the Goms.
The Rhône Glacier lies nearby.
In winter the pass road is closed.
A railway tunnel runs underneath the pass.

abschnitte.text: The **Furka Pass** lies at **2,429 metres** above sea level. It connects the **Urseren valley** in the canton of **Uri** with the **Goms** in the canton of **Valais**. On the Uri side, the road starts in **Realp**, and on the Valais side it ends in **Gletsch**. The road has many tight bends. Because there is a great deal of snow in winter, it is closed then.

The **Rhône Glacier** lies on the Valais side. Its meltwater forms the **Rhône**, which later flows through Lake Geneva and on to France. In the past, the glacier reached down into the valley at Gletsch. Today it has become much smaller because of global warming. In summer you can even go inside the glacier in an ice cave.

abschnitte.titel: Railway over and under the pass
abschnitte.text: In the past, a railway also ran over the pass. Since **1982**, trains have gone through the **Furka Base Tunnel**, deep under the mountain. Cars are also loaded onto trains there. In summer, the old mountain line is now used by a **steam railway** run by volunteers.

The winding pass road is popular with motorcyclists and cyclists. In 1964, scenes for the **James Bond film** “Goldfinger” were shot here. The old **Hotel Belvédère**, which stands right on a bend above the Rhône Glacier, is also well known.

gewusst: The Rhône, which rises at the Furka Pass, finally flows into the Mediterranean in the south of France.
In summer, part of the Rhône Glacier is covered with white sheets so that it melts less quickly.

teile.einleitung: In the Bear Park in Bern bears live in a large enclosure right on the bank of the Aare. Bears have a long tradition in Bern, for the bear is the heraldic animal of the city.
wichtigste: The Bear Park lies in Bern on the bank of the Aare.
It was opened in 2009.
It lies right next to the old Bear Pit.
The bears there have much more room than before.
The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.
Entry to the Bear Park is free.

abschnitte.text: The **Bear Park** lies on the steep slope between the old town and the **Aare**, right by the **Nydegg Bridge**. The bears can move there over a large area with trees, rocks and caves. They even have access to the water, where they can bathe and play. From paths and viewpoints you can watch the animals well. The park was opened **in 2009**.

Right next to the park lies the **Bear Pit** (Bärengraben). It is a round, walled pit in which Bern used to keep its bears. For the animals the pit was cramped and had a hard floor. That is why the new, much bigger Bear Park was built. The old Bear Pit is today joined to the park and still belongs to it.

The **bear** is the **heraldic animal** of the city and the canton of Bern. On the Bernese coat of arms a black bear walks on a golden stripe. A **legend** tells that Duke Berchtold of Zähringen named the city after the first animal killed on a hunt: a bear. Whether that is true is not known. What is certain is that Bern has kept live bears for centuries.

In the Bear Park live **brown bears**. Brown bears eat plants, fruit and insects, but also meat and fish. In winter they take a **winter rest**: they withdraw into a den and sleep a lot. In the wild in Switzerland bears are very rare. Now and then a bear wanders from Italy into the canton of the Grisons.

gewusst: Bern has kept live bears in the city since the Middle Ages.
In winter you can often hardly see the bears in the Bear Park, because they are resting in their den.

teile.einleitung: The Dammastock is the highest mountain in the canton of Uri. It lies in the Uri Alps on the border with the Valais and is surrounded by big glaciers.
wichtigste: The Dammastock is around 3,630 metres high.
It is the highest mountain in the canton of Uri.
It lies on the border between Uri and the Valais.
On its western side lies the Rhône Glacier.
It belongs to the group of the Uri Alps.
It was first climbed in 1864.

abschnitte.text: At around **3,630 metres** the **Dammastock** is the highest mountain in the canton of **Uri**. It belongs to a mountain chain called the **Damma chain**. The **cantonal border** between Uri and the Valais runs over its summit. So it is a border mountain between two cantons.

On the Valais side lies the **Rhône Glacier**. The **Rhône** rises from it and later flows through Lake Geneva. On the Uri side lies the **Damma Glacier**. Like almost all glaciers in the Alps, these too have melted a great deal in the last decades.

The Dammastock was first climbed in **1864**. Today it is a goal for experienced **high mountain hikers**. Because you have to cross glaciers, you need a rope, ice axe and crampons. The starting points are huts on the Uri or the Valais side.

East of the Dammastock lies the valley of the **Göscheneralp** with a big **reservoir**. In the west the road over the **Furka Pass** leads from the canton of Uri into the Valais. From there you can see the Rhône Glacier well. The region is among the wildest mountain areas of Central Switzerland.

gewusst: The Rhône Glacier at the foot of the Dammastock is the source of the Rhône, which flows all the way to the Mediterranean.
In summer parts of the ice on the Rhône Glacier are covered with white sheets so that it melts more slowly.

teile.einleitung: The Aescher mountain inn clings to a steep rock face under the Ebenalp in Appenzell Inner Rhodes. Photos of the little wooden house under the rock are known all over the world.
wichtigste: The Aescher mountain inn lies in Appenzell Inner Rhodes.
It stands under the Ebenalp right against a steep rock face.
Part of the inn is built into the rock.
Nearby lie the Wildkirchli caves.
You reach it on foot, for example from the Ebenalp.

abschnitte.text: The **Aescher** is an old mountain inn of wood. It stands under a huge rock overhang, so that the rock looks almost like a roof. The back wall of the house is the **rock** itself. Below the inn the slope drops steeply away. From the terrace you see far over the Alpstein area.

Very close by lie the caves of the **Wildkirchli**. There bones of **cave bears** and traces of people from the **Stone Age** were found. Later hermits lived in the caves and built a small chapel. The way to the Aescher leads through these caves.

With the **cable car** you go from Wasserauen up to the **Ebenalp**. From there you walk down to the Aescher in about half an hour. You can also walk up from below. Further down in the valley lies the **Seealpsee**. Because the place is so well known, many guests from all over the world come today.

gewusst: Because the house stands right against the rock, water sometimes drips from the rock wall inside.
The Aescher lies in the Alpstein, the range with the Säntis.

teile.einleitung: The Brünig Railway is a railway line that connects Lucerne with Interlaken. It runs through the canton of Obwalden and over the Brünig Pass into the Bernese Oberland.
wichtigste: The Brünig Railway connects Lucerne with Interlaken.
It runs through the canton of Obwalden and over the Brünig Pass.
The Brünig Railway is a narrow gauge railway with a track width of one metre.
On the steep sections at the Brünig the train runs with a cog wheel.
Today the line is operated by Zentralbahn.
On the way the train passes several lakes.

abschnitte.text: The Brünig Railway begins in **Lucerne** and ends at **Interlaken Ost**. On the way it runs along Lake Alpnach, through the canton of **Obwalden** with Sarnen and Lungern, then over the **Brünig Pass** down to **Meiringen**. After that it goes along **Lake Brienz** as far as Interlaken. The journey is one of the most beautiful railway routes in Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: Up the mountain with a cog wheel
abschnitte.text: On the steepest stretches the grip of the wheels on the rails is not enough. So there is a **rack rail** between the rails there. The train engages in it with a **cog wheel** and can thus travel safely uphill and downhill. Such sections exist, for example, between Giswil and the Brünig and on the side towards Meiringen. On the flat stretches the train runs quite normally without a cog wheel.

The Brünig Railway is a **narrow gauge railway**. The distance between its rails is only one metre, whereas on most railways in Switzerland it is almost one and a half metres. Narrow gauge railways are practical in the mountains because they can take tighter curves. That is why no normal SBB trains can run on the Brünig Railway.

The first sections of the Brünig Railway were opened **in 1888**. For a long time it belonged to the **SBB** and was its only narrow gauge line. Since 2005 it has been operated by **Zentralbahn**. Zentralbahn also runs from Lucerne to Engelberg. Today modern trains run on the line, carrying commuters, schoolchildren and many tourists.

gewusst: In Meiringen the trains have to change direction because the station there is a terminus.
The Brünig Railway was the only narrow gauge line of the SBB.

teile.einleitung: FC St Gallen is a football club from the city of St Gallen. It was founded in 1879, which makes it the oldest football club in Switzerland that still exists today.
wichtigste: FC St Gallen was founded in 1879.
It is considered the oldest football club in Switzerland that still exists.
The club colours are green and white.
It plays its home matches at the Kybunpark.
The club became Swiss champion in 1904 and in 2000.
The fans also call their team the “Espen”.

abschnitte.text: FC St Gallen was founded in **1879**. At that time, football was still completely new in Switzerland. No other football club in the country that still plays today is older. The club is even one of the oldest football clubs on the European mainland. The fans are very proud of this.

FC St Gallen became Swiss champion for the first time in **1904**. Almost a hundred years later, in **2000**, it won the championship title a second time. Many fans still remember this season very fondly. The club also won the Swiss Cup in 1969.

In the past, the club played at the Espenmoos stadium. This is where the nickname **“Espen”** comes from. Since 2008, FC St Gallen has played its home matches in a new stadium in the west of the city, which is now called the **Kybunpark**. It has room for almost 20,000 spectators.

The colours of the club are **green and white**. At home matches, the stadium is often full of green and white scarves and flags. The club is popular all over eastern Switzerland. It also trains many young players in its youth section.

gewusst: FC St Gallen is older than the Swiss Football Association, which was only founded in 1895.
There were 96 years between the club's first and second championship titles.

teile.einleitung: The Three Countries Corner (Dreiländereck) lies in the Rhine harbour of Basel. Here the borders of Switzerland, Germany and France meet.
wichtigste: At the Three Countries Corner Switzerland, Germany and France meet.
It lies in the Rhine harbour of Kleinhüningen in Basel.
The exact point where the borders meet lies in the middle of the Rhine.
On the bank stands a tall, silver monument.
With its Rhine harbours Basel is the port of Switzerland to the sea.
Directly opposite lie Weil am Rhein in Germany and Huningue in France.

abschnitte.text: At the **Three Countries Corner** the borders of three countries come together: **Switzerland**, **Germany** and **France**. The exact point lies in the middle of the **Rhine**, so you cannot step on it. On the bank in Basel, however, you stand very close to it. From there you see Germany on one side and France on the other.
At the tip of the harbour basin stands a tall **silver monument**. It looks a little like a rocket or a tower. It shows that three countries meet here. Many visitors take a photo here.

Around the Three Countries Corner lies the **Rhine harbour of Kleinhüningen**. Big **cargo ships** moor here. Over the Rhine they travel to the **North Sea**, for example to Rotterdam. For Switzerland, which has no sea, the Basel Rhine harbours are therefore very important for trade.

Opposite lie the towns of **Weil am Rhein** in Germany and **Huningue** in France. Between these two the **Three Countries Bridge** crosses the Rhine, a long bridge for pedestrians and bicycles. In the region around Basel many people cross a border every day to go to work or to school.

gewusst: At the Three Countries Corner you can see three countries in a few minutes without changing your position.
Ships from Basel can travel over the Rhine as far as the North Sea.

teile.einleitung: Ederswiler is a small municipality in the canton of Jura. It is the only municipality of the canton in which the majority of people speak German.
wichtigste: Ederswiler is a small municipality in the canton of Jura.
It lies on the border with the canton of Solothurn.
The majority of people there speak German.
In the rest of the canton of Jura people speak French.
Until 1978 Ederswiler belonged to the canton of Bern.

abschnitte.text: **Ederswiler** is a small farming village in the canton of **Jura**. It lies in the district of **Delémont** on the border with the canton of **Solothurn**. The village has only a few residents. All around there are meadows, fields and woods.

The **official language** of the canton of Jura is **French**. Ederswiler, however, is the only municipality of the canton in which the majority speak **German**. That is because the village lies on the language border and the neighbours in the canton of Solothurn also speak German. The language border between German and French does not always follow the cantonal borders.

abschnitte.titel: From the canton of Bern to the Jura
abschnitte.text: In the past Ederswiler belonged to the canton of **Bern**, like the whole of the northern Jura. In **1979** the new **canton of Jura** came into being. Since then Ederswiler has belonged to this canton. So the German speaking village became part of a French speaking canton.

gewusst: The canton of Jura has only one municipality in which the majority speak German: Ederswiler.

teile.einleitung: Buochs airfield lies in the canton of Nidwalden, close to Lake Lucerne. Right next to it, the company Pilatus builds aircraft and tests them here.
wichtigste: Buochs airfield lies in the canton of Nidwalden.
It is located between Stans, Buochs and Ennetbürgen.
The Pilatus aircraft works lie right next to it.
New Pilatus aircraft take off from here for their test flights.
In the past, the airfield was mainly used by the Swiss Army.

abschnitte.text: **Buochs airfield** lies on a plain in the canton of **Nidwalden**, not far from **Lake Lucerne**. Mountains such as the Stanserhorn and the Bürgenstock rise up all around. For a long time, Buochs was mainly a **military airfield** of the Swiss Army. Today it is also used for civilian flights.

Right next to the airfield lie the **Pilatus aircraft works** in Stans. The company was founded in 1939 and is named after Mount Pilatus near Lucerne. Pilatus builds smaller aircraft, for example **training aircraft** for pilots and **business aircraft**. The sturdy PC-6 Porter, which can land on very short runways, is also well known.

Before a new aircraft is delivered, it has to be tested thoroughly. For this, the aircraft take off from Buochs airfield on **test flights**. They check whether everything works properly. Pilatus aircraft from Nidwalden then fly in many countries around the world.

gewusst: The company Pilatus is named after Lucerne's local mountain, which can be seen well from Buochs.

teile.einleitung: The Glacier Garden in Lucerne is an open-air museum. There you can see traces of the last Ice Age in the rock, above all round glacier potholes. It shows that the area around Lucerne once lay under thick ice.
wichtigste: In the Glacier Garden you can see glacier potholes from the Ice Age.
Glacier potholes are round holes in the rock.
They were made by meltwater that spun stones around in a circle.
The potholes were discovered in 1872 while a cellar was being built.
In the rock you can also find traces of an ancient sea beach.
Right next to it stands the well-known Lion Monument.

abschnitte.text: During the last **Ice Age**, the area around Lucerne was covered by a huge **glacier**. The ice was hundreds of metres thick and flowed slowly from the Alps into the Central Plateau. When it became warmer, the glacier melted and left traces in the rock. In the Glacier Garden you can look at these traces up close today.

A lot of **meltwater** flowed under the glacier. It plunged down through cracks and formed whirlpools. Stones spun around in a circle and ground the rock deeper and deeper. This is how round holes, the **glacier potholes**, came about. Some are several metres deep, and the round grinding stones are still lying in them.

In **1872**, Joseph Wilhelm Amrein wanted to build a wine cellar into the rock. While doing so, the workers came across the first glacier pothole. Amrein had more of them uncovered and turned the site into a park for visitors. Since then, the Glacier Garden has been one of the best-known sights in Lucerne.

abschnitte.titel: A beach millions of years ago
abschnitte.text: In the rock of the Glacier Garden you can see even older traces. About 20 million years ago, the coast of a sea with a warm climate lay here. In the sandstone you can find **fossils** of shells and wave patterns from the beach. The museum also has an old **mirror maze**, in which it is easy to lose your way.

gewusst: Right next to the Glacier Garden is the Lion Monument, one of the best-known monuments in Switzerland.
The stones in the glacier potholes are called grinding stones, because they ground out the rock like a mill.

teile.einleitung: The Prince-Bishopric of Basel was a territory that was ruled for centuries by the Bishop of Basel. It also included the area of the present-day canton of Jura.
wichtigste: The Prince-Bishopric of Basel was ruled by the Prince-Bishop of Basel.
The Prince-Bishop was both a church ruler and a worldly ruler.
The area of the present-day canton of Jura belonged to the Prince-Bishopric.
After the Reformation, the Prince-Bishop lived in Porrentruy.
Around 1792 the Prince-Bishopric ended because of the French Revolution.
In 1815 most of the area went to the canton of Bern.

abschnitte.text: A **Prince-Bishop** was two things at once. As a **bishop**, he led the Church in his diocese. As a **prince**, he also ruled over an area in worldly terms, like a king over land and people. The area ruled by a Prince-Bishop was called a **Prince-Bishopric**. The Prince-Bishopric of Basel belonged to the Holy Roman Empire.

Large parts of the **Jura** belonged to the Prince-Bishopric of Basel. This included the area of the present-day **canton of Jura**, but also the Bernese Jura and parts of Basel-Landschaft. Its rule began in the year 999, when the bishop received the monastery of Moutier-Grandval with its lands. After that, the territory grew over many centuries.

The city of **Basel** became **Reformed** in 1529. The Catholic Prince-Bishop could no longer stay there. He therefore moved to **Porrentruy**, in German Pruntrut. The large **castle** where the Prince-Bishops lived still stands there today. Porrentruy thus became the capital of the Prince-Bishopric.

abschnitte.titel: The end and the canton of Jura
abschnitte.text: The **French Revolution** brought the Prince-Bishopric to an end from **1792**. The area went to France for a few years. At the **Congress of Vienna in 1815**, most of it was given to the **canton of Bern**. Many people in the Jura later wished for a canton of their own. Since **1979** there has been the **canton of Jura**, the youngest canton in Switzerland.

gewusst: The castle of Porrentruy, the former residence of the Prince-Bishops, is now the seat of the cantonal administration.
The bishop's crozier in the coat of arms of the canton of Jura recalls the old Prince-Bishopric of Basel.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzell house is a typical farmhouse from the Appenzell region. It is built of wood and clad with small wooden shingles. Striking are the long rows of windows.
wichtigste: Appenzell houses are built of wood.
The walls are often clad with wooden shingles.
Typical are long rows of windows on the gable side.
The living part and the stable are usually built together.
Many houses used to have a weaving cellar.

abschnitte.text: The **Appenzell house** is a wooden house. Its outer walls are often covered with many small **wooden shingles**. The shingles protect the house from rain and wind. Some houses are painted in colour. The houses mostly stand scattered singly in the green hilly landscape.

Typical are the long **rows of windows** on the **gable side**. Many windows lie close together. In this way a lot of light came into the parlours. Light was important because in many houses people wove or embroidered. The living part and the **stable** are usually built together into one building.

In the past many families in the Appenzell region earned money by **home weaving**. For this many houses had a **weaving cellar** on the lower floor. There stood the loom. The damp cellar air was good for the threads, because they then broke less. Today many of these houses are protected.

gewusst: Village scenes with Appenzell houses, such as in Gais, are known all over Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Lake Ägeri is, besides Lake Zug, the second larger lake in the canton of Zug. It lies in the Ägerital, higher than Lake Zug, between green hills.
wichtigste: Lake Ägeri lies in the Ägerital in the canton of Zug.
It lies over 700 metres above sea level.
On its shore lie the municipalities of Oberägeri and Unterägeri.
From the lake the Lorze flows towards Lake Zug.
Nearby lies Morgarten, known from Swiss history.

abschnitte.text: Lake Ägeri lies in the **Ägerital**, above the town of Zug. It is at over 700 metres above sea level and so clearly higher than Lake Zug. At the northern end lies **Unterägeri**, on the eastern shore **Oberägeri**. Around the lake there are meadows, woods and gentle hills.
From Lake Ägeri flows the **Lorze**. It plunges through a deep gorge, the **Lorzentobel**, down to Baar. After that it flows into Lake Zug. So the two Zug lakes are joined by the same river.

At the southern end of the lake lies **Morgarten**. There in **1315** the Battle of Morgarten took place. At that time the men of Schwyz defeated a Habsburg army. The battle is regarded as an important event in the early history of the Confederation. A monument recalls it.

In summer you can **swim** in Lake Ägeri, row, sail or take the scheduled boat. A path leads round the lake and is popular with walkers and cyclists. The Ägerital is also known for its fresh air. In the past there were even spa hotels here for people seeking rest and recovery.

gewusst: The Lorze joins Lake Ägeri with Lake Zug.
At Morgarten the battlefield of 1315 lies right on the shore of Lake Ägeri.

teile.einleitung: The sweet chestnut is a big tree that grows in southern Switzerland. Its fruits, the chestnuts, were once so important in Ticino that the tree was called the “bread tree”.
wichtigste: The sweet chestnut grows above all in Ticino and the southern valleys of the Grisons.
Its fruits are called chestnuts or marroni.
In the past people in Ticino ate a great many chestnuts in winter.
That is why the tree was called the “bread tree”.
The chestnuts sit in a prickly husk.
Today hot marroni are very popular in autumn.

abschnitte.text: The **sweet chestnut** can grow very big and live for several hundred years. It likes a **mild climate** and so grows mainly south of the Alps. In Switzerland you find it in **Ticino**, in the **Bregaglia**, in the **Misox** and in a few warm places north of the Alps. Its leaves are long and toothed at the edge.

The **chestnuts** grow in a green, prickly husk that looks like a little hedgehog. In autumn the husks fall down and burst open. Inside there are usually two or three shiny brown fruits. Big chestnuts are often called **marroni**.

In the past the people in the Ticino valleys were often poor. Grain grew badly in the steep valleys, but chestnuts grew well. So in winter families ate a great many **chestnuts**, fresh, boiled, dried or as **flour**. Because the tree was as important as bread, it was called the **bread tree**.

The chestnut woods in which the trees were looked after are called **selve**. For drying, the chestnuts went into little huts that are called **grà** in Ticino. There a fire burned, and its smoke slowly dried the fruits. Dried chestnuts could be kept for a long time.

Today chestnuts are eaten mainly in autumn and winter. In many Swiss cities **marroni stalls** sell hot, roasted marroni in paper bags. In Ticino there are **chestnut festivals**. **Vermicelles**, a sweet chestnut purée, is also a popular dessert.

gewusst: Sweet chestnuts, which you can eat, are not related to horse chestnuts, whose fruits are not edible for people.
Some sweet chestnuts in Ticino are several hundred years old.

teile.einleitung: Flumserberg is a popular skiing and walking area in the canton of St Gallen. It lies high above Lake Walen and offers wide views of the Churfirsten.
wichtigste: Flumserberg lies in the canton of St Gallen.
It belongs to the municipality of Flums.
The area lies on the south side, high above Lake Walen.
Opposite you can see the mountain chain of the Churfirsten.
In winter you can ski, in summer you can walk.
Because it is not far from Zurich, it is a popular place for days out.

abschnitte.text: Flumserberg lies in the municipality of **Flums** in the canton of **St Gallen**. The mountain villages and ski runs are on the south side of **Lake Walen**, on a sunny terrace. On the other side of the lake rise the steep peaks of the **Churfirsten**. The highest points of the area are over 2,000 metres above sea level.

In winter, Flumserberg is a big **ski area** with many runs for beginners and experienced skiers. Mountain railways take visitors up, and a gondola lift, for example, goes up from Unterterzen on Lake Walen. Besides skiing and snowboarding, you can also go tobogganing or on winter walks. Because the area is only about an hour from Zurich, many day visitors come.

In summer, Flumserberg becomes a **walking area**. There are paths to small mountain lakes and viewpoints. Families can discover a lot on playgrounds and adventure trails. A **toboggan run** adds variety. From the top there is a lovely view over the deep blue Lake Walen.

gewusst: The Churfirsten, which you can see from Flumserberg, are a chain of seven peaks.
Lake Walen is over 140 metres deep in some places.

teile.einleitung: In Roman times Aventicum was the capital of the Helvetii. Today the small town of Avenches in the canton of Vaud lies there, and many ruins recall the once great Roman city.
wichtigste: Aventicum was the capital of the Helvetii in Roman times.
The city lay where Avenches in the canton of Vaud is today.
Avenches lies near Lake Murten.
A long city wall surrounded the city.
The amphitheatre is still well preserved today.
In the Roman Museum you can see finds from the old city.

abschnitte.text: The **Helvetii** were a Celtic people who lived in the area of present day Switzerland. After the Romans had conquered the land, **Aventicum** became their most important place. Under Emperor Vespasian the city received in the 1st century AD the rank of a Roman **colony**. That made it one of the most important cities north of the Alps.

Aventicum was surrounded by a **city wall** several kilometres long. In the city there were temples, baths, a theatre and an **amphitheatre**. There people watched contests and performances. Of a great temple a single tall column still stands today, which is called the “Cigognier”.

Archaeologists have dug up many things from Roman times in Avenches: coins, tools, mosaics and statues. The most famous find is a **golden bust** of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, discovered in 1939. The **Roman Museum** stands right beside the amphitheatre. It shows how people lived then.

Today **Avenches** is a small town in the canton of Vaud. The old amphitheatre is still used: in summer concerts and opera performances take place there. So the spectators sit today on the same tiers as almost 2,000 years ago.

gewusst: The golden bust of Marcus Aurelius from Avenches is a national treasure of Switzerland.
Only a small part of the huge city of Aventicum has been built over, so something new keeps turning up in the ground.

teile.einleitung: Carl Spitteler was a Swiss poet and writer. He was born in Liestal in 1845 and in 1919 became the first Swiss to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.
wichtigste: Carl Spitteler was born in 1845 in Liestal in the canton of Basel Landschaft.
He was a poet and writer.
In 1919 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature.
He was the first Swiss to win this prize.
His best known work is the long poem “Olympischer Frühling” (Olympian Spring).
In the First World War he called on the Swiss to stand together.
He died in Lucerne in 1924.

abschnitte.text: Carl Spitteler was born in **1845** in **Liestal**, the main town of the canton of **Basel Landschaft**. He studied law first and then **theology**. After that he worked for a few years as a private tutor in Russia. Back in Switzerland he was a teacher and journalist. Later he lived in **Lucerne**, where he died in **1924**.

Spitteler wrote **poems**, **stories** and **novels**. His best known work is the **“Olympischer Frühling”** (Olympian Spring), a very long epic in verse. An **epic** is a long story in verse form. In it Spitteler tells of gods whom he invented after models from Greek mythology. His story “Die Mädchenfeinde” (The Girl Haters) is also well known, in which he tells of children.

The **Nobel Prize in Literature** is one of the most important prizes for writers worldwide. Spitteler received it for the year **1919**, above all for the “Olympischer Frühling”. He was thus the **first Swiss** to receive this prize. That made him famous all over Switzerland.

During the **First World War** the people in Switzerland were divided. Many German speaking Swiss sided with Germany, many French speaking Swiss with France. In **1914** Spitteler gave the speech **“Our Swiss Standpoint”** in Zurich. In it he called on all parts of the country to stand together and on Switzerland to remain **neutral**. This speech is still often mentioned today.

gewusst: Carl Spitteler published his first works under the name Carl Felix Tandem.
To this day only a few writers born in Switzerland have received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzell Biber is a gingerbread with an almond filling. It is a well known speciality from Appenzell and is often decorated with a picture.
wichtigste: The Biber is a baked speciality from Appenzell.
It is a gingerbread with honey and spices.
In the middle is a filling of almonds.
Often a picture is pressed into the dough.
The pictures are made with carved wooden moulds.
Small Biber are called Biberli.

abschnitte.text: A **Biber** consists of a dark **gingerbread dough** with honey and spices such as cinnamon, cloves and aniseed. In the middle lies a sweet **almond filling**. The dough is laid around the filling and then baked. In the process the Biber gets a shiny brown surface.

Many Biber are decorated with a **picture**. For this the dough is pressed into a carved wooden mould, a **Model**. The pictures often show herdsmen, cows, the ascent to the alp or coats of arms. Some moulds are very old and artistically carved. There are Biber in many sizes; small ones are called **Biberli**.

Biber have been baked in Appenzell for a long time. In the past they were a special gift, for example at New Year or on festival days. Today you can buy them all year round. They are a popular **souvenir** from eastern Switzerland.

gewusst: Biber also exist in other parts of eastern Switzerland, for example in St Gallen.
Large Biber with pictures are sometimes almost too beautiful to eat.

teile.einleitung: Henry Dunant was a businessman from Geneva and the founder of the Red Cross. For his work for wounded soldiers he received the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. He spent the last years of his life in Heiden in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
wichtigste: Henry Dunant was born in Geneva in 1828.
In 1859 he saw the aftermath of the Battle of Solferino in Italy.
He wrote the book “A Memory of Solferino”.
In 1863 the committee that became the Red Cross was founded in Geneva.
In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.
He lived in Heiden from 1887 and died there in 1910.

abschnitte.text: **Henry Dunant** was born in **Geneva** in **1828**. His family was devout and helped poor people. Dunant became a businessman and had plans for a company in North Africa. To get help for his business, he travelled to Italy in 1859, where the French emperor was with his army.

Near the town of **Solferino** in Italy, a great **battle** had just taken place. Thousands of wounded soldiers lay without help on the battlefield. Dunant organised the care of the wounded with women from the nearby village, no matter which country they came from. Afterwards he wrote the book “**A Memory of Solferino**”. In it he called for relief societies that would care for the wounded neutrally in every war.

In **1863**, Dunant and four other people from Geneva founded a committee that became the **International Committee of the Red Cross**. As early as 1864, several states signed the first **Geneva Convention**. It lays down that the wounded and their helpers must be protected in war. The emblem is a red cross on a white background, the reversed colours of the Swiss flag.

Dunant's business failed, and he lost all his money. He had to leave Geneva and lived in poverty for a long time. From **1887** he lived in **Heiden**, and later lived in the hospital there.
