A journalist drew the world's attention to him again. In **1901** he received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**. He died in Heiden in **1910**, where a museum now recalls his life.

gewusst: Dunant shared the first Nobel Peace Prize with the Frenchman Frédéric Passy.
His birthday, 8 May, is now World Red Cross Day.

teile.einleitung: Emmental is a famous Swiss cheese from the Emmental region in the canton of Bern. It is known all over the world for its big, round holes.
wichtigste: Emmental cheese comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern.
It is known for its big, round holes.
The holes are made by a gas that bacteria produce in the cheese.
One wheel is very large and can weigh about 100 kilograms.
Emmental is made from cow's milk.
The name is protected as a PDO (AOP).

abschnitte.text: **Emmental cheese** gets its name from the **Emmental**, a hilly landscape in the canton of **Bern**. It is made from **cow's milk** in **cheese dairies**. The wheels are very large and round and can weigh about 100 kilograms. This makes it one of the biggest cheeses in the world.

Tiny **bacteria** live in the cheese. While the cheese ripens, they produce a **gas** called **carbon dioxide**. Because the cheese is firm, the gas cannot escape and forms round bubbles. This is how the typical **holes** come about, which are also called **eyes**.

The milk is warmed and thickened with **rennet**. Then the mass is cut into small grains, heated and pressed into a mould. After that, the cheese sits in a **salt bath**. Then it **ripens** for several months in cellars, and the longer it ripens, the stronger its taste becomes.

Genuine Swiss Emmental carries the label **AOP** (protected designation of origin). This means it has to be made according to fixed rules in a certain area. In other countries there are many cheeses that look similar. In English, such cheeses are often simply called “Swiss cheese”.

gewusst: In 2015, researchers in Switzerland found that tiny bits of hay in the milk help the holes to form.
At the show dairy in Affoltern in the Emmental, you can watch how Emmental cheese is made.

teile.einleitung: Alberto Giacometti was one of the most famous sculptors of the 20th century. He came from the Bregaglia in the Grisons. His very thin, long bronze figures are known all over the world.
wichtigste: Alberto Giacometti was born in 1901 in the Bregaglia.
His father Giovanni Giacometti was a well known painter.
Alberto lived and worked in Paris for a long time.
His slender, long bronze figures are famous.
He was shown on the former 100 franc note.
He died in 1966 in Chur.

abschnitte.text: Alberto Giacometti was born in **1901** in the **Bregaglia**, a valley in the south of the **Grisons**. Italian is spoken there. His father **Giovanni Giacometti** was a painter and encouraged the art of his children. Even as a teenager Alberto drew and modelled a great deal. His brother Diego also became an artist.

In the 1920s Giacometti moved to **Paris**. There for decades he worked in a small, cramped studio. He knew many other artists and writers. He also painted, but he became famous as a **sculptor**. He returned to the Bregaglia again and again.

Typical of Giacometti are very **thin, long figures** of **bronze**. They stand or walk and often seem lonely. A well known work is the **“Walking Man”**. This figure could be seen on the former Swiss **100 franc note**. Giacometti died in **1966** in **Chur**. His works now stand in great museums all over the world.

gewusst: Works by Giacometti are among the most expensive sculptures ever sold.

teile.einleitung: The Forum of Swiss History is a museum in the main town of Schwyz. It shows how people in Switzerland lived in the past, and it belongs to the Swiss National Museum.
wichtigste: The Forum of Swiss History is in Schwyz, the main town of the canton.
It belongs to the Swiss National Museum.
The National Museum also includes the Landesmuseum in Zurich and the Château de Prangins.
The museum shows the history and everyday life of earlier times.
It opened in 1995.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss National Museum** has three museums in different parts of the country. The biggest is the **Landesmuseum Zurich**. In French-speaking Switzerland, the **Château de Prangins** on Lake Geneva belongs to it. In central Switzerland there is the **Forum of Swiss History Schwyz**. It opened in **1995**.

The museum tells the **history** of the area of present-day Switzerland. It shows how people used to live, work and live together. With objects, pictures and models, the past comes to life. There are also hands-on stations. In addition, **special exhibitions** on different topics are held from time to time.

abschnitte.titel: Schwyz, a place rich in history
abschnitte.text: The town of **Schwyz** is the main town of the canton of the same name. The name of the whole of Switzerland comes from the name Schwyz. Very close to the Forum is the **Museum of the Federal Charters**, where the Federal Charter of 1291 is kept. This means that in Schwyz you can visit two museums of Swiss history in a single day.

gewusst: Switzerland and the Swiss flag get their name from the canton of Schwyz.

teile.einleitung: Baden is a town on the Limmat in the canton of Aargau. Even the Romans bathed here in the hot springs, and the town has its name from that.
wichtigste: Baden lies on the Limmat in the canton of Aargau.
The town has been known for its hot springs since Roman times.
The Romans called the place Aquae Helveticae.
The water is the most mineral rich thermal water in Switzerland.
In 1847 the first railway in Switzerland ran from Zurich to Baden.
In Baden the firm Brown, Boveri and Cie was founded in 1891.

abschnitte.text: In Baden very warm **mineral water** bubbles out of the ground. It is about 47 degrees hot and contains many dissolved substances. The **Romans** already built baths here and called the place **Aquae Helveticae**, which means “Waters of the Helvetii”. To this day people bathe in the warm water of Baden.

The **old town** lies on a slope above the Limmat. An old **wooden bridge** leads over the river to the bailiff's castle. Above the town stands the ruin of **Stein** Castle. From the 15th to the 18th century the envoys of the Confederates often met in Baden for the **Federal Diet**.

In 1847 the **first railway** on Swiss soil ran between Zurich and Baden. It was called the **Spanisch-Brötli Railway**. The name comes from a pastry from Baden, the Spanischbrötli. Rich people in Zurich used to have these brought home fresh, and with the railway that went much faster.

In 1891 Charles Brown and Walter Boveri founded the firm **BBC** in Baden. It built generators, motors and turbines. The firm grew very large and made Baden an important **industrial town**. Today it belongs to the ABB group.

gewusst: The new thermal bath in Baden is called “Fortyseven”, after the temperature of the water.
The name Baden directly recalls bathing in the warm springs.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It is about 57 kilometres long and runs from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to Bodio in Ticino. Since it opened in 2016, trains travel through the Alps much faster.
wichtigste: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long.
It is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
The northern portal is at Erstfeld (UR), the southern portal at Bodio (TI).
The tunnel opened in 2016.
It consists of two separate tubes, each with one track.
It belongs to the New Rail Link through the Alps, NEAT for short.

abschnitte.text: A **base tunnel** does not run high up through a mountain, but right at the bottom, at the level of the valleys. This means the train hardly has to climb at all. The line is almost flat, which is called a **flat railway**. This lets trains go faster, and heavy freight trains need fewer locomotives.

The tunnel begins at **Erstfeld** in the canton of Uri and ends at **Bodio** in Ticino. It consists of two **tubes**, one for each direction of travel. The tubes are linked by cross passages, which serve as escape routes. In some places there are more than 2,000 metres of rock above the tunnel.

Work on the tunnel went on for many years. Huge **tunnel boring machines** cut their way through the hard rock. Thousands of workers were involved. In **2016** the tunnel was officially opened, and in December 2016 regular service with a timetable began.

The tunnel is part of the **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps. Swiss voters approved this project at the ballot box. The aim is to carry more goods through the Alps by rail rather than by lorry on the road. The NEAT also includes the Lötschberg Base Tunnel and the Ceneri Base Tunnel.

gewusst: With the base tunnel, the train journey from Zurich to Lugano takes much less time than it used to.
Inside the mountain it is so warm that the rock was over 40 degrees hot during construction.

teile.einleitung: Bad Ragaz is a well known spa town in the canton of St Gallen. Its warm thermal water comes from the nearby Tamina Gorge.
wichtigste: Bad Ragaz lies in the canton of St Gallen, in the Sarganserland.
The town is known for its warm thermal water.
The water comes from a spring in the Tamina Gorge.
The thermal water is about 36 degrees warm.
Bad Ragaz lies on the Rhine, near the border with the Grisons.
Many guests come for bathing and recovery.

abschnitte.text: In the wild **Tamina Gorge** above Bad Ragaz warm water bubbles out of the rock. It is about **36 degrees** warm, almost as warm as our body. The water was a long time on its way in the mountain and warmed up there. Such water is called **thermal water**.

The spring was discovered as early as the Middle Ages. In the past the sick had to climb down into the narrow, dark gorge to bathe. The monastery of **Pfäfers** looked after the bath. In the 19th century the water was led down in pipes to Bad Ragaz. Since then bathing has been much more comfortable.

Bad Ragaz became a famous **spa town**. A spa town is a place where people want to recover and get well. There are thermal baths, hotels, parks and a golf course. Guests from all over the world come here.

The **Tamina** is a mountain stream that has dug a deep, narrow gorge into the rock. You can walk to the Old Bath of Pfäfers and visit the gorge. The rock walls are so high and so close together that at the top you see only a narrow strip of sky.

gewusst: Bad Ragaz lies only a few kilometres from Liechtenstein.
The spring in the Tamina Gorge is among the most abundant thermal springs in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Erasmus of Rotterdam was one of the most famous scholars of his time. He lived in Basel for a long time, where many of his books were printed, and he is buried in Basel Minster.
wichtigste: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a humanist and scholar.
He was born around 1466 in Rotterdam, in what is now the Netherlands.
He lived and worked in Basel for a long time.
The Basel printer Johann Froben printed many of his books.
He died in Basel in 1536 and was buried in the Minster.
The Erasmus exchange programme for students is named after him.

abschnitte.text: **Erasmus of Rotterdam** lived about 500 years ago. He was a **humanist**. This is what we call scholars who studied the old writings of the **Greeks** and **Romans** and thought education was very important. Erasmus wrote in **Latin**, the language of scholars. He wrote letters to many clever people all over Europe.

At that time, Basel was an important city for **book printing**. The printer **Johann Froben** worked closely with Erasmus and printed many of his works. In 1516, the **New Testament** in Greek, edited by Erasmus, appeared in Basel. Because of this, his books were spread all over Europe.

A well-known book by Erasmus is called **“In Praise of Folly”**. In it, he makes witty fun of people's mistakes, including problems in the Church. Erasmus wanted to improve the Church, but he remained **Catholic**. He argued for **peace** and sensible discussion.

When Basel became **Reformed**, Erasmus moved to Freiburg im Breisgau for a few years. Later he returned to Basel. He died in **1536** in Basel and was buried in **Basel Minster**. A tombstone there still reminds visitors of him today.

gewusst: The painter Hans Holbein the Younger painted several portraits of Erasmus in Basel.
The European exchange programme Erasmus, which lets students go abroad, bears his name.

teile.einleitung: After the city of Lucerne, Emmen is the largest municipality in the canton of Lucerne. It lies right next to the city and is known for industry and a military airfield.
wichtigste: Emmen is the second largest municipality in the canton of Lucerne.
The municipality lies right next to the city of Lucerne.
It has over 30,000 inhabitants.
The district of Emmenbrücke belongs to Emmen.
At Emmenbrücke, the Kleine Emme flows into the Reuss.
There is an airfield of the Swiss Air Force in Emmen.

abschnitte.text: **Emmen** lies in the north, right next to the **city of Lucerne**. With over 30,000 inhabitants, it is the **second largest municipality** in the canton. Although Emmen is as big as a town, it officially calls itself a municipality. Well-known districts are **Emmenbrücke** and **Emmen Dorf**.

At **Emmenbrücke**, the **Kleine Emme** flows into the **Reuss**. The Reuss comes out of Lake Lucerne in the city of Lucerne. The **Seetalplatz**, an important traffic junction, lies where the rivers meet. Flood protection there has been improved in recent years.

Emmen has been a place of **industry** for over a hundred years. Large factories were built here, for example for **steel** and for artificial fibres. Many people therefore came to Emmen to work, also from other countries. That is why people of very different backgrounds live in Emmen.

In Emmen there is a **military airfield** of the Swiss **Air Force**. Fighter jets take off and land here. Next to the airfield there are also companies that service and build aircraft. For the people living nearby, the noise of the planes is part of everyday life.

gewusst: Emmen has more inhabitants than some cantonal capitals, but it is officially a municipality.
At Emmenbrücke, the Kleine Emme and the Reuss join together.

teile.einleitung: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich. According to legend, they were brother and sister who were killed in Roman times because of their Christian faith.
wichtigste: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich.
According to legend, they were brother and sister.
They are said to have died on the spot where the Wasserkirche stands today.
Together with Exuperantius, they are shown on the seal of the city of Zurich.
Their feast day is 11 September.
The Grossmünster, the Fraumünster and the Wasserkirche are closely linked with them.

abschnitte.text: The story of Felix and Regula is a **legend**, an old tale that is not firmly proven. According to it, the two siblings belonged to the **Theban Legion**, a group of Christian soldiers in the Roman army. They fled across the Alps and got as far as Zurich. There they are said to have refused to worship the Roman gods. That is why they were killed.

The place where they are said to have died lies on the Limmat. The **Wasserkirche** (“Water Church”) stands there today. The legend goes on to say that the saints then walked a little way up the hill. The **Grossmünster** now stands on the spot where they were buried. The **Fraumünster** on the other side of the river was also dedicated to them.

Felix and Regula can be seen together with their servant **Exuperantius** on the old **seal of the city of Zurich**. In the past, a seal was like an official signature of the city. The three are shown there holding their heads in their hands. This is how the saints can also be recognised in many old pictures.

In the Middle Ages, many people made pilgrimages to the graves of Felix and Regula. With the **Reformation** under Huldrych Zwingli from 1519, the worship of saints ended in Zurich. Even so, Felix and Regula remained a symbol of the city. Their feast day is **11 September**.

gewusst: On the old Zurich seal, the patron saints are shown holding their own heads in their hands.
Not only Zurich, but other places too keep relics of Felix and Regula.

teile.einleitung: Braunwald is a small village in the canton of Glarus that lies on a sunny mountain terrace high above the Linth Valley. The special thing: no ordinary cars drive in the village, and you get up there by funicular.
wichtigste: Braunwald lies in the canton of Glarus and belongs to the municipality of Glarus Süd.
The village lies on a sun terrace above the place Linthal.
Braunwald is car free.
From Linthal the Braunwald Railway, a funicular, goes up to the village.
In summer you can hike, in winter ski and sledge.

abschnitte.text: Braunwald lies at about 1,250 metres above sea level on a mountain slope in the rear **Glarus region**. Down in the valley lies the village of **Linthal**. Because Braunwald lies on a kind of balcony on the mountain, the sun often shines there. Such a position is called a **sun terrace**. All around stand high mountains of the Glarus Alps.

There is no road for ordinary traffic as far as the village. So you go up by the **Braunwald Railway**. It is a **funicular**: a car runs up the steep slope on rails and is pulled by a strong cable. The valley station lies in Linthal, not far from the railway station. In a few minutes you are at the top.

Braunwald is a **car free village**. That means that guests and residents leave their cars down in the valley. In the village you get about on foot or with small electric vehicles that carry luggage and goods, for example. As a result it is quiet there and the air is clean. Similar car free places in Switzerland are, for example, Zermatt, Saas-Fee or Wengen.

Braunwald is a popular **holiday resort**, especially for families. In summer many hiking trails lead over alpine pastures and to mountain lakes. For children there is an adventure trail with stories about a dwarf. In winter you can ski, sledge and go on winter walks. Mountain railways take the guests even higher.

gewusst: Because no cars run, in Braunwald many goods are brought through the village with small electric carts.
The Braunwald Railway has been running up from Linthal to the village for over 100 years.

teile.einleitung: Cailler is one of the oldest chocolate brands in Switzerland. The factory stands in Broc in the canton of Fribourg, and there in the Maison Cailler you can experience how chocolate is made.
wichtigste: Cailler makes chocolate.
The brand was founded in 1819.
It is the oldest chocolate brand in Switzerland that still exists.
The factory stands in Broc in the canton of Fribourg, in the Gruyère region.
Today Cailler belongs to the Nestlé group.
In the Maison Cailler you can visit the factory and taste chocolate.

abschnitte.text: The Cailler brand goes back to **François-Louis Cailler**. In **1819** he founded a chocolate factory near **Vevey**. That makes Cailler the **oldest chocolate brand** in Switzerland that still exists today. At that time chocolate was still something special that not everyone could afford.

At the end of the 19th century a new factory was built in **Broc** in the canton of **Fribourg**. Broc lies in the **Gruyère region**, an area with many cows and good milk. The fresh **milk** from the region was very important for milk chocolate. The factory still produces chocolate today. Since 1929 Cailler has belonged to the food group **Nestlé**.

An important invention is connected with the Cailler family. **Daniel Peter**, the son in law of François-Louis Cailler, developed one of the first **milk chocolates** in the 1870s. Before that there was only dark chocolate. Milk chocolate soon became popular all over the world. Switzerland thereby became a famous **land of chocolate**.

In Broc there is the **Maison Cailler**, a visitor centre next to the factory. There you learn where the **cocoa beans** come from and how chocolate is made from them. You can smell the ingredients and see how pralines are made. At the end you may taste different kinds. The Maison Cailler is one of the most popular destinations for outings in the canton of Fribourg.

gewusst: Cailler has existed for over 200 years.
Milk chocolate was invented in Switzerland, in the circle of the Cailler family.

teile.einleitung: Zurich Airport is the largest airport in Switzerland. It lies north of the city of Zurich near Kloten and connects Switzerland with destinations all over the world.
wichtigste: Zurich Airport is the largest airport in Switzerland.
It lies mostly within the municipality of Kloten.
It opened in 1948.
It has three runways for take-offs and landings.
There is a large railway station underneath the airport.
The airline Swiss has its most important base here.

abschnitte.text: **Zurich Airport** lies about ten kilometres north of the city of Zurich, near **Kloten**. It is the largest and most important airport in Switzerland. Planes fly from here to many countries in Europe and to other continents. For the airline **Swiss**, Zurich is the hub, the place where many flights begin and end.

In the past, planes serving Zurich took off from **Dübendorf**. Because this airfield became too small, a new site was built near Kloten. The new airport opened in **1948**. Since then it has been extended again and again, with new runways, terminals and docks.

The airport has **three runways**. So that people living nearby can sleep at night, there is a **night curfew** during which almost no planes may take off or land. Even so, aircraft noise keeps coming up as a topic in politics. Many municipalities around the airport are affected by it.

Underneath the airport there is a large **railway station**. Trains run from there directly to Zurich and to many other cities in Switzerland. There are also tram lines and buses. Right next to the airport, **The Circle** has stood since 2020, a large building complex with offices, hotels and shops.

gewusst: In 2019, more than 30 million passengers used Zurich Airport.
From a viewing terrace you can watch planes taking off and landing.

teile.einleitung: The Hackbrett, or hammered dulcimer, is a musical instrument with many strings that you strike with two small hammers. In Switzerland it belongs mainly to Appenzell folk music. Its bright, sparkling sound is typical of Appenzell string music.
wichtigste: The Hackbrett is a stringed instrument.
You strike the strings with two small hammers.
It belongs to typical Appenzell string music.
Violins, a cello and a double bass usually play along with it.
In the Valais there is also a Hackbrett tradition of its own.
Similar instruments exist in many countries of the world.

abschnitte.text: The Hackbrett is a flat wooden box, usually in the shape of a **trapezium**. Many **strings** are stretched across it. The musician holds a small **hammer** or beater in each hand and strikes the strings with them. Depending on the string, a high or a low note is made. Because you strike the strings, the Hackbrett is both a percussion instrument and a stringed instrument.

In **Appenzell**, folk music is often played in a **string band**. Typically it has two violins, a Hackbrett, a **cello** and a **double bass**. The violins play the melody, and the cello and bass provide the rhythm and the low notes. The Hackbrett adds ornamented runs and gives the music its special sound. You hear this music at festivals and in inns.

The Hackbrett is not only known in Appenzell. In the **Valais** too there is a Hackbrett tradition of its own, with instruments built a little differently. In folk music, melodies are often passed down from generation to generation. Today many children learn the Hackbrett at music schools.

Instruments like the Hackbrett exist in many countries. In Hungary and Romania, a large relative is called the **cimbalom**. In Iran people play the **santur**. China too has a similar instrument. What they all have in common is that strings stretched across a box are struck with little hammers.

gewusst: A Hackbrett has a great many strings, because for each note several strings are often stretched side by side.
A Hackbrett has to be tuned regularly, and because of the many strings this takes a long time.

teile.einleitung: The Saurer company of Arbon in the canton of Thurgau was once world famous. It built embroidery machines, lorries and Swiss Post buses. To this day a museum in Arbon recalls that time.
wichtigste: Saurer was an industrial firm in Arbon on Lake Constance.
The firm built embroidery machines and weaving machines.
Saurer lorries and Swiss Post buses also became well known.
The firm is named after the Saurer family of entrepreneurs.
In the Saurer Museum in Arbon you can see old vehicles and machines.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century the **Saurer** family founded a foundry and moved to **Arbon** on Lake Constance. Under **Adolph Saurer** the firm grew strongly. Eastern Switzerland was then a centre of **embroidery**. Saurer built **embroidery machines** for it, which were sold to many countries. Later weaving machines were added.

At the start of the 20th century Saurer began to build **engines** and **lorries**. The vehicles were regarded as sturdy and reliable. The Swiss army and the Post also used them. Many of the yellow **Swiss Post buses** that drove over the Alpine passes came from Saurer. At the start of the 1980s the building of Saurer lorries ended.

In Arbon today there is the **Saurer Museum**. There stand old **lorries**, Swiss Post buses and huge **embroidery machines**. Some machines are still demonstrated so that you can see how they worked. The museum shows how important industry once was for Arbon and the whole of **Thurgau**. Many people from the region used to work at Saurer.

gewusst: Saurer lorries were driven not only in Switzerland but exported to many countries.
A Saurer Swiss Post bus with its typical horn long belonged to the picture of Swiss mountain roads.

teile.einleitung: At 4,634 metres the Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland. It lies in the Monte Rosa massif in the canton of the Valais, near the border with Italy.
wichtigste: The Dufourspitze is 4,634 metres high.
It is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
It belongs to the Monte Rosa massif in the Valais on the border with Italy.
It is named after General Henri Dufour.
It was first climbed in 1855.
In the Alps only Mont Blanc is higher.

abschnitte.text: At **4,634 metres** the **Dufourspitze** is the highest mountain in Switzerland. It is the highest peak of the **Monte Rosa massif**. This big mountain massif lies in the canton of the **Valais** on the border with **Italy**. In the whole of the Alps only **Mont Blanc** is higher.

The mountain is named after **Guillaume Henri Dufour**. He was an engineer and general from Geneva. Under his direction the first accurate map of Switzerland came into being, the **Dufour Map**. He also helped to found the **Red Cross**. In his honour the peak received its name in 1863.

In **1855** a roped party reached the summit for the first time. It included English mountaineers and mountain guides from Switzerland. Today experienced alpinists usually set off from the **Monte Rosa Hut**. The climb is long and leads over glaciers and rock.

Around Monte Rosa lie big **glaciers**, for example the **Gorner Glacier**. It is among the biggest glaciers in the Alps. From the **Gornergrat** above **Zermatt** you see the Dufourspitze and the glaciers very well. Like all Alpine glaciers, it too is getting smaller because of warming.

gewusst: Before it was named after Dufour, the Dufourspitze was simply called the “Highest Peak”.
Henri Dufour led the work on the first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel in the canton of Ticino. It is around 15 kilometres long and since the end of 2020 has connected the Bellinzona region much faster with Lugano.
wichtigste: The Ceneri Base Tunnel lies in the canton of Ticino.
It is around 15 kilometres long.
It was opened in 2020.
It runs under Monte Ceneri.
It connects the Bellinzona region with Lugano.
It is part of the New Rail Link through the Alps (NEAT).
The tunnel consists of two tubes with one track each.

abschnitte.text: Between **Bellinzona** and **Lugano** lies a range of hills with **Monte Ceneri**. In the past the trains had to run on a winding line up over the Ceneri and down again. The new **Ceneri Base Tunnel** now runs deep down through the mountain. It is around **15 kilometres** long and almost flat. It begins at Camorino near Bellinzona and ends at Vezia north of Lugano.

The tunnel was opened **in 2020**. Since then the trains between Bellinzona, Lugano and Locarno have been much quicker. The journey from **Locarno** to **Lugano**, for example, takes much less time than before. **Commuters** and **schoolchildren** in Ticino benefit above all. Freight trains can also run through the tunnel.

The Ceneri Base Tunnel belongs to the **New Rail Link through the Alps**, or **NEAT** for short. The **Gotthard Base Tunnel** and the **Lötschberg Base Tunnel** belong to it too. The aim of the NEAT is that more goods are carried through the Alps by **rail** instead of by lorry. That protects the environment in the Alpine valleys. With the Ceneri Base Tunnel the NEAT through the Gotthard was completed.

The tunnel consists of **two tubes** that run side by side. In each tube there is one **track**, one for each direction of travel. Between the tubes there are **cross passages** at regular intervals. Through them you can get into the other tube in an emergency. That makes the tunnel safer.

gewusst: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is the third big base tunnel of the NEAT after the Lötschberg and the Gotthard.
A base tunnel lies deep down at the foot of a mountain, so it is almost flat.

teile.einleitung: On 2 September 1806 an enormous mass of rock and earth crashed down into the valley on the Rossberg in the canton of Schwyz. It buried the village of Goldau. It is one of the best known landslides in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Goldau landslide happened on 2 September 1806.
The masses of rock and earth broke away on the Rossberg.
The village of Goldau in the canton of Schwyz was buried.
Over 450 people lost their lives.
Part of Lake Lauerz was also filled in.
Today the Goldau Nature and Animal Park lies on the field of debris.

abschnitte.text: In summer 1806 it had rained long and hard. On the afternoon of **2 September** a huge mass of rock and earth broke away on the **Rossberg**. In a few minutes it slid into the valley and buried the village of **Goldau** and further hamlets. Over **450 people** lost their lives. Many houses, stables and fields disappeared under the rubble.

The Rossberg consists of sloping layers. One layer is **Nagelfluh**, a rock made of many stones baked together. Beneath it lie softer layers of **marl**. When the rainwater seeped into the mountain, these layers became slippery. The heavy rock slabs above then slid off as if on a slide.

Part of the masses crashed into **Lake Lauerz**. This created a great flood wave, which also did damage on the other shore. The lake became smaller, because rubble filled in part of it. After the disaster people from all over Switzerland helped the survivors.

The village of Goldau was later rebuilt. On the huge **field of debris** with the big boulders there lies today the **Goldau Nature and Animal Park**. Animals such as deer, wolves and bears live there. On the Rossberg you can still see the pale scar where the mountain broke away.

gewusst: The Goldau landslide was one of the first to be examined exactly by scientists.
Some of the boulders in the Goldau animal park are as big as a house.
